title_en: Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution of the People's Republic of China for the purposes of protecting the lawful rights and interests of civil subjects, regulating civil relations, maintaining social and economic order, meeting the requirements of the development of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and promoting the core socialist values.
Article 2 The civil law regulates personal and property relations among natural persons, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations that are equal in status.
Article 3 The personal rights, property rights, and other lawful rights and interests of civil subjects are protected by law, and no organization or individual shall infringe upon them.
Article 4 All civil subjects have equal legal status in civil activities.
Article 5 In conducting civil activities, civil subjects shall follow the principle of voluntariness, and establish, modify, or terminate civil legal relations based on their true intentions.
Article 6 In conducting civil activities, civil subjects shall follow the principle of fairness, and reasonably determine the rights and obligations of each party.
Article 7 In conducting civil activities, civil subjects shall follow the principle of good faith, act honestly, and abide by their commitments.
Article 8 In conducting civil activities, civil subjects shall not violate the law or contravene public order and good customs.
Article 9 In conducting civil activities, civil subjects shall act in a manner that conserves resources and protects the ecological environment.

Article 10 Civil disputes shall be resolved in accordance with the law. Where the law does not provide for a matter, custom may be applied, except that the custom shall not contravene public order and good customs.
Article 11 Where other laws make special provisions on civil relations, those provisions shall be followed.

Article 12 The laws of the People's Republic of China shall apply to civil activities within the territory of the People's Republic of China. Where the law provides otherwise, those provisions shall be followed.
Article 13 A natural person has civil capacity for rights from the time of birth until death, and may enjoy civil rights and assume civil obligations in accordance with law.
Article 14 All natural persons have equal civil capacity for rights.

Article 15 The time of birth and the time of death of a natural person shall be determined based on the time recorded on the birth certificate or the death certificate, respectively. In the absence of a birth certificate or a death certificate, the time recorded on the household registration or other valid identification registration shall prevail. Where there is other evidence sufficient to overturn the time recorded as above, the time certified by such evidence shall prevail.

Article 16 In matters involving the protection of the interests of a fetus, such as inheritance of an estate or acceptance of a gift, the fetus shall be deemed to have civil capacity for rights. However, if the fetus is stillborn at delivery, its civil capacity for rights shall be deemed never to have existed.
Article 17 A natural person aged 18 or over is an adult. A natural person under the age of 18 is a minor.

Article 18 An adult is a person with full civil capacity for conduct, and may independently perform civil juristic acts. A minor aged 16 or over whose primary source of income is his or her own labor shall be deemed a person with full civil capacity for conduct.

Article 19 A minor aged 8 or over is a person with limited civil capacity for conduct, and shall have his or her civil juristic acts performed by his or her legal representative or with the consent or ratification of his or her legal representative. However, such a minor may independently perform a civil juristic act that is purely for his or her benefit or that is appropriate to his or her age and intelligence.
Article 20 A minor under the age of 8 is a person with no civil capacity for conduct, and shall have his or her civil juristic acts performed by his or her legal representative.

Article 21 An adult who is unable to recognize his or her own conduct shall be a person having no capacity for civil conduct, and his or her legal representative shall act on his or her behalf to perform civil juristic acts. Where a minor aged eight or above is unable to recognize his or her own conduct, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply.

Article 22 An adult who is unable to fully recognize his or her own conduct shall be a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, and may perform civil juristic acts through his or her legal representative or with the consent or ratification of his or her legal representative; provided that he or she may independently perform civil juristic acts that are purely for his or her benefit or that are appropriate to his or her intellectual or mental health condition.
Article 23 The guardian of a person having no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct shall be his or her legal representative.

Article 24 For an adult who is unable to recognize or is unable to fully recognize his or her own conduct, an interested person or a relevant organization may apply to the People's Court for a determination that the adult is a person having no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct. Where a person has been determined by the People's Court as a person having no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, upon the application of the person himself or herself, an interested person or a relevant organization, the People's Court may, based on the recovery of his or her intellectual or mental health condition, determine that such adult has been restored to the status of a person with limited capacity for civil conduct or a person with full capacity for civil conduct. The relevant organizations referred to in this Article shall include: residents committees, villagers committees, schools, medical institutions, the Women's Federation, the Disabled Persons' Federation, organizations for the elderly lawfully established, the civil affairs department, and the like.

Article 25 A natural person shall take the domicile recorded in the household registration or other valid identity registration as his or her residence; where the habitual residence is inconsistent with the residence, the habitual residence shall be deemed as the residence.
Article 26 Parents shall have the obligation to raise, educate and protect their minor children. Adult children shall have the obligation to support, assist and protect their parents.

Article 27 The parents of a minor child shall be the guardians of the minor child. Where the parents of a minor are deceased or have no ability to be guardians, the following persons who have the ability to be guardians shall act as guardians in the following order: (1) paternal grandparents and maternal grandparents; (2) elder brothers and sisters; and (3) other individuals or organizations that are willing to act as guardians, provided that the consent of the residents committee, villagers committee or the civil affairs department of the place of the minor's residence is obtained.

Article 28 For an adult with no capacity for civil conduct or with limited capacity for civil conduct, the following persons who have the ability to be guardians shall act as guardians in the following order: (1) spouse; (2) parents and children; (3) other close relatives; and (4) other individuals or organizations that are willing to act as guardians, provided that the consent of the residents committee, villagers committee or the civil affairs department of the place of the ward's residence is obtained.
Article 29 Where the parents of a ward act as guardians, they may appoint a guardian by will.
Article 30 Persons who are legally qualified to be guardians may reach an agreement to determine a guardian. The determination of a guardian by agreement shall respect the true will of the ward.

Article 31 Where there is a dispute over the determination of a guardian, the residents committee, villagers committee or the civil affairs department of the place of the ward's residence shall designate a guardian. Where any relevant party disagrees with the designation, it may apply to the People's Court for the designation of a guardian; the relevant party may also directly apply to the People's Court for the designation of a guardian. The residents committee, villagers committee, civil affairs department or the People's Court shall respect the true will of the ward, and designate a guardian from among those who are legally qualified to be guardians in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the ward. Where, before the designation of a guardian in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1 of this Article, the personal rights, property rights and other lawful rights and interests of a ward are left unprotected, the residents committee, villagers committee, the relevant organization prescribed by law or the civil affairs department of the place of the ward's residence shall act as the provisional guardian. Once a guardian is designated, it shall not be changed without authorization; any unauthorized change shall not relieve the designated guardian of its liability.

Article 32 Where there is no person legally qualified to be a guardian, the guardianship shall be assumed by the civil affairs department, or may be assumed by the residents committee or villagers committee of the place of the ward's residence that is qualified to perform guardianship duties.

Article 33 An adult with full capacity for civil conduct may, through prior consultation with his or her close relatives, or other individuals or organizations willing to act as guardians, determine his or her own guardian in writing, and when he or she loses or partially loses capacity for civil conduct, such guardian shall perform guardianship duties.

Article 34 The duties of a guardian shall be to act on behalf of the ward to perform civil juristic acts, and to protect the personal rights, property rights and other lawful rights and interests of the ward. Rights arising from the guardian's lawful performance of guardianship duties shall be protected by law. Where a guardian fails to perform guardianship duties or infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the ward, the guardian shall bear legal liability. Where, due to an emergency or the like, the guardian is temporarily unable to perform guardianship duties, leaving the ward's life unattended, the residents committee, villagers committee or the civil affairs department of the place of the ward's residence shall arrange necessary provisional living care measures for the ward.

Article 35 A guardian shall perform guardianship duties in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the ward. A guardian shall not dispose of the ward's property except for safeguarding the interests of the ward. When performing guardianship duties and making decisions concerning the interests of a minor ward, the guardian shall, based on the age and intellectual status of the ward, respect the true will of the ward. When performing guardianship duties, the guardian of an adult ward shall, to the maximum extent, respect the true will of the ward, ensure and assist the ward in performing civil juristic acts that are appropriate to the ward's intellectual or mental health condition. The guardian shall not interfere with matters that the ward is capable of handling independently.

Article 36 Where a guardian falls under any of the following circumstances, the People's Court shall, upon application by the relevant individual or organization, disqualify the guardian, arrange necessary provisional guardianship measures, and designate a guardian according to law in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the ward: (1) committing acts that seriously harm the physical or mental health of the ward; (2) being negligent in performing guardianship duties, or being unable to perform guardianship duties and refusing to delegate part or all of the guardianship duties to another person, thereby leaving the ward in a dangerous or distressed condition; or (3) committing other acts that seriously infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the ward. The relevant individuals and organizations referred to in this Article shall include: other persons legally qualified to be guardians, residents committees, villagers committees, schools, medical institutions, the Women's Federation, the Disabled Persons' Federation, organizations for the protection of minors, organizations for the elderly lawfully established, the civil affairs department, and the like. Where the individuals and organizations other than the civil affairs department specified in the preceding paragraph fail to apply to the People's Court in a timely manner for the disqualification of a guardian, the civil affairs department shall apply to the People's Court.

Article 37 Parents, children, spouses, and the like who are legally obligated to pay child support, alimony, or support for the ward shall continue to perform such obligations after being disqualified as a guardian by the People's Court.

Article 38 Where the parent or child of a ward, after being disqualified as a guardian by the People's Court, shows genuine repentance, except in cases where he or she has committed an intentional crime against the ward, upon his or her application, the People's Court may, on the premise of respecting the true will of the ward, restore his or her qualification as a guardian as the circumstances may require, and the guardianship relationship between the guardian designated by the People's Court and the ward shall be terminated simultaneously.

Article 39 The guardianship relationship shall terminate under any of the following circumstances: (1) the ward acquires or regains full capacity for civil conduct; (2) the guardian loses the ability to be a guardian; (3) the ward or the guardian dies; or (4) other circumstances under which the People's Court determines that the guardianship relationship terminates. Where the ward still needs guardianship after the termination of the guardianship relationship, another guardian shall be determined according to law.
Article 40 Where a natural person has been missing for two years, an interested person may apply to the People's Court for a declaration that the natural person is a missing person.

Article 41 The time during which a natural person is missing shall be calculated from the date when he or she loses contact. For a person who goes missing in a war, the missing period shall commence on the date the war ends or on the date determined by relevant authorities as the start of the missing status.

Article 42 The property of a missing person shall be administered by his or her spouse, adult children, parents, or any other person willing to act as the property custodian. If a dispute arises over the administration, no person as specified in the preceding paragraph exists, or the person specified therein lacks the capacity to administer, the custodian shall be designated by the People's Court.

Article 43 A property custodian shall properly manage the missing person's property and protect his or her property rights and interests. Taxes, debts, and other expenses payable by the missing person shall be paid by the property custodian from the missing person's property. If a property custodian causes damage to the missing person's property intentionally or through gross negligence, he or she shall bear compensation liability.

Article 44 If a property custodian fails to perform administrative duties, infringes upon the missing person's property rights and interests, or loses the capacity to administer, any interested party of the missing person may apply to the People's Court for replacing the property custodian. A property custodian having a legitimate reason may apply to the People's Court for replacement. If the People's Court replaces a property custodian, the new custodian shall have the right to request the former custodian to promptly transfer the relevant property and report on the status of the property administration.

Article 45 If a missing person reappears, the People's Court shall revoke the declaration of missing person upon application by the person or any interested party. Upon reappearance, the missing person shall have the right to request the property custodian to promptly transfer the relevant property and report on the status of the property administration.

Article 46 Any interested party may apply to the People's Court for declaring the death of a natural person under any of the following circumstances: (1) the person has been missing for four years; or (2) the person has been missing for two years due to an accident. If a natural person goes missing due to an accident and relevant authorities have proven that survival is impossible, the application for declaring death shall not be subject to the two-year restriction.

Article 47 If, with respect to the same natural person, some interested parties apply for declaring death while others apply for declaring missing, and the conditions for declaring death as provided for in this Law are met, the People's Court shall declare death.

Article 48 For a person declared dead, the date of the People's Court's adjudication declaring death shall be deemed as the date of his or her death. If the declaration is due to missing following an accident, the date of the accident shall be deemed as the date of death.

Article 49 If a natural person is declared dead but is not actually deceased, the validity of civil juristic acts performed by that natural person during the period of being declared dead shall not be affected.
Article 50 If a person declared dead reappears, the People's Court shall revoke the declaration of death upon application by the person or any interested party.

Article 51 The marital relationship of a person declared dead shall be dissolved from the date of the declaration of death. If the declaration of death is revoked, the marital relationship shall be automatically restored from the date of revocation, except where the spouse has remarried or has made a written declaration to the marriage registration authority indicating unwillingness to restore the relationship.

Article 52 If a child of a person declared dead was lawfully adopted by another person during the period of the declaration of death, after the revocation of the declaration of death, the person shall not assert the invalidity of the adoption on the ground that his or her consent was not obtained.

Article 53 A person whose declaration of death is revoked shall have the right to request any civil subject who acquired his or her property in accordance with Title VI of this Law to return the property; if return is impossible, appropriate compensation shall be made. If an interested party, by concealing the truth, causes another person to be declared dead and thereby acquires that person's property, the interested party shall, in addition to returning the property, bear compensation liability for the losses caused thereby.

Article 54 A natural person who engages in industrial or commercial operations and is registered according to law shall be deemed as an individual industrial or commercial household. An individual industrial or commercial household may adopt a trade name.

Article 55 Members of a rural collective economic organization who obtain the right to contract and manage rural land according to law and engage in household contract operations shall be deemed as a rural contractual household.

Article 56 The debts of an individual industrial or commercial household shall be borne with personal property if operated individually, or with household property if operated by the family; if the nature of the operation cannot be distinguished, the debts shall be borne with household property. The debts of a rural contractual household shall be borne with the property of the household engaging in rural land contract operations; if the business is actually operated by some members of the household, the debts shall be borne with the property of such members.

Article 57 A legal person is an organization that has the capacity for civil rights and the capacity for civil conduct, and independently enjoys civil rights and assumes civil obligations according to law.

Article 58 A legal person shall be established according to law. A legal person shall have its own name, organizational structure, domicile, and property or funds. The specific conditions and procedures for the establishment of a legal person shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations. If a legal person is established subject to approval by relevant authorities as provided for by laws or administrative regulations, such provisions shall be followed.
Article 59 The capacity for civil rights and the capacity for civil conduct of a legal person shall commence when the legal person is established and shall cease when the legal person is terminated.
Article 60 A legal person shall bear civil liability independently with all of its property.

Article 61 In accordance with the provisions of law or the articles of association of a legal person, the person in charge who represents the legal person in engaging in civil activities shall be the legal representative of the legal person. The legal consequences of civil activities conducted by the legal representative in the name of the legal person shall be borne by the legal person. Any restriction imposed by the articles of association of the legal person or its governing body on the representative authority of the legal representative shall not be asserted against a bona fide counterparty.

Article 62 Where the legal representative causes harm to another person in the performance of his or her duties, the legal person shall bear civil liability. After the legal person bears civil liability, it may, in accordance with the provisions of law or its articles of association, seek recourse against the legal representative who is at fault.

Article 63 A legal person shall take the place where its principal office is located as its domicile. Where registration of the legal person is required by law, the place where its principal office is located shall be registered as its domicile.
Article 64 Where registered items of a legal person change during its existence, the legal person shall apply to the registration authority for modification of registration in accordance with law.
Article 65 Where the actual circumstances of a legal person are inconsistent with the registered items, such inconsistency shall not be asserted against a bona fide counterparty.
Article 66 The registration authority shall disclose relevant information on the registration of a legal person in a timely manner in accordance with law.

Article 67 Where a legal person is merged, the rights and obligations of the legal person shall be enjoyed and borne by the legal person resulting from the merger. Where a legal person is divided, the rights and obligations of the legal person shall be enjoyed as joint and several claims and borne as joint and several debts by the legal persons resulting from the division, unless the creditors and debtors agree otherwise.

Article 68 A legal person shall terminate upon occurrence of any of the following causes and completion of liquidation and deregistration in accordance with law: (1) the legal person is dissolved; (2) the legal person is declared bankrupt; or (3) other causes provided for by law. Where laws or administrative regulations require the approval of a relevant authority for the termination of a legal person, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 69 A legal person shall be dissolved under any of the following circumstances: (1) the period of existence prescribed in the articles of association of the legal person expires or other dissolution events prescribed in the articles of association occur; (2) the governing body of the legal person resolves to dissolve it; (3) dissolution is necessary due to a merger or division of the legal person; (4) the legal person's business license or registration certificate is lawfully revoked, or it is ordered to close down or is abolished; or (5) other circumstances provided for by law.

Article 70 Where a legal person is dissolved, except in the case of a merger or division, the person obligated to liquidate shall promptly form a liquidation panel to carry out liquidation. The members of the executive body or the decision-making body of the legal person, such as directors and council members, shall be the persons obligated to liquidate, unless otherwise provided for by laws or administrative regulations, in which case such provisions shall prevail. Where the person obligated to liquidate fails to perform the liquidation obligation in a timely manner, thereby causing damage, such person shall bear civil liability. The competent authority or an interested person may apply to the People's Court for appointing relevant persons to form a liquidation panel to carry out liquidation.

Article 71 The liquidation procedures and the functions and powers of the liquidation panel of a legal person shall be governed by the provisions of relevant laws. In the absence of such provisions, the relevant provisions of the company law shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 72 During the liquidation period, the legal person shall continue to exist but shall not engage in activities unrelated to the liquidation. The remaining property of the legal person after liquidation shall be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association of the legal person or the resolution of its governing body, unless otherwise provided for by law, in which case such provisions shall prevail. A legal person shall terminate upon the conclusion of liquidation and completion of its deregistration. Where a legal person is not required to undergo registration in accordance with law, it shall terminate upon the conclusion of liquidation.
Article 73 Where a legal person is declared bankrupt, the legal person shall terminate upon completion of bankruptcy liquidation and its deregistration in accordance with law.

Article 74 A legal person may establish branches in accordance with law. Where laws or administrative regulations require the branches to be registered, such provisions shall prevail. Where a branch engages in civil activities in its own name, the legal person shall bear the civil liability arising therefrom. Alternatively, the liability may first be satisfied from the property managed by such branch, and any deficiency shall be borne by the legal person.

Article 75 The legal consequences of civil activities conducted by a founder for the purpose of establishing a legal person shall be borne by the legal person. If the legal person is not established, the legal consequences shall be borne by the founder. Where there are two or more founders, they shall enjoy joint and several claims and bear joint and several debts. Where a founder engages in civil activities in its own name for the purpose of establishing a legal person and thereby incurs civil liability, a third party shall have the right to elect to demand that the legal person or the founder bear such liability.

Article 76 A legal person established for the purpose of obtaining profits and distributing them to its shareholders or other contributors shall be a for-profit legal person. For-profit legal persons include limited liability companies, companies limited by shares, and other enterprise legal persons.
Article 77 A for-profit legal person shall be established upon registration in accordance with law.

Article 78 A for-profit legal person established according to law shall be issued a business license for a for-profit legal person by the registration authority. The date of issuance of the business license shall be the date of establishment of the for-profit legal person.
Article 79 To establish a for-profit legal person, the articles of association of the legal person shall be formulated in accordance with law.

Article 80 A for-profit legal person shall have a governing body. The governing body shall exercise the powers of amending the articles of association of the legal person, electing or replacing members of the executive body and the supervisory body, and performing other functions as prescribed in the articles of association of the legal person.

Article 81 A for-profit legal person shall establish an executive body. The executive body shall exercise the functions of convening meetings of the authoritative body, deciding on the business plans and investment schemes of the legal person, deciding on the establishment of the internal management structure of the legal person, and other functions as provided for in the legal person's articles of association. Where the executive body is a board of directors or an executive director, the chairman of the board, the executive director, or the manager shall serve as the legal representative in accordance with the legal person's articles of association. Where no board of directors or executive director is established, the principal person in charge provided by the legal person's articles of association shall serve as its executive body and legal representative.

Article 82 Where a for-profit legal person establishes a supervisory body such as a board of supervisors or a supervisor, the supervisory body shall exercise, according to law, the functions of examining the finances of the legal person, supervising the performance of duties by members of the executive body and senior officers, and other functions as provided for in the legal person's articles of association.

Article 83 The contributors of a for-profit legal person shall not abuse their rights as contributors to harm the interests of the legal person or other contributors. Where the abuse of contributor rights causes losses to the legal person or other contributors, the abusive contributor shall bear civil liability according to law. The contributors of a for-profit legal person shall not abuse the independent status of the legal person and the limited liability of contributors to harm the interests of the legal person's creditors. Where the abuse of the independent status of the legal person and the limited liability of contributors to evade debts seriously harms the interests of the legal person's creditors, such contributors shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of the legal person.

Article 84 The controlling contributor, actual controller, directors, supervisors, and senior officers of a for-profit legal person shall not use their affiliated relationships to harm the interests of the legal person. Where the use of an affiliated relationship causes losses to the legal person, such persons shall bear compensation liability.

Article 85 Where the convening procedures or voting methods of a meeting of the authoritative body or executive body of a for-profit legal person for making a resolution violate any law, administrative regulation, or the legal person's articles of association, or the content of such a resolution violates the articles of association, a contributor of the for-profit legal person may request the People's Court to revoke the resolution. However, civil legal relationships formed between the for-profit legal person and a bona fide counterparty based on such a resolution shall not be affected.

Article 86 When engaging in business activities, a for-profit legal person shall abide by business ethics, maintain transaction security, accept the supervision of the government and the public, and bear social responsibility.

Article 87 A legal person established for a public interest purpose or other non-profit purpose, which does not distribute the profits it obtains to its contributors, founders, or members, is a non-profit legal person. Non-profit legal persons include public institutions, social organizations, foundations, social service institutions, and the like.

Article 88 A public institution that meets the conditions for being a legal person and is established to provide public services to meet the needs of economic and social development shall, upon being registered and established according to law, acquire the status of a public institution legal person. Where registration as a legal person is not required according to law, it shall have the status of a public institution legal person as of the date of its establishment.

Article 89 Where a public institution legal person establishes a board of directors, the board shall be its decision-making body, unless otherwise provided by law. The legal representative of a public institution legal person shall be appointed in accordance with the provisions of any law, administrative regulation, or the legal person's articles of association.

Article 90 A social organization that meets the conditions for being a legal person and is established based on the common will of its members for a non-profit purpose such as public interest or the common interests of its members shall, upon being registered and established according to law, acquire the status of a social organization legal person. Where registration as a legal person is not required according to law, it shall have the status of a social organization legal person as of the date of its establishment.

Article 91 To establish a social organization legal person, the articles of association of the legal person shall be formulated according to law. A social organization legal person shall establish an authoritative body such as a membership assembly or a membership representative assembly. A social organization legal person shall establish an executive body such as a board of directors. The responsible person such as the chairman or president shall serve as the legal representative in accordance with the provisions of the legal person's articles of association.

Article 92 A foundation, social service institution, or the like established with donated property for a public interest purpose and meeting the conditions for being a legal person shall, upon being registered and established according to law, acquire the status of a donation legal person. A religious activity site established according to law and meeting the conditions for being a legal person may apply for registration as a legal person and acquire the status of a donation legal person. Where any law or administrative regulation provides for religious activity sites, such provisions shall apply.

Article 93 To establish a donation legal person, the articles of association of the legal person shall be formulated according to law. A donation legal person shall establish a decision-making body such as a board of directors or a democratic management organization, and shall also establish an executive body. The responsible person such as the chairman of the board shall serve as the legal representative in accordance with the provisions of the legal person's articles of association. A donation legal person shall establish a supervisory body such as a board of supervisors.

Article 94 A donor shall have the right to inquire of the donation legal person about the use and management of the donated property and to make comments and suggestions, and the donation legal person shall provide prompt and truthful replies. Where the procedures for making a decision by the decision-making body, executive body, or legal representative of a donation legal person violate any law, administrative regulation, or the legal person's articles of association, or the content of such a decision violates the legal person's articles of association, the donor or other interested persons, or the competent authority may request the People's Court to revoke the decision. However, civil legal relationships formed between the donation legal person and a bona fide counterparty based on such a decision shall not be affected.

Article 95 When a non-profit legal person established for a public interest purpose is terminated, the residual property shall not be distributed to its contributors, founders, or members. The residual property shall be used for public interest purposes in accordance with the provisions of the legal person's articles of association or the resolution of its authoritative body. Where it cannot be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of the legal person's articles of association or the resolution of its authoritative body, the competent authority shall arrange for its transfer to a legal person with the same or similar purposes and make a public announcement.

Article 96 The organ legal persons, rural collective economic organization legal persons, urban and rural cooperative economic organization legal persons, and basic-level self-governing mass organization legal persons provided for in this Section are special legal persons.

Article 97 An organ with independent funds and a statutory body assuming administrative functions shall, as of the date of its establishment, have the status of an organ legal person and may engage in civil activities necessary for performing its functions.

Article 98 Where an organ legal person is abolished, the legal person shall terminate, and its civil rights and obligations shall be enjoyed and assumed by the succeeding organ legal person. Where there is no succeeding organ legal person, they shall be enjoyed and assumed by the organ legal person that made the abolition decision.

Article 99 A rural collective economic organization shall acquire the status of a legal person according to law. Where any law or administrative regulation provides for rural collective economic organizations, such provisions shall apply.

Article 100 An urban or rural cooperative economic organization shall acquire the status of a legal person according to law. Where any law or administrative regulation provides for urban or rural cooperative economic organizations, such provisions shall apply.

Article 101 A residents committee or a villagers committee has the legal person status of a grassroots self-governing mass organization and may engage in civil activities necessary for the performance of its functions. Where no rural collective economic organization has been established, the villagers committee may, according to law, perform the functions of the rural collective economic organization on its behalf.

Article 102 An unincorporated organization is an organization that does not have the status of a legal person but is able to engage in civil activities in its own name according to law. Unincorporated organizations include sole proprietorship enterprises, partnership enterprises, and professional service institutions without legal person status, among others.

Article 103 An unincorporated organization shall be registered in accordance with the provisions of law. Where the formation of an unincorporated organization is subject to approval by the relevant authority according to laws or administrative regulations, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 104 Where the property of an unincorporated organization is insufficient to satisfy its debts, its contributors or founders shall bear unlimited liability. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.
Article 105 An unincorporated organization may designate one or more persons to represent the organization in engaging in civil activities.

Article 106 An unincorporated organization shall be dissolved under any of the following circumstances: (1) the period of duration specified in its constitutive documents expires or another ground for dissolution specified in its constitutive documents occurs; (2) its contributors or founders decide to dissolve it; or (3) any other circumstance provided by law.
Article 107 Where an unincorporated organization is dissolved, it shall undergo liquidation according to law.
Article 108 In addition to the provisions of this Chapter, an unincorporated organization shall be governed mutatis mutandis by the relevant provisions of Section 1, Chapter 3 of this Part.
Article 109 The personal freedom and human dignity of a natural person shall be protected by law.

Article 110 A natural person enjoys the rights to life, physical integrity, health, name, portrait, reputation, honor, privacy, and freedom of marriage, among others. A legal person or an unincorporated organization enjoys the rights to name, reputation, and honor.

Article 111 The personal information of a natural person shall be protected by law. Any organization or individual that needs to obtain personal information of others shall obtain it according to law and ensure its security, and shall not illegally collect, use, process, or transmit personal information of others, nor illegally trade, provide, or disclose personal information of others.
Article 112 The personal rights of a natural person arising from marital or family relationships, among others, shall be protected by law.
Article 113 The property rights of civil subjects shall be equally protected by law.

Article 114 A civil subject shall enjoy real rights according to law. A real right is the right of the right holder to directly control and exclude others with respect to a specific property according to law, including ownership, usufruct, and security interests.
Article 115 Property includes immovable and movable property. Where a right is provided by law as the object of a real right, such provisions shall prevail.
Article 116 The types and content of real rights shall be provided by law.

Article 117 Where immovable or movable property is expropriated or requisitioned for the needs of the public interest, in accordance with the authority and procedures provided by law, fair and reasonable compensation shall be given.

Article 118 A civil subject shall enjoy obligatory rights according to law. An obligatory right is the right of the right holder to request a specific obligor to perform or refrain from performing a certain act, arising from a contract, tort, negotiorum gestio, unjust enrichment, or other provisions of law.
Article 119 A contract formed according to law shall be legally binding on the parties.
Article 120 Where a civil right or interest is infringed upon, the aggrieved party has the right to request the tortfeasor to bear tort liability.

Article 121 A person who, without a statutory or contractual obligation, manages the affairs of another to prevent harm to that other person's interests shall have the right to request the beneficiary to reimburse the necessary expenses incurred thereby.
Article 122 Where a person acquires unjust benefits without any legal basis, the person who suffers loss shall have the right to request the return of such unjust benefits.

Article 123 A civil subject shall enjoy intellectual property rights according to law. Intellectual property rights are the exclusive rights enjoyed by the right holder according to law in respect of the following subject matter: (1) works; (2) inventions, utility models, and designs; (3) trademarks; (4) geographical indications; (5) trade secrets; (6) layout designs of integrated circuits; (7) new plant varieties; (8) other subject matter as provided by law.
Article 124 A natural person shall enjoy the right of succession according to law. The lawful private property of a natural person may be inherited according to law.
Article 125 A civil subject shall enjoy equity interests and other investment rights according to law.
Article 126 A civil subject shall enjoy other civil rights and interests as provided by law.
Article 127 Where laws provide for the protection of data and network virtual property, such provisions shall apply.
Article 128 Where laws provide special provisions for the protection of the civil rights of minors, the elderly, persons with disabilities, women, consumers, and others, such provisions shall apply.
Article 129 Civil rights may be acquired through civil juristic acts, factual acts, events provided by law, or other means provided by law.
Article 130 A civil subject shall exercise civil rights according to its own will and in accordance with law, and shall not be interfered with.
Article 131 When exercising rights, a civil subject shall perform the obligations provided by law and agreed by the parties.
Article 132 A civil subject shall not abuse civil rights to harm the national interest, the public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others.
Article 133 A civil juristic act is an act of a civil subject to establish, modify, or terminate a civil juristic relationship through a declaration of intent.

Article 134 A civil juristic act may be established based on the consensus of declarations of intent of two or more parties, and may also be established based on the declaration of intent of a single party. Where a legal person or an unincorporated organization makes a resolution in accordance with the deliberation methods and voting procedures provided by law or its articles of association, such act of making a resolution shall be established.

Article 135 A civil juristic act may be made in writing, orally, or in any other form; where a law or administrative regulation provides or the parties agree that a specific form shall be used, such specific form shall be used.

Article 136 A civil juristic act shall become effective upon its establishment, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties. No actor shall, without the basis of legal provisions or the consent of the other party, arbitrarily modify or rescind a civil juristic act.

Article 137 A declaration of intent made in a dialogue shall become effective when the counterparty becomes aware of its content. A declaration of intent made otherwise than in a dialogue shall become effective when it reaches the counterparty. Where a declaration of intent is made otherwise than in a dialogue in the form of an electronic data message, and the counterparty has designated a specific system for receiving such data messages, it shall become effective when the data message enters that specific system; where no specific system is designated, it shall become effective when the counterparty knows or should know that the data message has entered its system. Where the parties have otherwise agreed on the effective time of a declaration of intent made in the form of an electronic data message, such agreement shall prevail.
Article 138 A declaration of intent made without a counterparty shall become effective upon completion of the declaration. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall apply.
Article 139 A declaration of intent made by public announcement shall become effective upon the issuance of the announcement.

Article 140 An actor may make a declaration of intent expressly or by implication. Silence shall be deemed a declaration of intent only where so provided by law, agreed by the parties, or in accordance with the transaction practices between the parties.

Article 141 A person may withdraw a declaration of intent. The notice of withdrawal of a declaration of intent shall reach the other party before or at the same time as the declaration of intent reaches the other party.

Article 142 The interpretation of a declaration of intent made to a counterparty shall be made in accordance with the wording used, and the meaning of the declaration of intent shall be determined by reference to the relevant provisions, the nature and purpose of the act, usages, and the principle of good faith. The interpretation of a declaration of intent not made to a counterparty shall not be strictly confined to the wording used, but the true intent of the person shall be determined by reference to the relevant provisions, the nature and purpose of the act, usages, and the principle of good faith.

Article 143 A civil juristic act that meets the following conditions is valid: (1) the person has corresponding capacity for civil conduct; (2) the declaration of intent is genuine; and (3) it does not violate the mandatory provisions of any law or administrative regulation, nor contravene public order and good customs.
Article 144 A civil juristic act performed by a person without capacity for civil conduct is void.

Article 145 A civil juristic act performed by a person with limited capacity for civil conduct that is purely beneficial to such person, or that is appropriate to such person's age, intelligence, or mental health condition, is valid; any other civil juristic act performed by such person is valid only after being consented to or ratified by the legal representative. The counterparty may urge the legal representative to ratify the act within thirty days from receipt of the notice. If the legal representative fails to respond, ratification shall be deemed to have been refused. Before the civil juristic act is ratified, a bona fide counterparty has the right to revoke the act. Revocation shall be made by notice.

Article 146 A civil juristic act performed by a person and the counterparty with a false declaration of intent is void. The validity of a civil juristic act concealed by a false declaration of intent shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws.
Article 147 A person who performs a civil juristic act based on a material mistake has the right to request a People's Court or an arbitration institution to revoke the act.

Article 148 Where a party, by means of fraud, causes the other party to perform a civil juristic act contrary to its true intent, the defrauded party has the right to request a People's Court or an arbitration institution to revoke the act.

Article 149 Where a third party commits fraud, causing one party to perform a civil juristic act contrary to its true intent, and the other party knows or should have known of the fraud, the defrauded party has the right to request a People's Court or an arbitration institution to revoke the act.

Article 150 Where a party or a third party, by means of duress, causes the other party to perform a civil juristic act contrary to its true intent, the coerced party has the right to request a People's Court or an arbitration institution to revoke the act.

Article 151 Where one party takes advantage of the other party's predicament, lack of judgment, or other circumstances, causing the civil juristic act to be manifestly unfair when concluded, the aggrieved party has the right to request a People's Court or an arbitration institution to revoke the act.

Article 152 The right to revocation is extinguished in any of the following circumstances: (1) a party fails to exercise the right to revocation within one year from the date it knows or should have known of the cause for revocation, or a party acting under a material mistake fails to exercise the right to revocation within ninety days from the date it knows or should have known of the cause for revocation; (2) a coerced party fails to exercise the right to revocation within one year from the date the duress ceases; or (3) a party, after learning of the cause for revocation, expressly states or indicates by its own conduct that it waives the right to revocation. The right to revocation is extinguished if a party fails to exercise it within five years from the date the civil juristic act took effect.

Article 153 A civil juristic act that violates a mandatory provision of any law or administrative regulation is void, unless the mandatory provision does not render the civil juristic act void. A civil juristic act that contravenes public order and good customs is void.
Article 154 A civil juristic act performed by a person and the counterparty through malicious collusion to harm the lawful rights and interests of another person is void.
Article 155 A civil juristic act that is void or has been revoked has no legally binding effect ab initio.
Article 156 Where part of a civil juristic act is void without affecting the validity of other parts, the other parts shall remain valid.

Article 157 After a civil juristic act is void, revoked, or confirmed to be ineffective, any property obtained by a person as a result of the act shall be returned; if it cannot be returned or return is unnecessary, compensation shall be made in monetary terms. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for any losses incurred thereby; if both parties are at fault, each party shall bear the corresponding liability. Where otherwise provided by law, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 158 A civil juristic act may be subject to a condition, unless it cannot be subject to a condition by its nature. A civil juristic act subject to a condition precedent shall take effect when the condition is fulfilled. A civil juristic act subject to a condition subsequent shall cease to have effect when the condition is fulfilled.

Article 159 Under a conditional civil juristic act, if a party improperly prevents the fulfillment of the condition for its own benefit, the condition shall be deemed to have been fulfilled; if a party improperly procures the fulfillment of the condition, the condition shall be deemed not to have been fulfilled.

Article 160 A civil juristic act may be subject to a time limit, unless it cannot be subject to a time limit by its nature. A civil juristic act subject to a time period for its commencement shall take effect when the time period arrives. A civil juristic act subject to a time period for its termination shall cease to have effect when the time period expires.

Article 161 A civil subject may perform a civil juristic act through an agent. A civil juristic act that shall be performed personally by the principal according to the provisions of law, the agreement of the parties, or the nature of the civil juristic act may not be performed through an agent.
Article 162 A civil juristic act performed by an agent in the name of the principal within the scope of the power of agency shall be binding on the principal.

Article 163 Agency includes mandated agency and statutory agency. A mandated agent shall exercise the power of agency in accordance with the mandate of the principal. A statutory agent shall exercise the power of agency in accordance with the provisions of law.

Article 164 Where an agent fails to perform or fails to fully perform its duties, causing damage to the principal, it shall bear civil liability. Where the agent and the other party maliciously collude, causing damage to the lawful rights and interests of the principal, the agent and the other party shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 165 Where a mandate for agency is made in written form, the power of attorney shall state the name of the agent, the matters of agency, the scope of authority and the term, and shall be signed or sealed by the principal.
Article 166 Where several persons act as agents for the same matters of agency, they shall jointly exercise the power of agency, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 167 Where an agent knows or should have known that the matters of agency are illegal but still performs the agency act, or the principal knows or should have known that the agent's act is illegal but raises no objection, the principal and the agent shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 168 An agent may not perform a civil juristic act in the name of the principal with itself, unless the principal consents or ratifies it. An agent may not perform a civil juristic act in the name of the principal with another person whom the agent also represents at the same time, unless both principals consent or ratify it.

Article 169 Where an agent needs to sub-entrust the agency to a third party, the agent shall obtain the consent or ratification of the principal. Where the sub-entrustment is consented to or ratified by the principal, the principal may directly give instructions to the third party regarding the agency matters, and the agent shall only be liable for the selection of the third party and for the instructions given to the third party. Where the sub-entrustment is not consented to or ratified by the principal, the agent shall be liable for the acts of the third party; except that, in an emergency situation, the agent needs to sub-entrust the agency to a third party in order to protect the interests of the principal.

Article 170 A civil juristic act performed by a person who performs tasks for a legal person or an unincorporated organization, within the scope of their duties, in the name of the legal person or unincorporated organization, shall be binding on the legal person or unincorporated organization. Any restriction by the legal person or unincorporated organization on the scope of duties of the person performing tasks for it may not be asserted against a bona fide other party.

Article 171 Where an actor performs an agency act without the power of agency, beyond the scope of agency, or after the power of agency has terminated, and such act is not ratified by the principal, it shall not be binding on the principal. The other party may demand that the principal ratify the act within thirty days after receiving the notice. If the principal does not respond, it shall be deemed a refusal to ratify. Before the act performed by the actor is ratified, a bona fide other party has the right to revoke it. The revocation shall be made by notice. Where the act performed by the actor is not ratified, a bona fide other party has the right to demand that the actor perform the obligation or compensate for the damage suffered. However, the scope of compensation may not exceed the benefits that the other party could have obtained if the principal had ratified the act. Where the other party knows or should have known that the actor has no power of agency, the other party and the actor shall bear liability according to their respective fault.

Article 172 Where an actor performs an agency act without the power of agency, beyond the scope of agency, or after the power of agency has terminated, and the other party has reason to believe that the actor has the power of agency, the agency act shall be valid.

Article 173 The mandated agency shall terminate under any of the following circumstances: (1) the term of agency expires or the matters of agency are completed; (2) the principal revokes the mandate or the agent resigns from the mandate; (3) the agent loses capacity for civil conduct; (4) the agent or the principal dies; or (5) the legal person or unincorporated organization acting as the agent or the principal terminates.

Article 174 After the death of the principal, the agency acts performed by the mandated agent shall be valid under any of the following circumstances: (1) the agent neither knew nor should have known of the death of the principal; (2) the successor of the principal recognizes the acts; (3) the authorization clearly states that the power of agency terminates upon completion of the matters of agency; or (4) the act has been performed before the death of the principal, and the agent continues to act for the benefit of the successor of the principal. Where the legal person or unincorporated organization acting as the principal terminates, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply by analogy.

Article 175 The statutory agency shall terminate under any of the following circumstances: (1) the principal acquires or regains full capacity for civil conduct; (2) the agent loses capacity for civil conduct; (3) the agent or the principal dies; or (4) other circumstances prescribed by law.
Article 176 A civil subject shall perform civil obligations and bear civil liability in accordance with the provisions of law or the agreement of the parties.

Article 177 Where two or more persons bear several liability according to law, if the extent of liability can be determined, each shall bear the corresponding liability; if it is difficult to determine the extent of liability, they shall bear the liability in equal shares.

Article 178 Where two or more persons bear joint and several liability according to law, the obligee has the right to demand that part or all of the jointly and severally liable persons bear the liability. The shares of liability of the jointly and severally liable persons shall be determined according to the extent of each person's liability; if it is difficult to determine the extent of liability, they shall bear the liability in equal shares. A jointly and severally liable person who actually bears liability exceeding its own share has the right to seek contribution from the other jointly and severally liable persons. Joint and several liability shall be provided for by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 179 The main methods of bearing civil liability include: (1) cessation of the infringement; (2) removal of the obstruction; (3) elimination of the danger; (4) return of property; (5) restoration to the original state; (6) repair, redoing, or replacement; (7) continued performance; (8) compensation for losses; (9) payment of liquidated damages; (10) elimination of adverse effects and restoration of reputation; and (11) extension of an apology. Where the law provides for punitive damages, such provisions shall apply. The methods of bearing civil liability provided for in this Article may be applied separately or in combination.

Article 180 Where a civil obligation cannot be performed due to force majeure, no civil liability shall be borne, unless otherwise provided by law. Force majeure means an objective circumstance that is unforeseeable, unavoidable, and insurmountable.

Article 181 If damage is caused by a justifiable defense, the person acting in such defense shall not bear civil liability. If the justifiable defense exceeds the necessary limit and causes undue damage, the person acting in such defense shall bear appropriate civil liability.

Article 182 If damage is caused by an act of rescue, civil liability shall be borne by the person who gave rise to the peril. If the peril arises from natural causes, the person performing the act of rescue shall not bear civil liability, but may provide appropriate compensation. If the measures taken in the act of rescue are improper or exceed the necessary limit and cause undue damage, the person performing the act of rescue shall bear appropriate civil liability.

Article 183 If a person suffers damage while protecting the civil rights and interests of another, civil liability shall be borne by the infringer, and the beneficiary may provide appropriate compensation. If there is no infringer, the infringer has fled, or the infringer is unable to bear civil liability, the beneficiary shall provide appropriate compensation if the victim requests compensation.
Article 184 If a person voluntarily renders emergency aid and causes damage to the aided person, the rescuer shall not bear civil liability.
Article 185 A person who infringes upon the name, likeness, reputation, or honor of heroes and martyrs, thereby harming the public interest, shall bear civil liability.

Article 186 If a party's breach of contract damages the personal or property rights and interests of the other party, the damaged party has the right to choose to request the breaching party to bear liability for breach of contract or liability for tort.

Article 187 If a civil subject shall bear civil liability, administrative liability, and criminal liability for the same act, the assumption of administrative liability or criminal liability shall not affect the assumption of civil liability; if the property of the civil subject is insufficient to pay all obligations, it shall first be used for assuming civil liability.

Article 188 The limitation of action for requesting the People's Court to protect civil rights shall be three years. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall prevail. The limitation of action shall commence on the date when the right holder knows or should have known that the right has been damaged and who the obligor is. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall prevail. However, if more than twenty years have elapsed since the right was damaged, the People's Court shall not grant protection; in special circumstances, the People's Court may decide to extend the period upon the application of the right holder.

Article 189 If the parties agree that the same debt shall be performed in installments, the limitation of action shall commence on the date on which the performance period for the last installment expires.

Article 190 The limitation of action for a claim of a person with no capacity for civil conduct or with limited capacity for civil conduct against his or her statutory agent shall commence on the date on which such statutory agency terminates.
Article 191 The limitation of action for a minor's claim for damages arising from sexual assault shall commence on the date on which the victim reaches the age of eighteen.

Article 192 If the limitation of action has expired, the obligor may raise a defense of non-performance. After the limitation of action has expired, if the obligor agrees to perform, the obligor may not use the expiration of the limitation of action as a defense; if the obligor has already voluntarily performed, the obligor may not request the return of the performance.
Article 193 The People's Court shall not apply the provisions on limitation of action ex officio.

Article 194 If, within the last six months of the limitation of action, a right holder is unable to exercise the right of claim due to the following obstacles, the limitation of action shall be suspended: (1) force majeure; (2) a person with no capacity for civil conduct or with limited capacity for civil conduct has no statutory agent, or the statutory agent has died, lost capacity for civil conduct, or lost the power of agency; (3) no heir or estate administrator has been determined after the commencement of succession; (4) the right holder is controlled by the obligor or another person; (5) other obstacles that prevent the right holder from exercising the right of claim. The limitation of action shall expire six months after the date on which the cause of suspension is eliminated.

Article 195 The limitation of action shall be interrupted in any of the following circumstances, and the limitation period shall recommence from the time of the interruption or the conclusion of the relevant proceedings: (1) the right holder requests the obligor to perform; (2) the obligor agrees to perform the obligation; (3) the right holder files a lawsuit or applies for arbitration; or (4) other circumstances having equivalent effect to filing a lawsuit or applying for arbitration.

Article 196 The following claims shall not be subject to the provisions on limitation of action: (1) claims for cessation of infringement, removal of obstruction, or elimination of danger; (2) claims by the holder of a real right in immovable property or a registered real right in movable property for the return of property; (3) claims for payment of child support, alimony, or maintenance; and (4) other claims that are not subject to the limitation of action according to law.

Article 197 The period of limitation of action, the method of calculation, and the grounds for suspension and interruption shall be provided by law; any agreement by the parties to the contrary shall be void. Any advance waiver by the parties of the benefits of the limitation of action shall be void.
Article 198 Where the law provides for a limitation period for arbitration, such provisions shall prevail; if no such provision exists, the provisions on limitation of action shall apply.

Article 199 The period of existence of a right of avoidance, right of dissolution, or other such rights provided by law or agreed by the parties shall, unless the law provides otherwise, commence on the date when the right holder knows or should have known that the right has arisen, and the provisions on suspension, interruption, and extension of the limitation of action shall not apply to it. Upon the expiration of the period of existence, the right of avoidance, right of dissolution, or other such rights shall be extinguished.
Article 200 Periods referred to in the Civil Code shall be calculated in accordance with the Gregorian calendar in years, months, days, and hours.

Article 201 Where a time period is calculated by year, month, or day, the first day shall not be counted, and the calculation shall start from the next day. Where a time period is calculated by hour, the calculation shall start from the time specified by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 202 Where a time period is calculated by year or month, the corresponding day of the month of expiration shall be the last day of the time period; if there is no such corresponding day, the last day of that month shall be the last day of the time period.

Article 203 If the last day of a time period falls on a legal holiday, the day after the end of such legal holiday shall be the last day of the time period. The deadline for the last day of a time period shall be twenty-four hours; if there is business operating time, the time at which business activities cease shall be the deadline.
Article 204 The method for calculating time periods shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, unless otherwise provided by law or otherwise agreed by the parties.
Article 205 This Book regulates the civil relations arising from the attribution and use of things.

Article 206 The State upholds and improves the basic socialist economic systems, including the system under which public ownership is the mainstay and multiple forms of ownership develop together, the system under which distribution according to work is the mainstay and multiple modes of distribution coexist, and the socialist market economy system. The State consolidates and develops the public sector of the economy, and encourages, supports, and guides the development of the non-public sector of the economy. The State practices a socialist market economy and guarantees the equal legal status and development rights of all market entities.

Article 207 The property rights of the State, collectives, and private persons, as well as those of other right holders, shall be equally protected by law, and no organization or individual shall infringe upon them.

Article 208 The creation, alteration, transfer, and extinguishment of property rights in immovable property shall be registered in accordance with the provisions of law. The creation and transfer of property rights in movable property shall be delivered in accordance with the provisions of law.

Article 209 The creation, alteration, transfer, and extinguishment of property rights in immovable property shall take effect upon registration in accordance with law; without registration, they shall not take effect, unless otherwise provided by law. The ownership of natural resources that are owned by the State according to law may be exempted from registration.

Article 210 Registration of immovable property shall be handled by the registration authority at the place where the immovable property is located. The State practices a unified registration system for immovable property. The scope, registration authorities, and registration methods for such unified registration shall be provided by laws and administrative regulations.

Article 211 A party applying for registration shall, depending on the different registration matters, provide certificates of title and necessary materials such as the boundaries and area of the immovable property.

Article 212 The registration authority shall perform the following duties: (1) inspecting the certificates of title and other necessary materials provided by the applicant; (2) inquiring with the applicant about the relevant registration matters; (3) accurately and promptly registering the relevant matters; and (4) other duties provided by laws and administrative regulations. If the relevant circumstances of the immovable property for which registration is applied require further verification, the registration authority may request the applicant to supplement materials, and may conduct an on-site inspection when necessary.

Article 213 The registration authority shall not engage in the following acts: (1) requiring an appraisal of the immovable property; (2) conducting duplicate registration under the guise of annual inspection or the like; or (3) other acts exceeding the scope of its registration duties.

Article 214 The creation, alteration, transfer, and extinguishment of a property right in immovable property, which shall be registered according to the provisions of law, shall take effect upon being entered in the immovable property register.

Article 215 A contract concluded between parties concerning the creation, alteration, transfer, or extinguishment of a property right in immovable property shall take effect upon its formation, unless otherwise provided by law or otherwise agreed by the parties; failure to complete the registration of the property right shall not affect the validity of the contract.

Article 216 The immovable property register shall be the basis for determining the attribution and content of property rights. The immovable property register shall be managed by the registration authority.

Article 217 The certificate of title to immovable property shall be the proof that the right holder enjoys the property right in such immovable property. The matters recorded in the certificate of title to immovable property shall be consistent with the immovable property register; in case of any inconsistency, the immovable property register shall prevail, unless there is evidence proving that the immovable property register is indeed erroneous.
Article 218 The right holder or any interested party may apply to inspect or reproduce the immovable property registration materials, and the registration authority shall provide them.
Article 219 An interested party shall not disclose or unlawfully use the immovable property registration materials of the right holder.

Article 220 If a right holder or an interested party believes that a matter recorded in the immovable property register is erroneous, that person may apply for a corrective registration. If the right holder recorded in the immovable property register consents in writing to the correction or if there is evidence proving that the registration is indeed erroneous, the registration authority shall make the correction. If the right holder recorded in the immovable property register does not consent to the correction, the interested party may apply for an objection registration. Where the registration authority makes the objection registration, the objection registration shall lapse if the applicant fails to bring a lawsuit within fifteen days from the date of the objection registration. If the objection registration is improper and causes damage to the right holder, the right holder may request the applicant to pay damages.

Article 221 Where the parties enter into an agreement for the sale of a house or any other agreement for a real right in immovable property, they may, in order to secure the realization of such real right in future, apply to the registration authority for advance notice registration in accordance with the agreement. After the advance notice registration is effected, any disposal of such immovable property without the consent of the right holder under the advance notice registration shall not have the effect of a real right. After the advance notice registration is effected, the advance notice registration shall cease to have effect if the obligatory claim is extinguished or if no application for registration of the immovable property is made within ninety days from the date on which such registration may be made.

Article 222 Where a party applying for registration with false materials causes damage to another person, it shall bear compensation liability. Where damage is caused to another person due to a registration error, the registration authority shall bear compensation liability. The registration authority, after making compensation, shall have the right of recourse against the person who caused the registration error.
Article 223 The fee for registration of immovable property shall be collected on a per-item basis and shall not be collected as a percentage of the area, volume, or price of the immovable property.
Article 224 The creation and transfer of a real right in movable property shall take effect upon delivery, unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 225 The creation, modification, transfer, or extinction of a real right in a vessel, aircraft, motor vehicle, or the like, if not registered, may not be asserted against a bona fide third party.

Article 226 Where, before the creation or transfer of a real right in movable property, the right holder already possesses such movable property, the real right shall take effect at the time when the civil juristic act becomes effective.

Article 227 Where, before the creation or transfer of a real right in movable property, the movable property is possessed by a third party, the person obligated to deliver may, in lieu of delivery, transfer the right to claim the return of the original property from such third party.

Article 228 Where, upon the transfer of a real right in movable property, the parties further agree that the transferor shall continue to possess the movable property, the real right shall take effect at the time when such agreement becomes effective.

Article 229 Where a real right is created, modified, transferred, or extinguished by reason of a legal document of a people's court or an arbitration authority, or an expropriation decision of the people's government, such real right shall take effect at the time when such legal document or expropriation decision becomes effective.
Article 230 Where a real right is acquired by succession, it shall take effect at the commencement of the succession.
Article 231 Where a real right is created or extinguished by a factual act such as lawful construction or demolition of a house, it shall take effect at the time when the factual act is accomplished.

Article 232 Where a real right in immovable property enjoyed in accordance with the provisions of this Section is disposed of and such disposition requires registration according to law, the disposition shall not have the effect of a real right without registration.
Article 233 Where a real right is infringed upon, the right holder may seek resolution by means such as compromise, mediation, arbitration, or litigation.
Article 234 Where a dispute arises over the attribution or content of a real right, an interested person may request a confirmation of the right.
Article 235 Where a person is in unauthorized possession of immovable or movable property, the right holder may demand the return of the original property.
Article 236 Where there is a nuisance to, or a possibility of nuisance to, a real right, the right holder may request the removal of the nuisance or the elimination of the danger.
