Article 237 Where immovable or movable property is damaged, the right holder may, in accordance with law, request repair, re-making, replacement, or restoration to its original condition.

Article 238 Where a real right is infringed upon, causing damage to the right holder, the right holder may, in accordance with law, request compensation for damages or demand that the infringer bear other civil liability.
Article 239 The means for protection of real rights provided in this Chapter may be applied separately or, depending on the circumstances of the infringement, cumulatively. Part Two Ownership
Article 240 An owner shall, in accordance with law, enjoy the right to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of its own immovable or movable property.

Article 241 The owner has the right to establish a usufruct or a security interest on its own immovable or movable property. When exercising their rights, the usufructuary or the holder of a security interest shall not harm the rights and interests of the owner.
Article 242 No organization or individual may acquire ownership of immovable or movable property that, according to law, is exclusively owned by the State.

Article 243 For the purpose of public interest, collectively-owned land and the houses and other immovable property owned by organizations or individuals may be expropriated in accordance with the scope of authority and procedures as provided by law. Where collectively-owned land is expropriated, land compensation fees, resettlement subsidies, and compensation for rural villagers' houses, other attachments on the land, and immature crops shall be paid in full and in a timely manner according to law, and social security expenses for the land-expropriated farmers shall be arranged, so as to ensure their livelihood and protect their lawful rights and interests. Where the houses or other immovable property of an organization or individual is expropriated, expropriation compensation shall be given according to law to protect the lawful rights and interests of the expropriated person; where a private residence is expropriated, the housing conditions of the expropriated person shall also be guaranteed. No organization or individual may embezzle, misappropriate, privately divide, withhold, or delay the payment of expropriation compensation fees or other such expenses.

Article 244 The State applies special protection to arable land, strictly restricts the conversion of agricultural land into construction land, and controls the total volume of construction land. Collectively-owned land shall not be expropriated in violation of the scope of authority and procedures as provided by law.

Article 245 For emergency needs such as emergency rescue and disaster relief, or epidemic prevention and control, an organization's or individual's immovable or movable property may be requisitioned in accordance with the scope of authority and procedures as provided by law. After the requisitioned immovable or movable property is used, it shall be returned to the person from whom it was requisitioned. If an organization's or individual's immovable or movable property is requisitioned or is damaged or lost after requisition, compensation shall be given.

Article 246 Property that, according to law, is owned by the State is owned by the State, that is, by the whole people. The State Council shall exercise ownership of State-owned property on behalf of the State. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.
Article 247 Mineral deposits, water flows, and sea areas are owned by the State.
Article 248 Uninhabited sea islands are owned by the State, and the State Council shall exercise ownership of uninhabited sea islands on behalf of the State.
Article 249 Land in cities is owned by the State. Land in rural areas and suburban areas that, according to law, is owned by the State is owned by the State.
Article 250 Natural resources such as forests, mountains, grasslands, wasteland, and tidal flats are owned by the State, except where the law provides that they are owned by the collectives.
Article 251 Wildlife resources that, according to law, are owned by the State are owned by the State.
Article 252 Radio spectrum resources are owned by the State.
Article 253 Cultural relics that, according to law, are owned by the State are owned by the State.

Article 254 National defense assets are owned by the State. Infrastructure such as railways, highways, electric power facilities, telecommunications facilities, and oil and gas pipelines that, pursuant to law, are owned by the State shall be owned by the State.

Article 255 State organs shall have the right to possess, use, and dispose of the immovable and movable property directly under their control in accordance with the law and the relevant regulations of the State Council.

Article 256 Public institutions established by the State shall have the right to possess, use, and obtain benefits from and dispose of the immovable and movable property directly under their control in accordance with the law and the relevant regulations of the State Council.

Article 257 For enterprises in which the State has made capital contributions, the State Council and local people's governments shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, respectively perform the duties of contributors on behalf of the State and enjoy the rights and interests of contributors.
Article 258 State-owned property is protected by law, and no organization or individual may appropriate, plunder, privately divide, withhold, or damage it.

Article 259 The institutions and their staff members that perform the duties of managing and supervising State-owned property shall strengthen, according to law, the management and supervision of State-owned property, promote the preservation and appreciation of State-owned property, and prevent losses to State-owned property; where any person abuses power or neglects duty, causing losses to State-owned property, the person shall bear legal liability according to law. Where any person, in violation of the provisions on the administration of State-owned property, through measures such as transferring at a low price, conspiring to privately divide property, providing unauthorized guarantees, or other means during processes including enterprise restructuring, merger, division, or related-party transactions, causes losses to State-owned property, the person shall bear legal liability according to law.

Article 260 Collectively-owned immovable and movable property includes: (1) land, forests, mountains, grasslands, wasteland, and tidal flats that, according to law, are owned by the collectives; (2) buildings, production facilities, and farmland water conservancy facilities owned by the collectives; (3) educational, scientific, cultural, health, and sports facilities owned by the collectives; and (4) other immovable and movable property owned by the collectives.

Article 261 The immovables and movables owned by a farmers' collective shall be collectively owned by the members of the collective. The following matters shall be decided by the members of the collective in accordance with statutory procedures: (1) the plan for land contracting and the leasing of land to entities or individuals outside the collective for contracting; (2) the adjustment of the contracted land among individual holders of land contractual management rights; (3) the method for the use and distribution of costs such as land compensation fees; (4) matters such as the change of ownership of enterprises with collective investment; and (5) other matters provided for by law.

Article 262 For land and forests, hills, grasslands, unreclaimed lands, tidelands, etc. owned by a collective, the ownership shall be exercised in accordance with the following provisions: (1) where they are owned by the village farmers' collective, the collective ownership shall be exercised on behalf of the collective by the village collective economic organization or the villagers' committee according to law; (2) where they are respectively owned by two or more farmers' collectives within the village, the collective ownership shall be exercised on behalf of each collective by the respective collective economic organization or the villagers' group within the village according to law; and (3) where they are owned by the township farmers' collective, the collective ownership shall be exercised on behalf of the collective by the township collective economic organization.

Article 263 The immovables and movables owned by an urban collective shall be enjoyed by the collective with the rights to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of them in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 264 A rural collective economic organization, or a villagers' committee or villagers' group shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and its articles of association or village regulations and folk conventions, disclose the status of collective property to its members. The members of the collective shall have the right to consult and reproduce relevant materials.

Article 265 The property owned by a collective shall be protected by law, and no entity or individual may embezzle, loot, privately divide, or destroy it. Where a decision made by a rural collective economic organization, a villagers' committee, or the responsible person thereof infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the members of the collective, the infringed members may request the People's Court to revoke the decision.

Article 266 A private individual shall enjoy the right of ownership over his or her lawful income, houses, articles of daily use, tools of production, raw materials, and other immovables and movables.
Article 267 The lawful property of a private individual shall be protected by law, and no entity or individual may embezzle, loot, or destroy it.

Article 268 The State, a collective, and a private individual may, according to law, make capital contributions to establish a limited liability company, a company limited by shares, or another enterprise. Where immovables or movables owned by the State, a collective, or a private individual are invested in an enterprise, the investors shall, in accordance with the agreement or in proportion to their respective capital contributions, enjoy the rights to receive asset returns, make major decisions, and select business managers, among others, and shall perform the corresponding obligations.

Article 269 A for-profit legal person shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and its articles of association, enjoy the rights to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of its immovables and movables. For the rights of a legal person other than a for-profit legal person over its immovables and movables, the provisions of relevant laws, administrative regulations, and its articles of association shall apply.
Article 270 The immovables and movables lawfully owned by a social organization legal person or a donation legal person shall be protected by law.

Article 271 An owner shall have ownership over the exclusive parts of a building, such as residential and commercial units, and shall have the right of common ownership and joint management over the common parts other than the exclusive parts.

Article 272 An owner shall have the right to possess, use, seek profits from, and dispose of the exclusive parts of the building. When exercising such rights, the owner shall not endanger the safety of the building or impair the lawful rights and interests of other owners.

Article 273 An owner shall have rights and bear obligations in respect of the common parts of a building other than the exclusive parts; the owner shall not fail to perform obligations on the ground of waiving rights. Where an owner transfers the residential or commercial unit in the building, the right of common ownership and joint management over the common parts shall be transferred together.

Article 274 Roads within the building zone shall be owned by the owners, except for those which are urban public roads. Green areas within the building zone shall be owned by the owners, except for those which are urban public green areas or expressly indicated as owned by an individual. Other public places, public facilities and premises for property management services within the building zone shall be owned by the owners.

Article 275 The ownership of parking spaces and garages planned for parking motor vehicles within the building zone shall be agreed by the parties by means of sale, gift, or lease, among others. Parking spaces occupying the roads or other sites owned by the owners for parking motor vehicles shall be owned by the owners.
Article 276 Parking spaces and garages planned for parking motor vehicles within the building zone shall first satisfy the needs of the owners.

Article 277 Owners may establish a owners' assembly and elect a owners' committee. The specific conditions and procedures for the formation of a owners' assembly and a owners' committee shall be governed by the provisions of laws and regulations. The relevant departments of the local people's government and the residents' committee shall provide guidance and assistance for the establishment of a owners' assembly and the election of a owners' committee.

Article 278 The following matters shall be decided jointly by the owners: (1) formulating and amending the rules of procedure of the owners' assembly; (2) formulating and amending the management regulations; (3) electing or replacing members of the owners' committee; (4) selecting and dismissing a property service enterprise or other manager; (5) using the maintenance funds for the building and its ancillary facilities; (6) raising the maintenance funds for the building and its ancillary facilities; (7) altering or rebuilding the building and its ancillary facilities; (8) changing the use of the common parts or utilizing the common parts for business activities; (9) other significant matters concerning the right of common ownership and joint management. A matter to be decided jointly by the owners shall be subject to voting by owners whose exclusive parts account for not less than two-thirds of the total area and who account for not less than two-thirds of the total number of owners. Decisions on matters specified in items (6) through (8) of the preceding paragraph shall be approved by owners whose exclusive parts account for not less than three-fourths of the area of the participating voting owners and who account for not less than three-fourths of the number of the participating voting owners. Decisions on other matters specified in the preceding paragraph shall be approved by owners whose exclusive parts account for more than half of the area of the participating voting owners and who account for more than half of the number of the participating voting owners.

Article 279 An owner shall not, in violation of laws, regulations, and the management regulations, change a residential unit into a commercial unit. Where an owner changes a residential unit into a commercial unit, in addition to complying with laws, regulations, and the management regulations, the owner shall obtain the unanimous consent of the interested owners.

Article 280 Decisions of the owners' assembly or the owners' committee shall be legally binding on the owners. Where a decision made by the owners' assembly or the owners' committee infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of an owner, the aggrieved owner may request the People's Court to revoke the decision.

Article 281 The maintenance funds for a building and its ancillary facilities shall be jointly owned by the owners. Upon a joint decision of the owners, such funds may be used for the repair, renewal, and renovation of the common parts such as elevators, roofs, external walls, and barrier-free facilities. The raising and use of the maintenance funds for a building and its ancillary facilities shall be published periodically. Where a building and its ancillary facilities need to be repaired under emergency circumstances, the owners' assembly or the owners' committee may, according to law, apply for the use of the maintenance funds for the building and its ancillary facilities.

Article 282 The income generated from the use of the common parts of the owners by the developer, the property service enterprise, or other managers, after deducting reasonable costs, shall be jointly owned by the owners.

Article 283 Matters such as the apportionment of expenses and the distribution of proceeds for a building and its ancillary facilities shall be handled in accordance with the agreement, if any; in the absence of an agreement or if the agreement is unclear, they shall be determined according to the proportion of the area of the owners' exclusive parts.

Article 284 Owners may manage the building and its ancillary facilities by themselves, or may entrust a property service enterprise or other manager with the management thereof. With respect to the property service enterprise or other manager engaged by the developer, the owners shall have the right to replace it according to law.

Article 285 A property service enterprise or other manager shall, based on the entrustment of the owners, manage the buildings and their ancillary facilities within the building zone in accordance with the provisions of Part Three of this Law concerning the property service contract, shall accept the supervision of the owners, and shall promptly reply to inquiries raised by the owners regarding the property service. A property service enterprise or other manager shall implement the emergency response measures and other management measures implemented by the government according to law, and shall actively cooperate in carrying out relevant work.

Article 286 Owners shall comply with laws, regulations, and the management covenant, and their relevant conduct shall meet the requirements of resource conservation and ecological environment protection. Owners shall, according to law, cooperate with the property service enterprise or other manager in implementing the emergency response measures and other management measures implemented by the government according to law. With respect to any act that harms the lawful rights and interests of others, such as arbitrarily discarding garbage, discharging pollutants or noise, raising animals in violation of regulations, constructing illegally, encroaching on passageways, or refusing to pay property management fees, the owners' assembly or the owners' committee shall have the right, in accordance with laws, regulations, and the management covenant, to request the actor to cease the infringement, remove the obstruction, eliminate the danger, restore the property to its original condition, or compensate for the losses. Where an owner or other actor refuses to perform the relevant obligations, the interested party may report or complain to the relevant administrative department, and the relevant administrative department shall handle the matter according to law.

Article 287 Owners shall have the right to request the developer, the property service enterprise or other manager, or other owners that infringe upon their lawful rights and interests to bear civil liability.

Article 288 Neighboring right holders of immovable property shall correctly handle neighboring relations in accordance with the principles of facilitating production, making life convenient, promoting solidarity and mutual assistance, and ensuring fairness and reasonableness.

Article 289 Where there are provisions in laws and regulations on handling neighboring relations, such provisions shall be followed; where there are no such provisions in laws and regulations, local customs may be followed.

Article 290 A right holder of immovable property shall provide necessary convenience to neighboring right holders for using water and draining water. The use of natural flowing water shall be reasonably distributed among the neighboring right holders of immovable property. The drainage of natural flowing water shall respect the natural flow direction.

Article 291 Where a neighboring right holder must use the land of a right holder of immovable property for passage or the like, the right holder of immovable property shall provide necessary convenience.

Article 292 Where a right holder of immovable property must use neighboring land or buildings for purposes such as constructing or repairing a building, or laying wires, cables, water pipes, heating pipes, or gas pipes, the right holder of such land or buildings shall provide necessary convenience.

Article 293 The construction of a building shall not violate the relevant national engineering construction standards, and shall not obstruct the ventilation, lighting, or sunshine of neighboring buildings.

Article 294 A right holder of immovable property shall not, in violation of national regulations, discard solid waste or discharge harmful substances such as air pollutants, water pollutants, soil pollutants, noise, light radiation, or electromagnetic radiation.

Article 295 Where a right holder of immovable property excavates land, constructs a building, lays pipelines, or installs equipment, it shall not endanger the safety of the neighboring immovable property.

Article 296 Where a right holder of immovable property uses neighboring immovable property for purposes such as using water, draining water, passing, or laying pipelines, it shall, to the extent possible, avoid causing damage to the neighboring right holder of immovable property.
Article 297 Immovable or movable property may be jointly owned by two or more organizations or individuals. Joint ownership includes ownership in shares and joint ownership.
Article 298 A co-owner by shares shall enjoy ownership of the jointly owned immovable or movable property according to its share.
Article 299 A joint co-owner shall jointly enjoy ownership of the jointly owned immovable or movable property.

Article 300 Co-owners shall manage the jointly owned immovable or movable property in accordance with the agreement; in the absence of an agreement or if the agreement is unclear, each co-owner shall have the right and obligation to manage it.

Article 301 For the disposition of a jointly owned immovable or movable property, or for major repairs, change of nature or use of such property, the consent of the co-owners by shares holding two-thirds or more of the shares or all the joint co-owners shall be obtained, unless otherwise agreed upon among the co-owners.

Article 302 Where the co-owners have agreed on the management expenses and other burdens of the jointly owned property, such agreement shall prevail; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the co-owners by shares shall bear the burdens in proportion to their shares, and the joint co-owners shall bear the burdens jointly.

Article 303 Where the co-owners have agreed not to partition the jointly owned immovable or movable property in order to maintain the co-ownership relationship, such agreement shall be followed; however, if a co-owner has a material reason requiring partition, he may request partition. Where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, a co-owner by shares may request partition at any time, and a joint co-owner may request partition when the basis of joint ownership is lost or there is a material reason requiring partition. If the partition causes damage to other co-owners, compensation shall be made.

Article 304 The co-owners may determine the method of partition through consultation. If no agreement is reached, where the jointly owned immovable or movable property is partitionable and its value shall not be diminished by partition, the property in kind shall be partitioned; where partition is difficult or the value shall be diminished by partition, the proceeds obtained from the appraised value, auction or sale shall be partitioned. If the immovable or movable property obtained by a co-owner through partition is defective, the other co-owners shall share the losses.
Article 305 A co-owner by shares may transfer his share in the jointly owned immovable or movable property. The other co-owners shall have a preemptive right to purchase under equal conditions.

Article 306 Where a co-owner by shares transfers his share in the jointly owned immovable or movable property, he shall promptly notify the other co-owners of the terms of transfer. The other co-owners shall exercise their preemptive right to purchase within a reasonable period. If two or more other co-owners claim to exercise the preemptive right to purchase, they shall determine their respective purchase proportions through consultation; if consultation fails, they shall exercise the preemptive right to purchase in proportion to their respective shares in the co-ownership at the time of transfer.

Article 307 With respect to claims and debts arising from the jointly owned immovable or movable property, in the external relationship, the co-owners shall enjoy joint claims and bear joint debts, unless otherwise provided by law or the third party knows that the co-owners do not have a joint claim-debt relationship; in the internal relationship among the co-owners, unless otherwise agreed by the co-owners, the co-owners by shares shall enjoy claims and bear debts in proportion to their shares, and the joint co-owners shall jointly enjoy claims and bear debts. A co-owner by shares who has repaid debts exceeding his own share shall have the right to claim recourse against the other co-owners.

Article 308 Where the co-owners have not agreed on whether the co-ownership of the immovable or movable property is co-ownership by shares or joint co-ownership, or the agreement is unclear, it shall be deemed as co-ownership by shares, unless the co-owners have a family relationship or similar.

Article 309 Where the shares of co-owners by shares in the jointly owned immovable or movable property are not agreed upon or the agreement is unclear, the shares shall be determined according to the amount of capital contribution; if the capital contribution cannot be determined, the shares shall be deemed to be equal.
Article 310 Where two or more organizations or individuals jointly enjoy a usufruct or security interest, the relevant provisions of this Chapter shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 311 Where a person without the right of disposition transfers an immovable or movable property to a transferee, the owner shall have the right to recover the property. Unless otherwise provided by law, where the following circumstances are met, the transferee shall acquire the ownership of the immovable or movable property: (1) the transferee is in good faith at the time of the transfer of the immovable or movable property; (2) the transfer is made at a reasonable price; (3) the transferred immovable or movable property that is required by law to be registered has been registered, and that which does not require registration has been delivered to the transferee. Where the transferee acquires the ownership of the immovable or movable property in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the original owner shall have the right to claim damages from the person without the right of disposition. Where a party acquires other real rights in good faith, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 312 The owner or other right holder shall have the right to recover a lost property. Where the lost property is possessed by another person through transfer, the right holder shall have the right to claim damages from the person without the right of disposition, or claim the return of the original property from the transferee within two years from the date when he knows or should have known the transferee; however, if the transferee has purchased the lost property through auction or from a qualified business operator, the right holder shall, when claiming the return of the original property, pay the expenses incurred by the transferee. After paying the expenses to the transferee, the right holder shall have the right to claim recourse against the person without the right of disposition.

Article 313 After a transferee in good faith acquires a movable property, the original rights on such movable property shall extinguish, unless the transferee in good faith knew or should have known of such rights at the time of the transfer.

Article 314 A person who finds a lost property shall return it to the right holder. The finder shall promptly notify the right holder to claim it, or deliver it to the public security organ or other relevant authorities.

Article 315 Where the relevant authority receives a lost property, if it knows the right holder, it shall promptly notify him to claim it; if it does not know, it shall promptly publish a notice for claiming.

Article 316 The finder shall take good care of the lost property before delivering it to the relevant authority, and the relevant authority shall take good care of it before it is claimed. If the lost property is damaged or lost due to intentional act or gross negligence, civil liability shall be borne.

Article 317 When claiming a lost property, the right holder shall pay the finder or the relevant authority the necessary expenses incurred for keeping the lost property and the like. If the right holder has offered a reward for finding the lost property, he shall perform his obligation as promised when claiming the lost property. If the finder has misappropriated the lost property, he shall have no right to claim the expenses incurred for keeping the lost property, nor shall he have the right to request the right holder to perform the obligation as promised.
Article 318 A lost property that is not claimed by anyone within one year from the date of publishing the notice for claiming shall vest in the State.

Article 319 For finding drifting objects, discovering buried objects or hidden objects, the relevant provisions on finding lost properties shall apply mutatis mutandis. Where there are other provisions in the law, those provisions shall prevail.
Article 320 Where the principal thing is transferred, the accessory thing shall be transferred together with the principal thing, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 321 Natural fruits shall be acquired by the owner; where there is both an owner and a usufructuary, the usufructuary shall acquire them. Where the parties have agreed otherwise, such agreement shall prevail. Legal fruits, where the parties have agreed on them, shall be acquired in accordance with the agreement; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, they shall be acquired in accordance with trade usage.

Article 322 The ownership of a thing arising from processing, attachment, or mixing shall, where there is an agreement, be determined in accordance with the agreement; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, it shall be determined in accordance with the law; where the law has no provisions, it shall be determined in accordance with the principle of giving full play to the utility of the thing and protecting the party without fault. Where damage is caused to another party due to the fault of one party or the determination of the ownership of the thing, compensation or indemnity shall be made. Part III Usufruct
Article 323 A usufructuary shall have the right to possess, use, and benefit from the immovable or movable property owned by another person in accordance with law.

Article 324 An organization or individual may, in accordance with law, possess, use, and benefit from natural resources owned by the State, owned by the State but used by collectives, and those owned by collectives as provided by law.
Article 325 The State shall implement a system of paid use of natural resources, unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 326 A usufructuary, in exercising its rights, shall comply with the provisions of laws on the protection and rational development and utilization of resources and the protection of the ecological environment. The owner shall not interfere with the usufructuary's exercise of its rights.

Article 327 Where the usufruct is extinguished or its exercise is affected due to the expropriation or requisition of immovable or movable property, the usufructuary shall have the right to obtain corresponding compensation in accordance with Articles 243 and 245 of this Law.
Article 328 The right to use sea areas obtained in accordance with law shall be protected by law.
Article 329 The rights to exploration, mining, water abstraction, and the right to use waters and tidal flats for aquaculture and fishing, obtained in accordance with law, shall be protected by law.

Article 330 Rural collective economic organizations shall implement a two-tier management system combining unified and separate operations based on the household contract management system. The system of land contract management shall be implemented in accordance with law for arable land, forestland, grassland, and other agricultural land owned by the farmer collective or owned by the State but used by the farmer collective.

Article 331 Holders of the right to land contract management shall have the right to possess, use, and benefit from the arable land, forestland, grassland, etc., they contract to operate in accordance with law, and shall have the right to engage in agricultural production such as crop farming, forestry, and animal husbandry.

Article 332 The contract period for arable land shall be 30 years. The contract period for grassland shall be 30 to 50 years. The contract period for forestland shall be 30 to 70 years. Upon the expiration of the contract period specified in the preceding paragraph, the holder of the right to land contract management may continue the contract in accordance with the provisions of the law on rural land contracting.

Article 333 The right to land contract management shall be established upon the entry into effect of the contract for land contract management. The registration authority shall issue certificates such as the certificate of the right to land contract management and the forest ownership certificate to the holder of the right to land contract management, and shall register them in a register to confirm the right to land contract management.

Article 334 A holder of the right to land contract management shall have the right to exchange or transfer the right to land contract management in accordance with law. Without approval in accordance with law, the contracted land shall not be used for non-agricultural construction.

Article 335 Where the right to land contract management is exchanged or transferred, the parties may apply to the registration authority for registration; without registration, such right shall not be asserted against a bona fide third party.

Article 336 During the contract period, the party granting the contract shall not adjust the contracted land. Where, due to special circumstances such as severe damage to the contracted land caused by natural disasters, appropriate adjustment of the contracted arable land and grassland is necessary, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the law on rural land contracting.
Article 337 During the contract period, the party granting the contract shall not withdraw the contracted land. If the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 338 Where the contracted land is expropriated, the holder of the right to land contract management shall have the right to obtain corresponding compensation in accordance with Article 243 of this Law.

Article 339 A holder of the right to land contract management may, on its own initiative, decide to transfer the land management right to others by means of lease, shareholding, or other methods in accordance with law.

Article 340 A holder of the land management right shall have the right to possess the rural land within the period agreed in the contract, to independently carry out agricultural production and operation, and to obtain benefits.

Article 341 The land management right with a transfer period of five years or more shall be established at the time when the transfer contract becomes effective. The parties may apply to the registration authority for the registration of the land management right; without registration, it shall not be invoked against a bona fide third party.

Article 342 Where rural land is contracted through bidding, auction, public negotiation or other means, and the ownership certificate is obtained upon registration according to law, the land management right may be transferred by leasing, equity contribution, mortgage or other means according to law.
Article 343 Where state-owned agricultural land is subject to contractual operation, the relevant provisions of this Part shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 344 The holder of the right to use construction land shall be entitled, according to law, to possess, use and benefit from the state-owned land, and shall have the right to use such land to construct buildings, structures and their auxiliary facilities.
Article 345 The right to use construction land may be established separately on the surface, above the ground or underground of the land.

Article 346 The establishment of the right to use construction land shall comply with the requirements of conserving resources and protecting the ecological environment, abide by the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on the purposes of land use, and shall not harm the existing usufruct.

Article 347 The right to use construction land may be established by means of grant or allocation. For commercial land such as industrial, commercial, tourism, entertainment and commercial residential land, and where there are two or more intended users for the same land, the grant shall be made by means of public bidding, auction or other public competitive pricing methods. The establishment of the right to use construction land by means of allocation shall be strictly restricted.

Article 348 Where the right to use construction land is established by means of grant through bidding, auction, agreement or other means, the parties shall conclude a contract for the grant of the right to use construction land in writing. A contract for the grant of the right to use construction land shall generally include the following terms: (1) the names and domiciles of the parties; (2) the boundaries, area, etc. of the land; (3) the space occupied by the buildings, structures and their auxiliary facilities; (4) the land use purposes and planning conditions; (5) the term of the right to use construction land; (6) the fees such as the grant price and the method of payment thereof; and (7) the method for dispute resolution.

Article 349 For the establishment of the right to use construction land, an application for the registration of the right to use construction land shall be made to the registration authority. The right to use construction land shall be established upon registration. The registration authority shall issue a title certificate to the holder of the right to use construction land.

Article 350 The holder of the right to use construction land shall make rational use of the land and shall not change the land use purpose; where it is necessary to change the land use purpose, approval shall be obtained from the relevant administrative department according to law.
Article 351 The holder of the right to use construction land shall pay fees such as the grant price in accordance with the provisions of laws and the contractual agreement.

Article 352 The ownership of the buildings, structures and their auxiliary facilities constructed by the holder of the right to use construction land shall belong to the holder of the right to use construction land, unless there is evidence to the contrary.

Article 353 The holder of the right to use construction land shall have the right to transfer, exchange, make capital contribution with, donate or mortgage the right to use construction land, unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 354 Where the right to use construction land is transferred, exchanged, made as capital contribution, donated or mortgaged, the parties shall conclude a corresponding contract in writing. The term of use shall be agreed upon by the parties, but shall not exceed the remaining term of the right to use construction land.

Article 355 Where the right to use construction land is transferred, exchanged, made as capital contribution or donated, an application for modification registration shall be made to the registration authority.

Article 356 Where the right to use construction land is transferred, exchanged, made as capital contribution or donated, the buildings, structures and their auxiliary facilities attached to the land shall be disposed of together therewith.

Article 357 Where the buildings, structures and their auxiliary facilities are transferred, exchanged, made as capital contribution or donated, the right to use construction land within the area occupied by such buildings, structures and their auxiliary facilities shall be disposed of together therewith.

Article 358 Where, before the expiration of the term of the right to use construction land, the land is required to be taken back in advance for the needs of the public interest, compensation shall be given for the houses and other immovable property on the land in accordance with the provisions of Article 243 of this Law, and the corresponding grant price shall be refunded.

Article 359 Where the term of the right to use residential construction land expires, it shall be automatically renewed. The payment or reduction of and exemption from the renewal fees shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations. The renewal of the right to use non-residential construction land after the expiration of its term shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of laws. The ownership of the houses and other immovable property on the land shall, if there is an agreement, be subject to the agreement; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.
Article 360 Where the right to use construction land is extinguished, the grantor shall promptly handle the deregistration. The registration authority shall withdraw the title certificate.
Article 361: Where collectively owned land is used as construction land, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of laws on land administration.

Article 362: The holder of the right to use a residential site shall, in accordance with law, have the right to possess and use the collectively owned land, and shall have the right to use such land in accordance with law for the construction of a residence and its auxiliary installations.
Article 363: The acquisition, exercise, and transfer of the right to use a residential site shall be governed by the laws on land administration and the relevant state regulations.

Article 364: If a residential site is extinguished due to a natural disaster or other reason, the right to use that residential site shall be extinguished. For villagers who have lost their residential site, a new residential site shall be reallocated to them in accordance with law.
Article 365: Where the registered right to use a residential site is transferred or extinguished, the modification registration or cancellation registration shall be promptly processed.

Article 366: The holder of a right of habitation shall, in accordance with the terms of the contract, have the right to possess and use the residence of another as a usufruct, in order to meet the needs of living and residence.

Article 367: To establish a right of habitation, the parties shall conclude a contract for the right of habitation in writing. A contract for the right of habitation generally includes the following terms: (1) the name or title and domicile of the parties; (2) the location of the residence; (3) the conditions and requirements for habitation; (4) the term of the right of habitation; and (5) the method for dispute resolution.

Article 368: A right of habitation shall be established gratuitously, unless the parties agree otherwise. Where a right of habitation is established, an application for the registration of the right of habitation shall be made to the registration authority. The right of habitation shall be established upon registration.
Article 369: A right of habitation shall not be transferred or inherited. A residence on which a right of habitation is established shall not be leased, unless the parties agree otherwise.

Article 370: The right of habitation shall be extinguished upon the expiration of its term or upon the death of the holder of the right of habitation. Where the right of habitation is extinguished, the cancellation registration shall be promptly processed.
Article 371: Where a right of habitation is established by will, the relevant provisions of this Chapter shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 372: The holder of an easement shall, in accordance with the terms of the contract, have the right to use the immovable property of another to improve the efficiency of his or her own immovable property. The immovable property of another referred to in the preceding paragraph is the servient tenement, and the party's own immovable property is the dominant tenement.

Article 373: To establish an easement, the parties shall conclude a contract for the easement in writing. A contract for an easement generally includes the following terms: (1) the name or title and domicile of the parties; (2) the location of the servient and dominant tenements; (3) the purpose and method of use; (4) the term of the easement; (5) the fees and the method of payment; and (6) the method for dispute resolution.

Article 374: An easement shall be established when the contract for the easement takes effect. If the parties request registration, they may apply to the registration authority for the registration of the easement; without registration, it shall not be set up against a bona fide third party.

Article 375: The holder of the servient tenement shall, in accordance with the terms of the contract, allow the holder of the easement to use his or her immovable property, and shall not interfere with the exercise of the right by the holder of the easement.

Article 376: The holder of the easement shall use the servient tenement in accordance with the purpose and method of use agreed upon in the contract, and shall minimize the restriction on the real right of the holder of the servient tenement.

Article 377: The term of an easement shall be agreed upon by the parties; however, it shall not exceed the remaining term of the usufruct such as the right to the contractual operation of land, the right to the use of land for construction, and similar rights.

Article 378: If the owner of the land enjoys an easement or bears an easement, when establishing a usufruct such as the right to the contractual operation of land or the right to use a residential site, the holder of such usufruct shall continue to enjoy or bear the easement already established.

Article 379: Where a usufruct such as the right to the contractual operation of land, the right to the use of land for construction, or the right to use a residential site has already been established on the land, the owner of the land shall not establish an easement without the consent of the holder of the usufruct.

Article 380: An easement shall not be transferred separately. Where the right to the contractual operation of land, the right to the use of land for construction, or any similar right is transferred, the easement shall be transferred together therewith, unless otherwise agreed in the contract.

Article 381 An easement shall not be mortgaged separately. Where the right to land management, the right to use construction land, or the like is mortgaged, the easement shall be transferred together when the mortgage is enforced.

Article 382 Where the dominant tenement and the right to land contractual management, the right to use construction land, or the like on the dominant tenement are partially transferred, if the transferred part involves the easement, the transferee shall simultaneously enjoy the easement.

Article 383 Where the servient tenement and the right to land contractual management, the right to use construction land, or the like on the servient tenement are partially transferred, if the transferred part involves the easement, the easement shall be legally binding on the transferee.

Article 384 Where the easement holder falls under any of the following circumstances, the servient tenement right holder may rescind the easement contract, and the easement shall be extinguished: (1) abusing the easement in violation of the provisions of the law or the contractual stipulations; or (2) in the case of exploiting the servient tenement with payment, failing to pay the fees within a reasonable period after the expiry of the agreed payment deadline upon two demands.

Article 385 Where a registered easement is modified, transferred, or extinguished, modification registration or cancellation registration shall be handled in a timely manner. Part IV Security Interests

Article 386 Where the debtor fails to perform an obligation due, or any circumstance agreed upon by the parties for enforcing a security interest occurs, the security interest holder shall have the right to seek priority in satisfying its claim from the security property in accordance with the law, unless otherwise provided by the law.

Article 387 Where a creditor, in order to secure the satisfaction of its claim in civil activities such as lending or sale, needs a guarantee, it may create a security interest in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other laws. Where a third party provides security to a creditor for a debtor, the third party may require the debtor to provide counter-security. The provisions of this Law and other laws shall apply to counter-security.

Article 388 To create a security interest, a security contract shall be concluded in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other laws. Security contracts include mortgage contracts, pledge contracts, and other contracts with security functions. A security contract is an ancillary contract to the principal claim and debt contract. If the principal claim and debt contract is void, the security contract shall be void, unless otherwise provided by the law. After a security contract is confirmed void, if the debtor, the guarantor, or the creditor is at fault, it shall bear the corresponding civil liability according to its fault.

Article 389 The scope of security covered by a security interest shall include the principal claim and its interest, liquidated damages, compensation for damages, the expenses for keeping the security property, and the expenses for enforcing the security interest. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 390 During the security period, if the security property is damaged, destroyed, or requisitioned, the security interest holder may seek priority in satisfying its claim from the insurance proceeds, compensation, or damages, etc. obtained. If the performance period for the secured claim has not expired, the said insurance proceeds, compensation, or damages, etc. may also be deposited.

Article 391 Where a third party provides security, if the creditor allows the debtor to transfer all or part of the debt without the third party's written consent, the guarantor shall no longer bear the corresponding security liability.

Article 392 Where a secured claim has both a security interest and a guarantee, if the debtor fails to perform an obligation due, or any circumstance agreed upon by the parties for enforcing a security interest occurs, the creditor shall enforce the claim in accordance with the agreement. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and the debtor itself provides the security interest, the creditor shall first enforce the claim against the security interest. If a third party provides the security interest, the creditor may enforce the claim against the security interest or request the guarantor to bear the guarantee liability. After a third party who provides the security bears the security liability, it shall have the right of recourse against the debtor.

Article 393 A security interest shall be extinguished in any of the following circumstances: (1) the principal claim is extinguished; (2) the security interest is enforced; (3) the creditor abandons the security interest; or (4) any other circumstance provided by the law for the extinction of a security interest.

Article 394 To secure the performance of a debt, where the debtor or a third party does not transfer the possession of a property but mortgages the property to the creditor, if the debtor fails to perform an obligation due, or any circumstance agreed upon by the parties for enforcing the mortgage occurs, the creditor shall have the right to seek priority in satisfying its claim from such property. The debtor or the third party as specified in the preceding paragraph is the mortgagor, the creditor is the mortgagee, and the property provided as security is the mortgaged property.

Article 395 The following property over which the debtor or a third party is entitled to dispose may be mortgaged: (1) buildings and other structures affixed to the land; (2) the right to use construction land; (3) the right to use sea areas; (4) production equipment, raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products; (5) buildings, vessels, and aircraft under construction; (6) means of transport; and (7) other property that is not prohibited from being mortgaged by any law or administrative regulation. The mortgagor may mortgage all of the property listed in the preceding paragraph together.

Article 396 An enterprise, individual industrial or commercial household, or agricultural production operator may mortgage its existing and future-to-be-acquired production equipment, raw materials, semi-finished products, and finished products. If the debtor fails to perform an obligation due, or any circumstance agreed upon by the parties for enforcing the mortgage occurs, the creditor shall have the right to seek priority in satisfying its claim from the movable property as identified at the time the mortgage is enforced.

Article 397 Where a building is mortgaged, the right to use construction land within the area occupied by such building shall be mortgaged together. Where the right to use construction land is mortgaged, the building on the land shall be mortgaged together. If the mortgagor does not mortgage the property together in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the unmortgaged property shall be deemed to be mortgaged together.

Article 398 The right to use construction land of a township or village enterprise shall not be mortgaged separately. Where a building such as a factory building of a township or village enterprise is mortgaged, the right to use construction land within the area occupied by such building shall be mortgaged together.

Article 399 The following property shall not be mortgaged: (1) land ownership; (2) the right to use collectively owned land, such as residential land, private plots of cropland, and private plots of hilly land, except as otherwise provided by the law; (3) educational facilities, medical and health facilities, and other public welfare facilities of non-profit legal persons established for public welfare purposes, such as schools, kindergartens, and medical institutions; (4) property whose ownership or right to use is unclear or disputed; (5) property that is sealed up, detained, or placed under supervision in accordance with the law; or (6) other property that is prohibited from being mortgaged by any law or administrative regulation.

Article 400 To create a mortgage, the parties shall enter into a mortgage contract in writing. A mortgage contract generally includes the following clauses: (1) the type and amount of the secured claim; (2) the time limit for the debtor to perform the debt; (3) the name, quantity, and other information of the mortgaged property; and (4) the scope of the security.

Article 401 If a mortgagee and a mortgagor agree before the expiration of the performance period of the debt that the mortgaged property shall vest in the creditor if the debtor fails to perform the due debt, the mortgagee may only enjoy priority of compensation from the mortgaged property in accordance with law.

Article 402 Where a mortgage is created on the property specified in Items (1) to (3) of the first paragraph of Article 395 of this Code or on a building under construction specified in Item (5), a mortgage registration shall be effected. The mortgage right shall be established upon registration.

Article 403 Where a mortgage is created on chattels, the mortgage right shall be established upon the entry into effect of the mortgage contract; without registration, it may not be set up against a bona fide third party.
Article 404 Where a mortgage is created on chattels, it may not be set up against a buyer who has paid a reasonable price and obtained the mortgaged property in the ordinary course of business.

Article 405 If the mortgaged property has been leased and possession thereof has been transferred before the establishment of the mortgage right, the original lease relationship shall not be affected by such mortgage right.

Article 406 During the mortgage period, the mortgagor may transfer the mortgaged property. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail. The mortgage right shall not be affected by the transfer of the mortgaged property. Where the mortgagor transfers the mortgaged property, the mortgagor shall promptly notify the mortgagee. If the mortgagee can prove that the transfer of the mortgaged property may prejudice the mortgage right, the mortgagee may request the mortgagor to apply the proceeds from the transfer to the advance repayment of the debt or to have them deposited with the mortgagee. The portion of the transfer proceeds exceeding the amount of the claim shall belong to the mortgagor, and the shortfall shall be paid by the debtor.

Article 407 A mortgage right shall not be transferred separately from the claim it secures, nor shall it be used as a security for another claim. Where the claim is assigned, the mortgage right securing such claim shall be assigned together therewith, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 408 If the mortgagor's conduct is sufficient to cause a decrease in the value of the mortgaged property, the mortgagee shall have the right to request the mortgagor to cease such conduct; if the value of the mortgaged property has decreased, the mortgagee shall have the right to request the restoration of the value of the mortgaged property or the provision of security corresponding to the decreased value. If the mortgagor neither restores the value of the mortgaged property nor provides such security, the mortgagee shall have the right to request the debtor to repay the debt before maturity.

Article 409 A mortgagee may waive the mortgage right or the ranking of the mortgage right. The mortgagee and the mortgagor may, by agreement, modify the ranking of the mortgage right and the amount of the claim secured thereby, provided that any modification that has not obtained the written consent of other mortgagees shall not adversely affect such other mortgagees. Where a debtor creates a mortgage on its own property, and the mortgagee waives such mortgage right, the ranking thereof, or modifies the mortgage right, the guarantors other than the debtor shall be released from their guarantee liability to the extent of the priority right to compensation that the mortgagee has lost, unless such other guarantors undertake to continue to provide the guarantee.

Article 410 If the debtor fails to perform its due debt or a circumstance agreed upon by the parties for the enforcement of the mortgage right occurs, the mortgagee may reach an agreement with the mortgagor to obtain priority payment out of the proceeds from the conversion of the mortgaged property into money or from the auction or sale of such property. If such agreement prejudices the interests of other creditors, those other creditors may request the People's Court to revoke the agreement. If the mortgagee and the mortgagor fail to reach an agreement on the method for enforcing the mortgage right, the mortgagee may request the People's Court to auction or sell the mortgaged property. Where the mortgaged property is converted into money or sold, the market price shall be taken as a reference.

Article 411 Where a mortgage is created in accordance with Article 396 of this Code, the mortgaged property shall be determined upon the occurrence of any of the following circumstances: (1) the performance period for the debt has expired and the claim has not been satisfied; (2) the mortgagor has been declared bankrupt or dissolved; (3) a circumstance agreed upon by the parties for the enforcement of the mortgage right occurs; or (4) other circumstances that materially impair the satisfaction of the claim.

Article 412 Where the debtor fails to perform its due debt or a circumstance agreed upon by the parties for the enforcement of the mortgage right occurs, resulting in the mortgaged property being seized by the People's Court in accordance with law, the mortgagee shall, from the date of seizure, have the right to collect the natural fruits or legal fruits from the mortgaged property, unless the mortgagee has failed to notify the obligor who is obligated to satisfy the legal fruits. The fruits referred to in the preceding paragraph shall first be applied to cover the expenses incurred in collecting them.

Article 413 After the mortgaged property is converted into money, auctioned, or sold, the portion of the proceeds exceeding the amount of the claim shall belong to the mortgagor, and the shortfall shall be paid by the debtor.

Article 414 Where the same property is mortgaged to two or more creditors, the proceeds from the auction or sale of the mortgaged property shall be used for repayment in accordance with the following rules: (1) where the mortgage rights have been registered, the order of payment shall be determined according to the chronological order of registration; (2) a registered mortgage right shall be paid before an unregistered one; and (3) where the mortgage rights are not registered, payment shall be made in proportion to the amounts of the claims. The order of payment for other registrable security interests shall be determined by reference to the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 415 Where both a mortgage right and a pledge right are created on the same property, the order of payment from the proceeds of the auction or sale of such property shall be determined according to the chronological order of registration and delivery.

Article 416 Where the principal claim secured by a chattel mortgage is the purchase price of the collateral, and the mortgage registration is effected within ten days after the delivery of the subject matter, the mortgagee shall be paid in priority over other secured creditors of the buyer of the collateral, except for a lien holder.

Article 417 After the mortgage of the right to use construction land is created, the buildings newly constructed on such land shall not form part of the mortgaged property. When the mortgage right is enforced on the right to use construction land, the newly constructed buildings on such land shall be disposed of together with the right to use construction land; however, the mortgagee shall have no right to obtain priority compensation from the proceeds of the newly constructed buildings.

Article 418 Where the right to use collectively-owned land is mortgaged in accordance with law, after the enforcement of the mortgage right, the nature of the land ownership and the purpose of the land shall not be altered without going through the statutory procedures.
Article 419 A mortgagee shall exercise its mortgage right within the limitation period for the principal claim; if it fails to do so, the People's Court shall not provide protection.

Article 420 Where, to secure the performance of a debt, a debtor or a third party provides security property for claims to arise continuously within a certain period, and if the debtor fails to perform its due debt or a circumstance agreed upon by the parties for the enforcement of the mortgage right occurs, the mortgagee shall have the right to obtain priority payment from the security property within the maximum amount of the claims. Claims that already exist before the creation of the maximum mortgage right may, with the consent of the parties, be included within the scope of claims secured by the maximum mortgage right.

Article 421 Prior to the determination of the claims secured by a maximum mortgage for floating claims, if part of the claims is assigned, the said maximum mortgage right shall not be assigned, unless the parties agree otherwise.

Article 422 Prior to the determination of the claims secured by a maximum mortgage for floating claims, the mortgagee and the mortgagor may, by agreement, change the period for the determination of the claims, the scope of the claims, and the maximum amount of the claims. However, such a change shall not adversely affect any other mortgagee.

Article 423 The claims of the mortgagee shall be determined under any of the following circumstances: (1) the agreed period for determination of the claims expires; (2) if there is no agreement on a period for determination of the claims or the agreement is ambiguous, the mortgagee or mortgagor requests determination of the claims within two years from the date of creation of the maximum mortgage for floating claims; (3) the occurrence of new claims becomes impossible; (4) the mortgagee knows or should have known that the mortgaged property has been sealed up or distrained; (5) the debtor or mortgagor is declared bankrupt or dissolved; or (6) other circumstances provided by law for the determination of claims arise.
Article 424 In addition to the provisions of this Section, the relevant provisions of Section 1 of this Chapter shall apply to a maximum mortgage for floating claims.

Article 425 To secure the performance of an obligation, if a debtor or a third party pledges his or its chattel to the creditor for possession, and the debtor fails to perform the obligation as it falls due or if any circumstance upon which the pledge is to be realized as agreed by the parties occurs, the creditor shall be entitled to be paid in priority out of the proceeds of such chattel. The debtor or the third party mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall be the pledgor, the creditor shall be the pledgee, and the delivered chattel shall be the pledged property.
Article 426 Chattels whose transfer is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations shall not be pledged.

Article 427 To create a pledge, the parties shall enter into a pledge contract in writing. A pledge contract generally contains the following terms: (1) the type and amount of the claim secured; (2) the time limit for the debtor to perform the obligation; (3) the name, quantity and other information of the pledged property; (4) the scope of the security; and (5) the time and manner of delivery of the pledged property.

Article 428 If the pledgee and the pledgor agree, prior to the expiration of the time limit for the performance of the obligation, that the pledged property shall vest in the creditor if the debtor fails to perform the obligation as it falls due, the pledgee may only be entitled to be paid in priority out of the said pledged property in accordance with law.
Article 429 A pledge shall be created upon delivery of the pledged property by the pledgor.

Article 430 The pledgee shall have the right to collect the fruits of the pledged property, unless the contract provides otherwise. The fruits prescribed in the preceding paragraph shall first be used to offset the expenses incurred in collecting them.

Article 431 If the pledgee, during the existence of the pledge, without the consent of the pledgor, uses or disposes of the pledged property, causing damage to the pledgor, the pledgee shall be liable for compensation.

Article 432 The pledgee shall be obligated to keep the pledged property in safe custody; if the pledged property is damaged or lost due to improper custody, the pledgee shall be liable for compensation. If the behavior of the pledgee may cause damage or loss to the pledged property, the pledgor may request the pledgee to deposit the pledged property, or request the advance payment of the obligation and the return of the pledged property.

Article 433 If the pledged property may be damaged or its value may obviously decrease due to a cause not attributable to the pledgee to such an extent as to endanger the rights of the pledgee, the pledgee shall have the right to request the pledgor to provide additional security; if the pledgor fails to do so, the pledgee may auction or sell off the pledged property, and agree with the pledgor to use the proceeds from the auction or sale for advance payment of the obligation or deposit them for safekeeping.

Article 434 If the pledgee, during the existence of the pledge, re-pledges the pledged property without the consent of the pledgor, causing damage or loss to the pledged property, the pledgee shall be liable for compensation.

Article 435 The pledgee may waive the pledge. If the debtor pledges his own property and the pledgee waives the pledge, the other sureties shall be exempted from the suretyship liability to the extent of the priority right to be paid that the pledgee loses, unless the other sureties promise to continue to provide the suretyship.

Article 436 If the debtor performs his obligation or the pledgor pays in advance the secured claim, the pledgee shall return the pledged property. If the debtor fails to perform the obligation as it falls due or if any circumstance upon which the pledge is to be realized as agreed by the parties occurs, the pledgee may agree with the pledgor on the conversion of the pledged property into money, or be paid in priority out of the proceeds from the auction or sale of the pledged property. Where the pledged property is converted into money or sold, the market price shall be taken as a reference.

Article 437 The pledgor may request the pledgee, after the expiration of the time limit for the performance of the obligation, to exercise the pledge in a timely manner; if the pledgee fails to do so, the pledgor may request a people's court to auction or sell off the pledged property. If the pledgor requests the pledgee to exercise the pledge in a timely manner, and the pledgee causes damage to the pledgor due to his failure to do so, the pledgee shall be liable for compensation.

Article 438 After the pledged property has been converted into money, auctioned or sold, if the proceeds thereof exceed the amount of the claim, the balance shall be returned to the pledgor; if the proceeds thereof are insufficient, the debtor shall pay the balance.

Article 439 The pledgor and the pledgee may agree to create a maximum pledge for floating claims. In addition to the relevant provisions of this Section, the relevant provisions of Section 2, Chapter 17 of this Part shall apply mutatis mutandis to a maximum pledge for floating claims.

Article 440 The following rights that a debtor or a third party is entitled to dispose of may be pledged: (1) bills of exchange, promissory notes and cheques; (2) bonds and certificates of deposit; (3) warehouse receipts and bills of lading; (4) transferrable fund shares and equity interests; (5) property rights in intellectual property rights, such as the right to exclusive use of registered trademarks, patent rights, and copyrights, which are transferrable; (6) accounts receivable, existing and future; and (7) other property rights that may be pledged as provided by laws and administrative regulations.

Article 441 Where a bill of exchange, promissory note, cheque, bond, certificate of deposit, warehouse receipt or bill of lading is pledged, the pledge right shall be established upon delivery of the title certificate to the pledgee; if there is no title certificate, the pledge right shall be established upon registration of the pledge. Where the law provides otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 442 Where the date of payment or delivery of a bill of exchange, promissory note, cheque, bond, certificate of deposit, warehouse receipt or bill of lincoln falls prior to the maturity of the principal claim, the pledgee may cash or take delivery of the goods, and shall, through agreement with the pledgor, use the proceeds or the goods obtained to repay the debt in advance or deposit them with a competent authority.

Article 443 Where fund units or shares are pledged, the pledge right shall be established upon registration of the pledge. After fund units or shares are pledged, they may not be transferred, except where the pledgor and the pledgee so agree through consultation. The proceeds obtained by the pledgor from the transfer of fund units or shares shall be used to repay the debt to the pledgee in advance or be deposited with a competent authority.

Article 444 Where property rights in intellectual property such as the right to exclusive use of a registered trademark, patent right or copyright are pledged, the pledge right shall be established upon registration of the pledge. After property rights in intellectual property are pledged, the pledgor may not transfer or license the use thereof to others, except where the pledgor and the pledgee so agree through consultation. The proceeds obtained by the pledgor from the transfer or licensing of the pledged property rights in intellectual property shall be used to repay the debt to the pledgee in advance or be deposited with a competent authority.

Article 445 Where an account receivable is pledged, the pledge right shall be established upon registration of the pledge. After an account receivable is pledged, it may not be transferred, except where the pledgor and the pledgee so agree through consultation. The proceeds obtained by the pledgor from the transfer of the account receivable shall be used to repay the debt to the pledgee in advance or be deposited with a competent authority.
Article 446 In addition to the provisions of this Section, the relevant provisions of Section 1 of this Chapter shall apply to the pledge of rights.

Article 447 Where the debtor fails to perform its obligations that have fallen due, the creditor may retain the debtor's movables which are already in the creditor's lawful possession, and shall be entitled to seek satisfaction in priority out of such movables. The creditor specified in the preceding paragraph shall be the lienholder, and the movables in possession shall be the retained property.
Article 448 The movables retained by the creditor shall be under the same legal relationship with the claim, except for retention between enterprises.
Article 449 Movables which shall not be retained under the provisions of the law or the agreement of the parties may not be retained.
Article 450 Where the retained property is divisible, the value of the retained property shall correspond to the amount of the debt.

Article 451 The lienholder shall have the duty to properly keep the retained property, and shall bear the liability for compensation if the retained property is damaged, destroyed or lost due to improper keeping.

Article 452 The lienholder shall be entitled to collect the fruits of the retained property. The fruits specified in the preceding paragraph shall first be applied to cover the expenses for their collection.

Article 453 The lienholder and the debtor shall agree on the period for performing the debt after the property has been retained; if there is no such agreement or the agreement is unclear, the lienholder shall give the debtor a period of not less than sixty days to perform the debt, except where it involves fresh, perishable or other movables that are difficult to keep. If the debtor still fails to perform at the expiry of such period, the lienholder may reach an agreement with the debtor on the conversion of the retained property into a sum of money as payment, or may seek satisfaction in priority out of the proceeds from the auction or sale of the retained property. Where the retained property is converted into a sum of money or sold, the market price shall be taken as a reference.

Article 454 The debtor may request the lienholder to exercise the lien after the debt performance period has expired; if the lienholder fails to do so, the debtor may request the People's Court to auction or sell the retained property.

Article 455 After the retained property is converted into a sum of money or auctioned or sold, the portion of the proceeds exceeding the amount of the claim shall belong to the debtor, and any insufficiency shall be satisfied by the debtor.
Article 456 Where a mortgage or pledge has been established on the same movable, and the movable is retained afterwards, the lienholder shall have priority in satisfaction.
Article 457 Where the lienholder loses possession of the retained property or the lienholder accepts other security provided separately by the debtor, the lien shall extinguish. Part Five: Possession

Article 458 For possession arising from a contractual relationship or other relationships, matters such as the use, earnings, and liability for breach of contract concerning immovable or movable property shall be governed by the contract; if there is no such provision in the contract or the provision is unclear, the relevant laws shall apply.
Article 459 Where the possessor, by using the immovable or movable property in its possession, causes damage to such property, a malicious possessor shall bear the liability for compensation.

Article 460 Where immovable or movable property is possessed by a possessor, the right holder may request the return of the original property and its fruits; provided, however, that the right holder shall pay the necessary expenses incurred by the good-faith possessor in maintaining such immovable or movable property.

Article 461 Where an immovable or movable property in possession is damaged or lost, and the right holder of such immovable or movable property claims compensation, the possessor shall return to the right holder any insurance proceeds, compensation or indemnity obtained due to the damage or loss. Where the damage to the right holder is not sufficiently compensated, the possessor in bad faith shall also compensate for the loss.

Article 462 Where an immovable or movable property in possession is encroached upon, the possessor shall have the right to request return of the original property. Where possession is obstructed, the possessor shall have the right to request removal of the obstruction or elimination of the danger.
