Where damage is caused by the encroachment or obstruction, the possessor shall have the right to request compensation for the damage according to law. Where the possessor's right to request return of the original property is not exercised within one year from the date of the encroachment, such right shall be extinguished.
Article 463 This Part regulates civil relations arising from contracts.

Article 464 A contract is an agreement between civil subjects to establish, modify or terminate a civil legal relationship. Agreements concerning personal status relations, such as marriage, adoption and guardianship, shall be governed by the legal provisions concerning such personal status relations. In the absence of such provisions, the provisions of this Part may be applied by reference based on the nature of such agreements.
Article 465 A contract lawfully formed shall be protected by law. A contract lawfully formed shall be legally binding only on the parties thereto, unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 466 Where the parties dispute the understanding of a contract clause, the meaning of the disputed clause shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 142, paragraph 1 of this Law. Where a contract is concluded in two or more languages and it is agreed that all versions are equally authentic, the words and sentences used in each version shall be presumed to have the same meaning. Where the words and sentences used in each version are inconsistent, the contract shall be interpreted in light of the relevant clauses, the nature and purpose of the contract, and the principle of good faith.

Article 467 Contracts not expressly provided for in this Law or other laws shall be governed by the general provisions of this Part, and may be governed by reference to the provisions on the most similar type of contract under this Part or other laws. Contracts for Sino-foreign equity joint venture enterprises, contracts for Sino-foreign contractual joint venture enterprises, and contracts for Sino-foreign cooperative exploration and development of natural resources performed within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China.

Article 468 Obligatory rights and obligations relations not arising from a contract shall be governed by the legal provisions concerning such obligatory rights and obligations relations. In the absence of such provisions, the relevant provisions of the general provisions of this Part shall apply, unless they cannot be applied due to the nature of such relations.

Article 469 The parties may conclude a contract in written, oral or other forms. A written form refers to a form which can tangibly express the content contained therein, such as a contract instrument, letter, telegram, telex or facsimile. A data message in the form of electronic data interchange or email, among others, which can tangibly express the content contained therein and can be accessed for reference at any time, shall be deemed a written form.

Article 470 The content of a contract shall be agreed upon by the parties and generally includes the following clauses: (1) the names or titles and domiciles of the parties; (2) the subject matter; (3) the quantity; (4) the quality; (5) the price or remuneration; (6) the time limit, place and method of performance; (7) liability for breach of contract; and (8) the method for dispute resolution. The parties may conclude a contract by reference to model texts of various types of contracts.
Article 471 The parties may conclude a contract by means of an offer and acceptance or by other means.

Article 472 An offer is a manifestation of intent to conclude a contract with another person, and such manifestation of intent shall meet the following conditions: (1) the content is specific and definite; and (2) it indicates that the offeror shall be bound by the manifestation of intent upon acceptance by the offeree.

Article 473 An invitation to offer is a manifestation by which a person invites another person to make an offer to him or her. Auction announcements, tender announcements, prospectuses, bond offering memoranda, fund prospectuses, commercial advertisements and promotions, and mailed price lists, among others, shall constitute invitations to offer. Where the content of a commercial advertisement or promotion meets the conditions for an offer, it shall constitute an offer.
Article 474 The time when an offer takes effect shall be subject to the provisions of Article 137 of this Law.
Article 475 An offer may be withdrawn. The withdrawal of an offer shall be subject to the provisions of Article 141 of this Law.

Article 476 An offer may be revoked, except under any of the following circumstances: (1) the offeror expressly states, by fixing a time limit for acceptance or otherwise, that the offer is irrevocable; or (2) the offeree has reason to believe that the offer is irrevocable and has made reasonable preparations for performing the contract.

Article 477 Where the manifestation of intent to revoke an offer is made orally, the content of such manifestation of intent shall be known to the offeree before the offeree makes an acceptance. Where the manifestation of intent to revoke an offer is made by non-oral means, it shall reach the offeree before the offeree makes an acceptance.

Article 478 An offer shall cease to be effective under any of the following circumstances: (1) the offer is rejected; (2) the offer is revoked according to law; (3) the time limit for acceptance expires and the offeree has not made an acceptance; or (4) the offeree makes a material modification to the content of the offer.
Article 479 An acceptance is a manifestation of intent by the offeree to assent to the offer.
Article 480 An acceptance shall be made by means of a notice, unless, according to trade practices or the offer, the acceptance may be made by performing an act.

Article 481 An acceptance shall reach the offeror within the time limit specified in the offer. If the offer does not specify a time limit for acceptance, the acceptance shall reach the offeror in accordance with the following provisions: (1) If the offer is made in the form of a dialogue, the acceptance shall be made immediately; (2) If the offer is made in a non-dialogue form, the acceptance shall reach the offeror within a reasonable time.

Article 482 If an offer is made by letter or telegram, the time limit for acceptance shall begin to run from the date shown in the letter or the date of dispatch of the telegram. If the letter does not show a date, the time limit shall run from the postmark date of the letter. If the offer is made by means of instantaneous communication such as telephone, facsimile, or electronic mail, the time limit for acceptance shall begin to run from the moment the offer reaches the offeree.
Article 483 A contract is formed when the acceptance becomes effective, except as otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 484 The time when an acceptance made by means of a notice becomes effective shall be governed by the provisions of Article 137 of this Law. If an acceptance does not require a notice, it becomes effective when the act of acceptance is performed in accordance with trade usage or the requirements of the offer.
Article 485 An acceptance may be withdrawn. The withdrawal of an acceptance shall be governed by the provisions of Article 141 of this Law.

Article 486 If an offeree dispatches an acceptance after the time limit for acceptance has expired, or dispatches an acceptance within the time limit but under normal circumstances it would not reach the offeror in due time, such acceptance constitutes a new offer; unless the offeror promptly informs the offeree that the acceptance is effective.

Article 487 If an offeree dispatches an acceptance within the time limit for acceptance, and under normal circumstances it would reach the offeror in due time, but the acceptance reaches the offeror after the time limit has expired due to other reasons, the acceptance shall be effective unless the offeror promptly informs the offeree that the acceptance is not accepted because it has exceeded the time limit.

Article 488 The content of an acceptance shall be consistent with the content of the offer. If the offeree materially alters the content of the offer, such acceptance constitutes a new offer. A material alteration to the content of the offer includes, among others, a change in the subject matter, quantity, quality, price or remuneration, time limit for performance, place and method of performance, liability for breach of contract, and method of dispute resolution.

Article 489 If an acceptance makes immaterial alterations to the content of the offer, the acceptance shall be effective and the content of the contract shall be the content of the acceptance, unless the offeror promptly objects to such alterations or the offer indicates that the acceptance shall not make any alteration to the content of the offer.

Article 490 If the parties conclude a contract in the form of a written agreement, the contract is formed when all parties have signed, affixed their seals, or affixed their fingerprints. Before signing, affixing seals, or affixing fingerprints, if one party has already performed the principal obligation and the other party accepts it, the contract is formed. If laws or administrative regulations provide, or the parties agree, that a contract shall be concluded in written form, and the parties do not adopt the written form, but one party has already performed the principal obligation and the other party accepts it, the contract is formed.

Article 491 If the parties conclude a contract in the form of letters, data messages, etc., and require a confirmation letter to be signed, the contract is formed when the confirmation letter is signed. If the information on goods or services published by one party through the Internet or other information networks satisfies the conditions for an offer, and the other party selects such goods or services and successfully submits the order, the contract is formed, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 492 The place where the acceptance becomes effective is the place where the contract is formed. If the contract is concluded in the form of data messages, the principal place of business of the recipient is the place where the contract is formed; if there is no principal place of business, the domicile of the recipient is the place where the contract is formed. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 493 If the parties conclude a contract in the form of a written agreement, the place where the last party signs, affixes its seal, or affixes its fingerprint is the place where the contract is formed, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 494 If the State issues national procurement orders or mandatory tasks for emergency rescue and disaster relief, epidemic prevention and control, or other needs, the relevant civil subjects shall conclude contracts in accordance with the rights and obligations stipulated by relevant laws and administrative regulations. A party that is obliged to make an offer in accordance with the provisions of laws or administrative regulations shall promptly dispatch a reasonable offer. A party that is obliged to accept an offer in accordance with the provisions of laws or administrative regulations shall not refuse the other party's reasonable request to conclude a contract.

Article 495 A subscription letter, order letter, booking letter, or the like, in which the parties agree to enter into a contract within a certain period in the future, constitutes a preliminary contract. If one party fails to perform the obligation to enter into a contract as agreed in the preliminary contract, the other party may request that party bear the liability for breach of the preliminary contract.

Article 496 Standard terms are clauses that are prepared in advance by a party for repeated use and are not subject to negotiation with the other party at the time of concluding the contract. If a contract is concluded using standard terms, the party providing the standard terms shall determine the rights and obligations between the parties in accordance with the principle of fairness, and shall take reasonable means to draw the other party's attention to the clauses that have a significant bearing on the other party's interest, such as clauses that exclude or limit the providing party's liability, and shall explain such clauses upon the other party's request. If the party providing the standard terms fails to perform the obligation of drawing attention or explanation, thereby causing the other party not to notice or understand a clause that has a significant bearing on the other party's interest, the other party may claim that such clause does not become part of the contract.

Article 497 Standard terms are void under any of the following circumstances: (1) The circumstances for invalidity provided in Section 3 of Chapter 6 of Part One of this Law and Article 506 of this Law exist; (2) The party providing the standard terms unreasonably excludes or limits its own liability, increases the other party's liability, or restricts the other party's principal rights; (3) The party providing the standard terms excludes the other party's principal rights.

Article 498 If a dispute arises over the understanding of a standard term, such term shall be interpreted according to the ordinary understanding. If there are two or more interpretations of a standard term, an interpretation unfavorable to the party providing the standard terms shall be adopted. If a standard term is inconsistent with a non-standard term, the non-standard term shall prevail.
Article 499 If a reward offeror publicly declares that it shall pay a reward to a person who completes a specific act, the person who completes such act may request the reward.

Article 500 A party shall bear compensation liability if, during the process of concluding a contract, it causes losses to the other party under any of the following circumstances: (1) Negatively conducting negotiations under the pretext of concluding a contract; (2) Intentionally concealing material facts related to the conclusion of the contract or providing false information; (3) Having other acts that violate the principle of good faith.

Article 501 Where a party knows trade secrets or other information that shall be kept confidential during the process of concluding a contract, it shall not disclose or improperly use such trade secrets or information, regardless of whether the contract is established; if the disclosure or improper use of such trade secrets or information causes loss to the other party, it shall bear compensation liability.

Article 502 A contract lawfully formed shall take effect upon its formation, unless otherwise provided by law or otherwise agreed by the parties. Where, according to the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, a contract shall undergo approval formalities or other such formalities, those provisions shall apply. The failure to undergo approval formalities that affects the contract's taking effect shall not affect the validity of the clauses on obligations to submit for approval and related clauses in the contract. If a party who shall undergo formalities such as applying for approval fails to perform its obligations, the other party may request it to bear liability for breaching such obligations. Where, according to the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, the modification, transfer, or dissolution of a contract, among other circumstances, shall undergo approval formalities or other such formalities, the preceding paragraph shall apply.

Article 503 Where an agent without authority concludes a contract in the name of the principal, and the principal has begun to perform the contractual obligations or has accepted the performance by the other party, the contract shall be deemed to have been ratified.

Article 504 Where a contract is concluded by the legal representative of a legal person or the responsible person of an unincorporated organization acting beyond their authority, such representational act shall be effective, and the contract concluded shall be binding on the legal person or unincorporated organization, unless the other party knew or should have known that they were acting beyond their authority.

Article 505 The validity of a contract concluded by a party beyond its scope of business shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Section 3, Chapter VI, Part One of this Law and the relevant provisions of this Part; the contract shall not be deemed void solely on the ground of being beyond the scope of business.

Article 506 The following exculpatory clauses in a contract shall be void: (1) those causing personal injury to the other party; or (2) those causing property loss to the other party due to intentional act or gross negligence.
Article 507 The ineffectiveness, voidness, revocation, or termination of a contract shall not affect the validity of the clauses in the contract concerning the methods for dispute resolution.
Article 508 Where this Part has no provisions on the validity of a contract, the relevant provisions of Chapter VI, Part One of this Law shall apply.

Article 509 The parties shall fully perform their obligations in accordance with the agreement. The parties shall follow the principle of good faith and perform the obligations of notification, assistance, and confidentiality, among others, in accordance with the nature, purpose, and trade practices of the contract. During the performance of the contract, the parties shall avoid wasting resources, polluting the environment, and damaging the ecosystem.

Article 510 After the contract takes effect, if the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on matters such as quality, price or remuneration, or place of performance, they may enter into a supplementary agreement; if a supplementary agreement cannot be reached, the contract shall be determined in accordance with the relevant clauses of the contract or trade practices.

Article 511 Where the parties have not clearly agreed on the relevant contents of the contract and the matter cannot be determined in accordance with the preceding article, the following provisions shall apply: (1) if the quality requirement is unclear, performance shall be in accordance with mandatory national standards; in the absence of mandatory national standards, performance shall be in accordance with recommended national standards; in the absence of recommended national standards, performance shall be in accordance with industry standards; in the absence of national standards or industry standards, performance shall be in accordance with ordinary standards or specific standards consistent with the purpose of the contract; (2) if the price or remuneration is unclear, performance shall be in accordance with the market price at the place of performance at the time of conclusion of the contract; if government-set prices or government-guided prices are to be implemented according to law, performance shall be in accordance with such provisions; (3) if the place of performance is unclear, where the subject matter is payment of money, performance shall be at the place of the party receiving the money; where the subject matter is delivery of immovable property, performance shall be at the place where the immovable property is located; for any other subject matter, performance shall be at the place of the party performing the obligation; (4) if the time limit for performance is unclear, the debtor may perform at any time, and the creditor may demand performance at any time, but a reasonable period necessary for preparation shall be given to the other party; (5) if the method of performance is unclear, performance shall be in a manner conducive to achieving the purpose of the contract; and (6) if the burden of performance expenses is unclear, the party performing the obligation shall bear the expenses; expenses increased due to the cause of the creditor shall be borne by the creditor.

Article 512 Where the subject matter of an electronic contract concluded through the Internet or other information networks is the delivery of goods and is delivered by express logistics, the time of receipt by the consignee shall be the time of delivery. Where the subject matter of an electronic contract is the provision of services, the time indicated in the generated electronic voucher or physical voucher shall be the time of service provision; if the voucher does not indicate the time or the indicated time is inconsistent with the actual time of service provision, the actual time of service provision shall prevail. Where the subject matter of an electronic contract is delivered by online transmission, the time at which the subject matter of the contract enters the specific system designated by the other party and can be retrieved and identified shall be the time of delivery. Where the parties to an electronic contract have otherwise agreed on the method or time of delivery of goods or provision of services, such agreement shall be followed.

Article 513 Where government-set prices or government-guided prices are implemented, if the government adjusts the prices within the delivery period agreed in the contract, the prices at the time of delivery shall be used for pricing. Where the subject matter is delivered late, if the price increases, the original price shall apply; if the price decreases, the new price shall apply. Where the subject matter is collected late or payment is made late, if the price increases, the new price shall apply; if the price decreases, the original price shall apply.

Article 514 For an obligation with the content of paying money, unless otherwise provided by law or otherwise agreed by the parties, the creditor may request the debtor to perform in the legal tender of the place of actual performance.

Article 515 Where there are multiple subject matters and the debtor only needs to perform one of them, the debtor shall have the right of choice; provided that, unless otherwise provided by law, otherwise agreed by the parties, or otherwise provided by trade practices. If the party with the right of choice fails to make a choice within the agreed period or before the expiration of the performance period, and fails to make a choice within a reasonable period after being urged, the right of choice shall shift to the other party.

Article 516 When exercising the right of choice, a party shall promptly notify the other party; the subject matter shall be determined when the notice reaches the other party. The subject matter shall not be changed after it is determined, unless the other party consents. Where a circumstance of impossibility of performance occurs for an optional subject matter, the party with the right of choice may not select the subject matter that is impossible to perform, unless such impossibility was caused by the other party.

Article 517 Where there are two or more creditors, and the subject matter is divisible, and each creditor has a claim in proportion to its share, it shall be a several claim; where there are two or more debtors, and the subject matter is divisible, and each debtor bears the obligation in proportion to its share, it shall be a several obligation. Where the shares of several creditors or several debtors are difficult to determine, the shares shall be deemed to be equal.

Article 518 Where there are two or more creditors, and all or part of the creditors may request the debtor to perform the obligation, it shall be a joint and several claim; where there are two or more debtors, and the creditor may request all or part of the debtors to perform the entire obligation, it shall be a joint and several obligation. A joint and several claim or joint and several obligation shall be provided by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 519 Where the shares among joint and several debtors are difficult to determine, the shares shall be deemed to be equal. A joint and several debtor that has actually performed an obligation exceeding its own share shall have the right to seek recourse from the other joint and several debtors for the excess within the scope of their unperformed shares and shall correspondingly enjoy the rights of the creditor, provided that the creditor's interests are not prejudiced. Other joint and several debtors may raise defenses against the creditor against such debtor. If the joint and several debtor against whom recourse is sought cannot perform its share, the other joint and several debtors shall bear the share proportionally within the corresponding scope.

Article 520 Where some joint and several debtors perform, set off the obligation, or deposit the subject matter, the obligations of other debtors to the creditor shall be discharged to the corresponding extent; such debtors may seek recourse from the other debtors in accordance with the preceding article. Where the creditor discharges the obligation of some joint and several debtors, the obligations of the other debtors to the creditor shall be discharged within the scope of the share that such discharged debtors shall bear. Where the obligation of some joint and several debtors and the creditor's claim are merged in one person, the creditor's claim against the other debtors shall continue to exist after deducting the share that such debtors shall bear. Where the creditor is delayed in accepting performance from some joint and several debtors, it shall have effect on the other joint and several debtors.

Article 521 Where the share of each joint creditor cannot be determined, it shall be deemed that they have equal shares. A joint creditor who has actually received performance of the obligatory right shall return the corresponding portion to the other joint creditors in proportion to their respective shares. Joint obligatory rights shall be governed by reference to the relevant provisions of this Chapter on joint obligations.

Article 522 Where the parties agree that the debtor shall perform the obligation to a third party, and the debtor fails to perform the obligation to such third party or the performance is not in conformity with the agreement, the debtor shall bear the liability for breach of contract to the creditor. Where a law provides or the parties agree that the third party may directly request the debtor to perform the obligation to it, and the third party fails to explicitly refuse such performance within a reasonable period, but the debtor fails to perform the obligation to such third party or the performance is not in conformity with the agreement, the third party may request the debtor to bear the liability for breach of contract; and the defenses that the debtor has against the creditor may be asserted against the third party.

Article 523 Where the parties agree that a third party shall perform the obligation to the creditor, and the third party fails to perform the obligation or the performance is not in conformity with the agreement, the debtor shall bear the liability for breach of contract to the creditor.

Article 524 Where the debtor fails to perform its obligation, and a third party has a legitimate interest in performing such obligation, the third party shall be entitled to perform on behalf of the debtor to the creditor, unless such obligation may only be performed by the debtor by its nature, as agreed by the parties, or as provided by law. After the creditor accepts the performance by the third party, the creditor's obligatory right against the debtor shall be assigned to the third party, unless otherwise agreed by the debtor and the third party.

Article 525 Where the parties owe obligations to each other and there is no order of priority for performance, they shall perform such obligations simultaneously. A party shall have the right to reject the other party's request for performance before the latter performs its own obligation. Where the other party's performance is not in conformity with the agreement, a party shall have the right to reject the other party's corresponding request for performance.

Article 526 Where the parties owe obligations to each other, and there is an order of priority for performance, the party that is obligated to perform later shall have the right to reject the request for performance of the party that is obligated to perform first but fails to do so. Where the performance of the party that is obligated to perform first is not in conformity with the agreement, the party that is obligated to perform later shall have the right to reject the corresponding request for performance of the former party.

Article 527 A party that is obligated to perform its obligation first may suspend its performance if it has conclusive evidence showing that the other party falls under any of the following circumstances: (1) its business operations are seriously deteriorating; (2) it is transferring property or withdrawing funds to evade obligations; (3) it has lost its business reputation; or (4) there are other circumstances where it has lost or may lose its ability to perform its obligation. Where a party suspends performance without conclusive evidence, it shall bear the liability for breach of contract.

Article 528 Where a party suspends performance in accordance with the preceding article, it shall promptly notify the other party. If the other party provides appropriate security, the suspending party shall resume performance. After the suspension of performance, if the other party fails to restore its ability to perform and fails to provide appropriate security within a reasonable period, it shall be deemed as indicating by its own conduct that it shall not perform the main obligation. The party that suspended performance may dissolve the contract and may request the other party to bear the liability for breach of contract.

Article 529 Where a creditor is divided, merged, or changes its domicile without notifying the debtor, thereby making it difficult for the debtor to perform the obligation, the debtor may suspend performance or deposit the subject matter with a competent authority.

Article 530 A creditor may reject the debtor's early performance of the obligation, unless such early performance does not harm the creditor's interests. Any additional costs incurred by the creditor due to the debtor's early performance shall be borne by the debtor.

Article 531 A creditor may reject the debtor's partial performance of the obligation, unless such partial performance does not harm the creditor's interests. Any additional costs incurred by the creditor due to the debtor's partial performance shall be borne by the debtor.

Article 532 After a contract has taken effect, a party shall not refuse to perform its contractual obligations on the ground of a change in its name or the name of the party, or a change in its legal representative, the person in charge, or the handler.

Article 533 After the conclusion of a contract, if a fundamental condition of the contract undergoes a material change that the parties could not have foreseen at the time of concluding the contract and that does not constitute a commercial risk, and the continued performance of the contract is manifestly unfair to one party, the party that is adversely affected may renegotiate with the other party. If the renegotiation fails within a reasonable period, the party may request the People's Court or an arbitration institution to modify or dissolve the contract. The People's Court or the arbitration institution shall, taking into account the actual circumstances of the case, modify or dissolve the contract in accordance with the principle of fairness.

Article 534 Where a party uses a contract to engage in any conduct that harms the interests of the State or the public interest, the market supervision and administration authorities and other relevant competent administrative departments shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, be responsible for supervising and handling the matter.

Article 535 Where the debtor's failure to diligently exercise its obligatory right or any accessory right related thereto affects the realization of the creditor's due obligatory right, the creditor may apply to the People's Court to exercise by subrogation, in its own name, the debtor's rights against the counterparty, unless such rights exclusively belong to the debtor. The scope of exercising the right of subrogation shall be limited to the creditor's due obligatory right. The necessary expenses incurred by the creditor in exercising the right of subrogation shall be borne by the debtor. The defenses that the counterparty has against the debtor may be asserted against the creditor.

Article 536 Before the creditor's obligatory right falls due, if the debtor's obligatory right or any accessory right related thereto is in a situation such as the limitation period for litigation is about to expire, or the creditor has failed to declare the obligatory right in bankruptcy in a timely manner, which affects the realization of the creditor's obligatory right, the creditor may by subrogation request the debtor's counterparty to perform to the debtor, declare it to the bankruptcy administrator, or take other necessary actions.

Article 537 If the People's Court establishes the right of subrogation, the counterparty of the debtor shall perform its obligation to the creditor. After the creditor accepts the performance, the corresponding rights and obligations between the creditor and the debtor, and between the debtor and the counterparty, shall be terminated. If the debtor's obligatory right against the counterparty or any accessory right related thereto has been subjected to preservation or enforcement measures, or if the debtor has become bankrupt, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws.

Article 538 If the debtor disposes of its property rights and interests without consideration by means of waiving its obligatory rights, waiving security for its obligatory rights, transferring property without consideration, or maliciously extends the period for performance of its due obligatory rights, thereby affecting the realization of the creditor's obligatory rights, the creditor may request the People's Court to revoke the debtor's act.

Article 539 If the debtor transfers property at a manifestly unreasonably low price, acquires another person's property at a manifestly unreasonably high price, or provides security for another person's obligations, thereby affecting the realization of the creditor's obligatory rights, and if the counterparty of the debtor knew or should have known such circumstances, the creditor may request the People's Court to revoke the debtor's act.

Article 540 The scope of exercising the right of revocation shall be limited to the creditor's obligatory right. The necessary expenses incurred by the creditor in exercising the right of revocation shall be borne by the debtor.

Article 541 The right of revocation shall be exercised within one year from the day when the creditor knows or should have known the cause for revocation. If the right of revocation has not been exercised within five years from the day when the debtor's act occurred, such right of revocation shall be extinguished.
Article 542 Where an act of the debtor that affects the realization of the creditor's claim is revoked, such act shall have no legal binding force from the very beginning.
Article 543 The parties may modify the contract upon mutual agreement.
Article 544 Where the parties do not agree clearly on the content of a modification of the contract, it shall be presumed that the contract has not been modified.

Article 545 A creditor may assign all or part of its claim to a third party, except in any of the following circumstances: (1) the claim is not assignable by its nature; (2) the claim is not assignable according to the agreement between the parties; or (3) the claim is not assignable according to the provisions of law. Where the parties agree that a non-monetary claim shall not be assigned, such agreement may not be asserted against a bona fide third party. Where the parties agree that a monetary claim shall not be assigned, such agreement may not be asserted against any third party.

Article 546 Where a creditor assigns a claim without notifying the debtor, such assignment shall not be binding on the debtor. A notice of assignment of a claim may not be revoked, except with the consent of the assignee.

Article 547 Where a creditor assigns a claim, the assignee shall acquire the ancillary rights related to the claim, except where such ancillary rights are exclusively personal to the creditor. The acquisition of ancillary rights by the assignee shall not be affected by the failure to undergo registration of transfer or deliver possession of the ancillary rights.
Article 548 After receiving the notice of assignment of the claim, the debtor may assert against the assignee any defense that the debtor has against the assignor.

Article 549 The debtor may set off against the assignee its claim in any of the following circumstances: (1) at the time the debtor receives the notice of assignment of the claim, the debtor has a claim against the assignor, and such claim of the debtor falls due before or at the same time as the assigned claim; or (2) the debtor's claim and the assigned claim arise from the same contract.
Article 550 The assignor shall bear the additional performance costs arising from the assignment of the claim.

Article 551 Where a debtor transfers all or part of its debt to a third party, it shall obtain the consent of the creditor. The debtor or the third party may urge the creditor to give consent within a reasonable period of time; if the creditor does not respond, it shall be deemed to have withheld consent.

Article 552 Where a third party agrees with the debtor to join in the debt and notifies the creditor thereof, or where the third party indicates to the creditor that it is willing to join in the debt, and the creditor does not expressly refuse within a reasonable period of time, the creditor may request the third party to assume joint and several liability with the debtor within the scope of the debt that the third party is willing to assume.

Article 553 Where a debtor transfers its debt, the new debtor may assert any defense that the original debtor has against the creditor; however, if the original debtor has a claim against the creditor, the new debtor may not set off such claim against the creditor.

Article 554 Where a debtor transfers its debt, the new debtor shall assume the ancillary obligations related to the principal debt, except where such ancillary obligations are exclusively personal to the original debtor.
Article 555 A party may transfer its rights and obligations under the contract to a third party together, subject to the consent of the other party.
Article 556 Where the rights and obligations under a contract are transferred together, the relevant provisions on the assignment of claims and the transfer of debts shall apply.

Article 557 A claim and debt shall be extinguished in any of the following circumstances: (1) the debt has been performed; (2) the debts are set off against each other; (3) the debtor has lawfully deposited the subject matter; (4) the creditor has released the debt; (5) the claim and debt are merged in the same person; or (6) any other circumstance in which the claim and debt are extinguished as provided by law or agreed by the parties. Upon rescission of a contract, the rights and obligations under such contract shall be extinguished.

Article 558 After a claim and debt are extinguished, the parties shall, in accordance with the principle of good faith and other principles, and based on the trade practices, perform the obligations of notification, assistance, confidentiality, and recycling of used items, among others.

Article 559 When a claim and debt are extinguished, the ancillary rights of the claim shall also be extinguished simultaneously, except where the law provides otherwise or the parties agree otherwise.

Article 560 Where a debtor owes several debts of the same type to the same creditor and the debtor's performance is insufficient to discharge all the debts, the debtor shall, at the time of performance, designate which debt it is performing, except where the parties agree otherwise. If the debtor fails to make such designation, it shall first perform the debt that has fallen due; where all the debts have fallen due, it shall first perform the debt that is lacking security or is least secured; where none of the debts is secured or all are equally secured, it shall first perform the debt that is the most burdensome for the debtor; where the burdens are equal, the debts shall be performed in the order of their maturity; and where they fall due at the same time, they shall be performed in proportion to each debt.

Article 561 Where a debtor, in addition to performing the principal obligation, shall also pay interest and the relevant expenses for realizing the creditor's rights, and the debtor's performance is insufficient to discharge all obligations, unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the performance shall be made in the following order: (1) the relevant expenses for realizing the creditor's rights; (2) interest; and (3) the principal obligation.

Article 562 The parties may dissolve the contract upon mutual agreement. The parties may agree on the grounds for one party to dissolve the contract. When the grounds for dissolution of the contract occur, the party entitled to dissolution may dissolve the contract.

Article 563 A party may dissolve the contract under any of the following circumstances: (1) the purpose of the contract cannot be achieved due to force majeure; (2) before the expiration of the performance period, the other party expressly states or indicates by its own conduct that it shall not perform the principal obligation; (3) the other party delays in performing the principal obligation and still fails to perform it within a reasonable period after being urged; (4) the other party delays in performing its obligations or commits other breaches of contract that render the purpose of the contract unachievable; or (5) other circumstances as provided by law. For a contract of indefinite duration that involves a continuous performance obligation, a party may dissolve the contract at any time, provided that it shall notify the other party within a reasonable period in advance.

Article 564 Where the law provides or the parties agree on a period for exercising the right to dissolve the contract, and the party fails to exercise it upon the expiration of such period, that right shall lapse. Where the law does not provide or the parties have not agreed on a period for exercising the right to dissolve the contract, that right shall lapse if it is not exercised within one year from the date on which the person entitled to dissolution knew or should have known of the grounds for dissolution, or if it is not exercised within a reasonable period after being urged by the other party.

Article 565 Where one party claims dissolution of the contract according to law, it shall notify the other party. The contract shall be dissolved upon the receipt of the notice by the other party; if the notice states that the contract shall be automatically dissolved if the debtor fails to perform its obligations within a certain period, and the debtor fails to perform its obligations within that period, the contract shall be dissolved upon the expiration of the period specified in the notice. If the other party objects to the dissolution, either party may request the People's Court or an arbitration institution to confirm the validity of the dissolution. Where one party, without notifying the other party, claims dissolution of the contract according to law directly by filing a lawsuit or applying for arbitration, and the People's Court or arbitration institution confirms the claim, the contract shall be dissolved upon the service of a copy of the statement of claim or a copy of the arbitration application on the other party.

Article 566 After the dissolution of a contract, the performance of obligations not yet performed shall be terminated; for those already performed, a party may, based on the performance status and the nature of the contract, request the restoration of the original status or the adoption of other remedial measures, and shall have the right to claim damages. Where a contract is dissolved due to a breach of contract, the party entitled to dissolution may request the breaching party to bear the liability for breach of contract, unless otherwise agreed by the parties. After the dissolution of the principal contract, the guarantor shall still bear the guarantee liability for the civil liability that the debtor shall bear, unless otherwise agreed in the guarantee contract.
Article 567 The termination of the relationship of rights and obligations under a contract shall not affect the validity of the clauses in the contract concerning settlement and liquidation.

Article 568 Where the parties owe obligations to each other, and the subject matter of such obligations is of the same type and quality, either party may set off its own obligation against the other party's due obligation; however, such set-off shall not apply where it is prohibited by the nature of the obligation, by agreement of the parties, or by law. Where a party claims a set-off, it shall notify the other party. The notice shall take effect upon its receipt by the other party. A set-off shall not be subject to any condition or time limit.
Article 569 Where the parties owe obligations to each other, and the subject matter of such obligations is not of the same type and quality, they may also effect a set-off by mutual agreement.

Article 570 Under any of the following circumstances, where performance of the obligation is difficult, the debtor may deposit the subject matter: (1) the creditor refuses to accept performance without just cause; (2) the creditor's whereabouts are unknown; (3) the creditor dies without a designated heir or estate administrator, or loses capacity for civil conduct without a designated guardian; or (4) other circumstances as provided by law. If the subject matter is unsuitable for deposit or the deposit costs are excessively high, the debtor may auction or sell the subject matter according to law and deposit the proceeds.

Article 571 The deposit shall be established when the debtor delivers the subject matter or the proceeds from the auction or sale of the subject matter according to law to the deposit authority. Once the deposit is established, the debtor shall be deemed to have delivered the subject matter to the extent of the deposit.
Article 572 After the subject matter is deposited, the debtor shall promptly notify the creditor or the creditor's heir, estate administrator, guardian, or property custodian.

Article 573 After the subject matter is deposited, the risk of damage or loss shall be borne by the creditor. During the period of deposit, the fruits of the subject matter shall belong to the creditor. The deposit costs shall be borne by the creditor.

Article 574 The creditor may collect the deposited subject matter at any time. However, if the creditor owes a due obligation to the debtor, the deposit authority shall, upon the debtor's request, refuse the creditor's collection of the deposited subject matter until the creditor performs the obligation or provides security. The right of the creditor to collect the deposited subject matter shall lapse if it is not exercised within five years from the date of deposit, and the deposited subject matter, after deducting the deposit costs, shall belong to the State. However, if the creditor fails to perform its due obligation to the debtor, or the creditor indicates in writing to the deposit authority that it waives the right to collect the deposited subject matter, the debtor shall be entitled to take back the deposited subject matter after bearing the deposit costs.

Article 575 Where the creditor remits part or all of the debtor's obligation, the creditor's rights and debtor's obligations shall be terminated in part or in whole, unless the debtor refuses such remission within a reasonable period.

Article 576 Where the creditor's rights and debtor's obligations are vested in the same person, the creditor's rights and debtor's obligations shall be terminated, unless the interests of a third party are prejudiced.

Article 577 Where one party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, it shall bear the liability for breach of contract, such as continuing performance, adopting remedial measures, or compensating for losses.

Article 578 Where one party expressly states or indicates by its own conduct that it shall not perform its contractual obligations, the other party may request it to bear the liability for breach of contract before the expiration of the performance period.
Article 579 Where one party fails to pay the price, remuneration, rent, or interest, or fails to perform other monetary obligations, the other party may request payment.

Article 580 Where one party fails to perform a non-monetary obligation or performs it in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, the other party may request performance, except under any of the following circumstances: (1) performance is legally or factually impossible; (2) the subject matter of the obligation is unsuitable for compulsory performance or the cost of performance is excessively high; or (3) the creditor fails to request performance within a reasonable period. Where one of the excepted circumstances provided in the preceding paragraph renders the purpose of the contract unachievable, the People's Court or an arbitration institution may, upon a party's request, terminate the relationship of rights and obligations under the contract, but such termination shall not affect the liability for breach of contract.

Article 581 Where one party fails to perform an obligation, or the performance of an obligation does not conform to the agreement, and compulsory performance is not possible due to the nature of the obligation, the other party may request that the former bear the costs of performance by a third party in lieu thereof.

Article 582 Where the performance does not conform to the agreement, the party in breach shall bear the liability for breach of contract in accordance with the agreement of the parties. If there is no agreement on liability for breach of contract or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the aggrieved party may, in light of the nature of the subject matter and the extent of the loss, reasonably elect to request that the other party bear the liability for breach of contract by way of repair, rework, replacement, return of the goods, reduction of the price or remuneration, or other such remedies.

Article 583 Where one party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner not in conformity with the agreement, and the other party suffers other losses after performance of the obligations or adoption of remedial measures, the former shall compensate for such losses.

Article 584 Where one party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner not in conformity with the agreement, thereby causing losses to the other party, the amount of compensation for losses shall be equivalent to the losses caused by the breach of contract, including the benefits that could have been obtained after the performance of the contract; provided, however, that it shall not exceed the losses that the party in breach foresaw or ought to have foreseen as possible consequences of the breach at the time of conclusion of the contract.

Article 585 The parties may agree that, in the event of a breach of contract by one party, it shall pay a certain sum of liquidated damages to the other party in light of the circumstances of the breach, and may also agree on the method for calculating the amount of compensation for losses arising from the breach of contract. Where the agreed amount of liquidated damages is lower than the losses caused, the People's Court or an arbitration institution may, upon the request of a party, increase it; where the agreed amount of liquidated damages is excessively higher than the losses caused, the People's Court or an arbitration institution may, upon the request of a party, reduce it appropriately. Where the parties agree on liquidated damages for delay in performance, the defaulting party shall, after paying the liquidated damages, still perform its obligations.

Article 586 The parties may agree that one party pays a deposit to the other party as a guarantee for the performance of an obligation. A deposit contract shall be formed upon the actual payment of the deposit. The amount of the deposit shall be agreed upon by the parties; however, it shall not exceed twenty percent of the value of the subject matter of the principal contract, and any amount in excess shall not have the effect of a deposit. Where the amount of the deposit actually paid is more or less than the agreed amount, the agreed amount of deposit shall be deemed to have been modified.

Article 587 Where the obligor performs its obligation, the deposit shall be applied towards the price or be returned. Where the party paying the deposit fails to perform the obligation or performs it in a manner not in conformity with the agreement, thereby defeating the purpose of the contract, it shall not be entitled to request the return of the deposit; where the party receiving the deposit fails to perform the obligation or performs it in a manner not in conformity with the agreement, thereby defeating the purpose of the contract, it shall return double the amount of the deposit.

Article 588 Where the parties have agreed on both liquidated damages and a deposit, in the event of a breach of contract by one party, the other party may elect to apply either the liquidated damages clause or the deposit clause. Where the deposit is insufficient to compensate for the losses caused by the breach of one party, the other party may request compensation for losses in excess of the amount of the deposit.

Article 589 Where the obligor performs its obligation in accordance with the agreement, but the obligee refuses to accept performance without justifiable reason, the obligor may request the obligee to compensate for the increased expenses incurred. During the period of delay by the obligee in accepting performance, the obligor shall not be required to pay interest.

Article 590 Where one party is unable to perform the contract due to force majeure, it shall be partially or wholly exempted from liability depending on the impact of the force majeure, unless otherwise provided by law. Where a party is unable to perform the contract due to force majeure, it shall promptly notify the other party to mitigate the potential losses that may be caused to the other party, and shall provide proof within a reasonable period. Where an event of force majeure occurs after one party has delayed in performance, the liability of the party for breach of contract shall not be exempted.

Article 591 After one party breaches the contract, the other party shall take appropriate measures to prevent the aggravation of losses; if the other party fails to take appropriate measures resulting in the aggravation of losses, it shall not be entitled to claim compensation for the aggravated portion of the losses. The reasonable expenses incurred by a party in preventing the aggravation of losses shall be borne by the defaulting party.

Article 592 Where both parties breach the contract, each party shall bear its respective liability. Where the breach of one party causes losses to the other party, and the other party is at fault for the occurrence of the losses, the amount of compensation for losses may be reduced accordingly.

Article 593 Where one party breaches the contract due to the act of a third party, it shall bear liability for the breach of contract to the other party in accordance with law. Any disputes between that party and the third party shall be dealt with in accordance with legal provisions or the agreement between them.

Article 594 The prescription period for bringing an action or applying for arbitration arising from disputes under a contract for the international sale of goods or a technology import and export contract shall be four years. Subsection II: Model Contracts
Article 595 A sales contract is a contract under which the seller transfers the ownership of the subject matter to the buyer, and the buyer pays the price.

Article 596 The contents of a sales contract shall generally include terms such as the name, quantity, quality, and price of the subject matter, the performance period, place and method of performance, packaging method, inspection standards and methods, settlement method, the language used for the contract and its validity, and other such terms.

Article 597 Where the seller's failure to obtain the right of disposition results in the inability to transfer the ownership of the subject matter, the buyer may rescind the contract and request the seller to bear liability for breach of contract. In the case of subject matters the transfer of which is prohibited or restricted by laws or administrative regulations, the provisions thereof shall govern.

Article 598 The seller shall perform the obligations of delivering the subject matter or the documents for taking delivery of the subject matter to the buyer, and of transferring the ownership of the subject matter.

Article 599 The seller shall deliver to the buyer, in accordance with the agreement or trade usage, the relevant documents and materials other than the documents for taking delivery of the subject matter.

Article 600 Where a subject matter with intellectual property rights is sold, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties, such intellectual property rights in the subject matter shall not belong to the buyer.
Article 601 The seller shall deliver the subject matter at the agreed time. If a period for delivery is agreed upon, the seller may deliver at any time within such period.
Article 602 If the parties have not agreed on a time limit for delivery of the subject matter or such agreement is unclear, the provisions of Articles 510 and 511(4) of this Law shall apply.

Article 603 The seller shall deliver the subject matter at the agreed place. If the parties have not agreed on the place of delivery or such agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the following provisions shall apply: (1) if the subject matter requires carriage, the seller shall deliver the subject matter to the first carrier for conveyance to the buyer; (2) if the subject matter does not require carriage, and the seller and the buyer, at the time of entering into the contract, know that the subject matter is at a certain place, the seller shall deliver the subject matter at that place; if they do not know that the subject matter is at a certain place, the seller shall deliver the subject matter at the seller's place of business at the time of entering into the contract.

Article 604 The risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the seller before delivery and by the buyer after delivery, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 605 If the subject matter is not delivered within the agreed time limit due to the buyer, the buyer shall bear the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter from the time of such breach of agreement.

Article 606 Where the seller sells the subject matter which is in transit and under carriage by a carrier, unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the buyer from the time of formation of the contract.

Article 607 After the seller transports the subject matter to the place designated by the buyer and delivers it to the carrier in accordance with the agreement, the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the buyer. If the parties have not agreed on the place of delivery or such agreement is unclear, and the subject matter requires carriage under Article 603(2)(1) of this Law, after the seller delivers the subject matter to the first carrier, the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the buyer.

Article 608 If the seller places the subject matter at the place of delivery in accordance with the agreement or under Article 603(2)(2) of this Law, and the buyer, in breach of the agreement, fails to take delivery, the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the buyer from the time of such breach of agreement.

Article 609 The seller's failure to deliver the documents and materials relating to the subject matter in accordance with the agreement shall not affect the transfer of the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter.

Article 610 If the subject matter fails to meet the quality requirements, thereby preventing the realization of the purpose of the contract, the buyer may refuse to accept the subject matter or dissolve the contract. If the buyer refuses to accept the subject matter or dissolves the contract, the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the seller.

Article 611 Where the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter is borne by the buyer, this shall not affect the buyer's right to demand that the seller bear liability for breach of contract due to the seller's failure to perform its obligations in accordance with the agreement.
Article 612 The seller shall have the obligation to warrant that no third party has any right to the delivered subject matter, unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 613 If the buyer knew or should have known, at the time of entering into the contract, that a third party had rights to the subject matter of the sale, the seller shall not bear the obligation provided for in the preceding article.

Article 614 If the buyer has conclusive evidence proving that a third party has rights to the subject matter, the buyer may suspend payment of the corresponding price, unless the seller provides appropriate guarantee.

Article 615 The seller shall deliver the subject matter in accordance with the agreed quality requirements. If the seller has provided a description of the quality of the subject matter, the delivered subject matter shall meet the quality requirements set out in such description.

Article 616 If the parties have not agreed on the quality requirements for the subject matter or such agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the provisions of Article 511(1) of this Law shall apply.

Article 617 If the subject matter delivered by the seller does not meet the quality requirements, the buyer may, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 582 to 584 of this Law, demand that the seller bear liability for breach of contract.

Article 618 If the parties agree to mitigate or exempt the seller from liability for defects in the subject matter, but the seller, intentionally or by gross negligence, fails to inform the buyer of such defects, the seller shall have no right to claim mitigation or exemption of liability.

Article 619 The seller shall deliver the subject matter in the agreed packaging method. If there is no agreement on the packaging method or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the subject matter shall be packaged in a generally accepted manner; if there is no generally accepted manner, the packaging method shall be one that is sufficient to protect the subject matter and is conducive to resource conservation and ecological environment protection.
Article 620 Upon receipt of the subject matter, the buyer shall inspect it within the agreed inspection period. If no inspection period is agreed, the buyer shall inspect it promptly.

Article 621 Where the parties agree on an inspection period, the buyer shall notify the seller within the inspection period if the quantity or quality of the subject matter does not conform to the agreement. If the buyer is dilatory in giving such notice, the quantity or quality of the subject matter shall be deemed to conform to the agreement. Where the parties have not agreed on an inspection period, the buyer shall notify the seller within a reasonable period after discovering or should have discovered that the quantity or quality of the subject matter does not conform to the agreement. If the buyer fails to give notice within a reasonable period, or fails to give notice to the seller within two years from the date of receipt of the subject matter, the quantity or quality of the subject matter shall be deemed to conform to the agreement; provided that, if a quality guarantee period is applicable to the subject matter, the quality guarantee period shall apply instead of the said two-year period. Where the seller knew or should have known that the delivered subject matter did not conform to the agreement, the buyer shall not be subject to the time limits for notice prescribed in the preceding two paragraphs.

Article 622 If the inspection period agreed upon by the parties is so short that, given the nature of the subject matter and trade practices, it is difficult for the buyer to complete a comprehensive inspection within such period, such period shall be deemed only as the period for the buyer to raise objections concerning the apparent defects of the subject matter. If the agreed inspection period or quality guarantee period is shorter than the period prescribed by laws or administrative regulations, the period prescribed by such laws or administrative regulations shall prevail.

Article 623 Where the parties have not agreed on an inspection period, and the delivery note, confirmation note or the like signed by the buyer specifies the quantity, model, and specification of the subject matter, it shall be presumed that the buyer has inspected the quantity and apparent defects of the subject matter, unless there is sufficient relevant evidence to the contrary.

Article 624 Where the seller delivers the subject matter to a third party as instructed by the buyer, and the inspection standard agreed upon between the seller and the buyer is inconsistent with that agreed upon between the buyer and the third party, the inspection standard agreed upon between the seller and the buyer shall prevail.

Article 625 Where, according to laws or administrative regulations or the agreement of the parties, the subject matter shall be recycled after the expiration of its useful life, the seller shall bear the obligation to recycle the subject matter itself or to entrust a third party to do so.

Article 626 The buyer shall pay the price in the agreed amount and by the agreed method of payment. If the amount or method of payment is not agreed upon or the agreement is unclear, the provisions of Articles 510, and subparagraphs (2) and (5) of Article 511 of this Law shall apply.

Article 627 The buyer shall pay the price at the agreed place. If the place of payment is not agreed upon or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the buyer shall pay at the seller's place of business; provided that, if the payment of the price is conditional upon the delivery of the subject matter or the documents for taking delivery of the subject matter, payment shall be made at the place where the subject matter or the documents for taking delivery thereof are delivered.

Article 628 The buyer shall pay the price at the agreed time. If the time of payment is not agreed upon or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the buyer shall pay simultaneously upon receipt of the subject matter or the documents for taking delivery of the subject matter.

Article 629 If the seller delivers an excess quantity of the subject matter, the buyer may accept or reject the excess part. If the buyer accepts the excess part, it shall pay for it at the agreed price; if the buyer rejects the excess part, it shall notify the seller promptly.
Article 630 Fruits generated from the subject matter before delivery shall belong to the seller; those generated after delivery shall belong to the buyer. However, unless the parties agree otherwise.

Article 631 Where the contract is dissolved due to the non-conformity of the principal component of the subject matter, the dissolution shall extend to the accessory component. Where the contract is dissolved due to the non-conformity of the accessory component, the dissolution shall not extend to the principal component.

Article 632 Where the subject matter consists of several items, and one of them does not conform to the agreement, the buyer may dissolve the contract only with respect to that item. However, if the separation of that item from the others would materially impair the value of the subject matter, the buyer may dissolve the contract with respect to all the items.

Article 633 Where the seller delivers the subject matter in installments, if the seller fails to deliver one installment or delivers it in a manner that does not conform to the agreement, thereby frustrating the purpose of the contract for that installment, the buyer may dissolve the contract with respect to that installment. If the seller fails to deliver one installment or delivers it in a manner that does not conform to the agreement, thereby frustrating the purpose of the contract for the subsequent installments, the buyer may dissolve the contract with respect to that installment and all subsequent installments. If the buyer dissolves the contract with respect to one installment, and if that installment is interdependent with the other installments, the buyer may dissolve the contract with respect to all installments, whether delivered or not.

Article 634 If the buyer under an installment sale fails to pay an amount of the price due which reaches one-fifth of the total price, and still fails to pay the amount due within a reasonable period after receiving a demand for payment, the seller may request the buyer to pay the entire outstanding price or dissolve the contract. If the seller dissolves the contract, it may request the buyer to pay a fee for the use of the subject matter.

Article 635 In a sale by sample, the parties shall seal the sample and may provide a description of the quality of the sample. The subject matter delivered by the seller shall conform to the quality of the sample and its description.

Article 636 In a sale by sample, if the buyer is unaware of latent defects in the sample, even if the delivered subject matter is the same as the sample, the quality of the subject matter delivered by the seller shall still conform to the usual standards for goods of the same type.

Article 637 The parties to a sale on trial may agree on a trial period for the subject matter. If the trial period is not agreed upon or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, it shall be determined by the seller.

Article 638 The buyer in a sale on trial may purchase the subject matter or refuse to purchase it during the trial period. Upon expiration of the trial period, if the buyer does not indicate whether to purchase the subject matter, it shall be deemed to have purchased it. If the buyer in a sale on trial has paid part of the price or has performed acts such as selling, leasing, or creating a security interest over the subject matter during the trial period, it shall be deemed to have agreed to purchase it.

Article 639 If the parties to a sale on trial have not agreed on a fee for the use of the subject matter, or the agreement is unclear, the seller shall have no right to request the buyer to pay such a fee.
Article 640 The risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter during the trial period shall be borne by the seller.

Article 641 The parties may agree in a sales contract that the ownership of the subject matter shall remain with the seller if the buyer fails to perform the obligation to pay the price or other obligations. The seller's retained ownership of the subject matter may not be asserted against a bona fide third party unless it has been registered.

Article 642 Where the parties agree that the seller shall retain ownership of the subject matter of the contract, and before the transfer of ownership of the subject matter, the buyer commits any of the following acts causing damage to the seller, unless the parties agree otherwise, the seller has the right to repossess the subject matter: (1) failing to pay the price as agreed and still failing to pay within a reasonable period after demand for payment; (2) failing to fulfill specific conditions as agreed; (3) selling, pledging, or otherwise improperly disposing of the subject matter. The seller may negotiate with the buyer for the repossession of the subject matter; if negotiation fails, the procedures for the realization of security interests may be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 643 After the seller repossesses the subject matter in accordance with paragraph 1 of the preceding Article, if the buyer eliminates the grounds for the seller's repossession of the subject matter within the reasonable redemption period agreed by the parties or designated by the seller, the buyer may request redemption of the subject matter. If the buyer fails to redeem the subject matter within the redemption period, the seller may sell the subject matter to a third party at a reasonable price. If, after deducting the unpaid price and necessary expenses from the proceeds of the sale, there is a surplus, it shall be returned to the buyer; if there is a deficiency, the buyer shall make up the shortfall.
Article 644 The rights and obligations of the parties to a sale by tender and the tender procedures, among others, shall be governed by the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Article 645 The rights and obligations of the parties to an auction and the auction procedures, among others, shall be governed by the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 646 Where a law provides for other types of onerous contracts, such provisions shall apply; where there are no such provisions, the relevant provisions on sales contracts shall apply mutatis mutandis.
Article 647 Where the parties agree to a barter transaction for the transfer of ownership of the subject matter, the relevant provisions on sales contracts shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 648 A power supply contract is a contract under which a power supplier supplies electricity to a power consumer and the power consumer pays the electricity fee. A power supplier that supplies electricity to the public shall not reject a reasonable request of a power consumer to conclude a contract.

Article 649 The contents of a power supply contract generally include clauses on the method, quality, and time of power supply; the capacity, address, and nature of power consumption; the metering method; the electricity price and the method of settlement of electricity fees; and the maintenance responsibilities for power supply and consumption facilities.

Article 650 The place of performance of a power supply contract shall be as agreed by the parties; if there is no agreement between the parties or the agreement is unclear, the boundary point of the property rights of the power supply facilities shall be the place of performance.

Article 651 A power supplier shall supply electricity safely in accordance with the power supply quality standards prescribed by the State and the agreement. If the power supplier fails to supply electricity safely in accordance with the power supply quality standards prescribed by the State and the agreement, causing losses to the power consumer, the power supplier shall bear compensation liability.

Article 652 Where a power supplier needs to interrupt the power supply due to scheduled maintenance, temporary maintenance, lawful curtailment of power, or illegal use of electricity by the power consumer, among other reasons, the power supplier shall notify the power consumer in advance in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State; if the power supplier fails to notify the power consumer in advance of the interruption of power supply, causing losses to the power consumer, the power supplier shall bear compensation liability.

Article 653 Where a power outage occurs due to natural disasters or other reasons, the power supplier shall promptly carry out emergency repairs in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State; if the power supplier fails to carry out emergency repairs promptly, causing losses to the power consumer, the power supplier shall bear compensation liability.

Article 654 A power consumer shall pay the electricity fee promptly in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and the agreement of the parties. If the power consumer fails to pay the electricity fee when due, the power consumer shall pay liquidated damages in accordance with the agreement. If, after demand for payment, the power consumer still fails to pay the electricity fee and liquidated damages within a reasonable period, the power supplier may suspend the power supply in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the State. If the power supplier suspends the power supply pursuant to the preceding paragraph, the power supplier shall notify the power consumer in advance.

Article 655 A power consumer shall use electricity safely, economically, and as planned in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and the agreement of the parties. If the power consumer fails to use electricity in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and the agreement of the parties, causing losses to the power supplier, the power consumer shall bear compensation liability.
Article 656 Contracts for the supply of water, gas, or heat shall apply mutatis mutandis the relevant provisions on power supply contracts.
Article 657 A gift contract is a contract under which a donor gives the donor's own property to a donee gratuitously, and the donee expresses acceptance of the gift.

Article 658 The donor may revoke the gift before the transfer of the rights to the gifted property. The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall not apply to a notarized gift contract or a gift contract of a public welfare or moral obligation nature, such as for disaster relief, poverty alleviation, or assistance to the disabled, which shall not be revoked according to law.
Article 659 Where the gifted property is required by law to undergo registration or other procedures, the relevant procedures shall be completed.
