Article 660 Where a notarized gift contract or a gift contract of a public welfare or moral obligation nature, such as for disaster relief, poverty alleviation, or assistance to the disabled, which shall not be revoked according to law, if the donor fails to deliver the gifted property, the donee may demand delivery. If the gifted property that should be delivered pursuant to the preceding paragraph is damaged or lost due to the donor's intentional act or gross negligence, the donor shall bear compensation liability.
Article 661 A gift may be made subject to an obligation. Where a gift is made subject to an obligation, the donee shall perform the obligation in accordance with the agreement.

Article 662 Where the donated property has defects, the donor shall not bear any liability. Where a gift is made subject to an obligation, if the donated property has defects, the donor shall, within the limits of the obligation imposed, bear the same liability as a seller. Where the donor intentionally fails to inform the donee of the defects or warrants that the property is free from defects, thereby causing losses to the donee, the donor shall bear compensation liability.

Article 663 The donor may revoke the gift under any of the following circumstances: (1) the donee seriously infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the donor or any of the donor's close relatives; (2) the donee fails to perform the obligation of supporting the donor; or (3) the donee fails to perform the obligations agreed upon in the contract of gift. The donor's right of revocation shall be exercised within one year from the date when the donor knows or should have known the cause for revocation.

Article 664 Where the donor dies or loses his or her capacity for civil conduct due to the illegal act of the donee, the donor's successor or legal agent may revoke the gift. The successor or legal agent of the donor shall exercise the right of revocation within six months from the date when they know or should have known the cause for revocation.
Article 665 Where the person entitled to revocation revokes the gift, such person may demand the donee to return the donated property.

Article 666 Where the donor's financial circumstances deteriorate significantly, seriously affecting its/his/her production, business operations, or family life, the donor may discontinue the performance of the gift obligation.
Article 667 A loan contract is a contract whereby the borrower borrows money from the lender and repays the borrowed money with interest at maturity.

Article 668 A loan contract shall be made in writing, except where the loan is between natural persons and otherwise agreed. The contents of a loan contract generally include the type, currency, purpose, amount, interest rate, term, and method of repayment of the loan, among other terms.

Article 669 When concluding a loan contract, the borrower shall, as required by the lender, provide truthful information regarding its/his/her business activities and financial status related to the borrowing of money.

Article 670 Interest on a loan shall not be deducted from the principal in advance. Where the interest is deducted from the principal in advance, the loan shall be repaid and interest shall be calculated based on the actual amount of the loan.

Article 671 Where the lender fails to provide the loan on the agreed date and in the agreed amount, thereby causing losses to the borrower, the lender shall compensate for the losses. Where the borrower fails to draw down the loan on the agreed date and in the agreed amount, the borrower shall pay interest on the agreed date and in the agreed amount.

Article 672 The lender may, in accordance with the agreement, inspect and supervise the use of the borrowed money. The borrower shall regularly provide the lender with relevant financial accounting reports or other materials in accordance with the agreement.
Article 673 Where the borrower fails to use the borrowed money for the agreed purpose, the lender may stop granting the loan, recall the loan before its maturity, or dissolve the contract.

Article 674 The borrower shall pay interest at the agreed time limit. Where there is no agreement on the time limit for payment of interest, or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, if the term of the loan is less than one year, the interest shall be paid together with the repayment of the loan when the loan is repaid; if the term of the loan is one year or more, the interest shall be paid at the end of each year, and if the remaining term is less than one year, the interest shall be paid together with the repayment of the loan when the loan is repaid.

Article 675 The borrower shall repay the borrowed money at the agreed time limit. Where there is no agreement on the term of the loan, or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the borrower may repay the loan at any time; and the lender may call on the borrower to repay the loan within a reasonable time limit.

Article 676 Where the borrower fails to repay the borrowed money within the agreed time limit, the borrower shall pay overdue interest in accordance with the agreement or the relevant provisions of the State.
Article 677 Where the borrower repays the borrowed money in advance, the interest shall be calculated based on the actual period of the loan, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
Article 678 The borrower may apply to the lender for an extension of the repayment term before the repayment term expires; if the lender agrees, the term may be extended.
Article 679 A loan contract between natural persons shall be formed at the time when the lender provides the loan.

Article 680 Usurious lending is prohibited, and the interest rate on loans shall not violate the relevant provisions of the State. Where there is no agreement on the payment of interest in a loan contract, it shall be deemed that there is no interest. Where the agreement on the payment of interest in a loan contract is unclear, and the parties cannot reach a supplementary agreement, the interest shall be determined based on factors such as local or the parties' transaction methods, transaction practices, and market interest rates; for a loan between natural persons, it shall be deemed that there is no interest.

Article 681 A suretyship contract is a contract under which a surety and a creditor agree that the surety shall perform the obligation or bear the liability when the debtor fails to perform the due obligation or when the circumstances agreed upon by the parties occur, in order to ensure the satisfaction of the claim.

Article 682 A suretyship contract is an ancillary contract to the principal obligatory contract. If the principal obligatory contract is void, the suretyship contract shall be void, unless otherwise provided by law. Where a suretyship contract is confirmed to be void, if the debtor, the surety, or the creditor is at fault, each shall bear civil liability according to their respective fault.

Article 683 An organ as a legal person may not act as a surety, unless it is approved by the State Council for the purpose of on-lending loans from foreign governments or international economic organizations. A non-profit legal person or an unincorporated organization established for a public welfare purpose may not act as a surety.

Article 684 The contents of a suretyship contract generally include clauses such as the type and amount of the principal claim secured, the time limit for the debtor to perform the obligation, the method, scope, and period of suretyship, among others.

Article 685 A suretyship contract may be a separate written contract or a surety clause in the principal obligatory contract. Where a third party makes a surety to the creditor in writing on its own, and the creditor receives it and raises no objection, the suretyship contract is formed.

Article 686 The methods of suretyship include general suretyship and joint and several suretyship. Where the parties have not agreed upon the method of suretyship or the agreement is unclear in the suretyship contract, the surety shall bear suretyship liability in accordance with general suretyship.

Article 687 Where the parties agree in the suretyship contract that the surety shall bear suretyship liability when the debtor is unable to perform the obligation, it is a general suretyship. A surety in a general suretyship may refuse to bear suretyship liability to the creditor before the dispute on the principal contract is adjudicated or arbitrated and the debtor's property has been subjected to compulsory enforcement but still fails to perform the obligation, unless it falls under any of the following circumstances: (1) the debtor's whereabouts are unknown and there is no property available for enforcement; (2) a People's Court has accepted a bankruptcy case of the debtor; (3) the creditor has evidence proving that the debtor's property is insufficient to perform all the obligations or that the debtor has lost the ability to perform the obligation; (4) the surety has waived in writing the right provided in this paragraph.

Article 688 Where the parties agree in the suretyship contract that the surety and the debtor shall bear joint and several liability for the obligation, it is a joint and several suretyship. Where the debtor in a joint and several suretyship fails to perform the due obligation or when the circumstances agreed upon by the parties occur, the creditor may request the debtor to perform the obligation, and may also request the surety to bear suretyship liability within its suretyship scope.
Article 689 A surety may require the debtor to provide counter-suretyship.

Article 690 The surety and the creditor may negotiate to conclude a contract for a maximum amount suretyship, agreeing that the surety shall provide suretyship for claims continuously arising within a certain period up to a maximum amount of claim. For a maximum amount suretyship, in addition to the application of the provisions of this Chapter, the relevant provisions on maximum amount mortgage in Book II of this Code shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 691 The scope of suretyship includes the principal claim and its interest, liquidated damages, damages for loss, and the expenses for enforcing the claim. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 692 The suretyship period is the period during which the surety's suretyship liability is determined, and it shall not be suspended, interrupted, or extended. The creditor and the surety may agree on the suretyship period. However, if the agreed suretyship period expires earlier than or on the same date as the performance period of the principal obligation, it shall be deemed as no agreement; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the suretyship period shall be six months from the date when the performance period of the principal obligation expires. If the creditor and the debtor have no agreement or the agreement is unclear on the performance period of the principal obligation, the suretyship period shall be calculated from the date when the grace period for the debtor to perform the obligation requested by the creditor expires.

Article 693 If a creditor in a general suretyship fails to file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration against the debtor within the suretyship period, the surety shall no longer bear suretyship liability. If a creditor in a joint and several suretyship fails to request the surety to bear suretyship liability within the suretyship period, the surety shall no longer bear suretyship liability.

Article 694 Where a creditor in a general suretyship files a lawsuit or applies for arbitration against the debtor before the expiration of the suretyship period, the statute of limitations for the suretyship obligation shall begin to run from the date when the surety's right to refuse to bear suretyship liability is extinguished. Where a creditor in a joint and several suretyship requests the surety to bear suretyship liability before the expiration of the suretyship period, the statute of limitations for the suretyship obligation shall begin to run from the date when the creditor requests the surety to bear suretyship liability.

Article 695 Where the creditor and the debtor, without the written consent of the surety, negotiate to modify the content of the principal obligatory contract, if the obligation is reduced, the surety shall still bear suretyship liability for the modified obligation; if the obligation is increased, the surety shall not bear suretyship liability for the increased part. Where the creditor and the debtor modify the performance period of the principal obligatory contract without the written consent of the surety, the suretyship period shall not be affected.

Article 696 Where the creditor transfers all or part of the claim without notifying the surety, such transfer shall not be effective against the surety. Where the surety and the creditor have agreed to prohibit the transfer of the claim, and the creditor transfers the claim without the written consent of the surety, the surety shall no longer bear suretyship liability to the transferee.

Article 697 Where the creditor, without the written consent of the surety, allows the debtor to transfer all or part of the obligation, the surety shall no longer bear suretyship liability for the transferred obligation unless otherwise agreed between the creditor and the surety. Where a third party joins the obligation, the surety's suretyship liability shall not be affected.

Article 698 After the performance period of the principal obligation expires, if a surety in a general suretyship provides the creditor with truthful information about the debtor's property available for enforcement, and the creditor waives or fails to exercise its rights, resulting in the inability to enforce such property, the surety shall no longer bear suretyship liability to the extent of the value of the property available for enforcement provided.

Article 699 Where there are two or more sureties for the same obligation, the sureties shall bear suretyship liability in accordance with the suretyship share agreed upon in the suretyship contract. If there is no agreement on the suretyship share, the creditor may request any surety to bear suretyship liability within its suretyship scope.

Article 700 After bearing suretyship liability, the surety shall have the right to seek recourse against the debtor within the scope of the suretyship liability it has borne and shall be subrogated to the rights of the creditor against the debtor, unless otherwise agreed by the parties; however, it shall not harm the interests of the creditor.

Article 701 A surety may assert against the creditor any defense that the debtor has against the creditor. If the debtor waives such defense, the surety shall still have the right to assert that defense against the creditor.
Article 702 If the debtor has a right of set-off or a right of revocation against the creditor, the surety may refuse to bear the suretyship liability within the corresponding scope.
Article 703 A lease contract is a contract whereby the lessor delivers the leased property to the lessee for use and enjoyment, and the lessee pays rent.

Article 704 The contents of a lease contract generally include clauses such as the name, quantity, and purpose of the leased property, the lease term, the rent and its payment term and method, and the maintenance of the leased property.

Article 705 The lease term shall not exceed twenty years. Where it exceeds twenty years, the excess part shall be void. Upon expiration of the lease term, the parties may renew the lease contract; provided that the agreed lease term shall not exceed twenty years from the date of renewal.

Article 706 Failure by the parties to go through the registration and filing procedures for a lease contract as required by laws or administrative regulations shall not affect the validity of the contract.

Article 707 Where the lease term is six months or more, a written form shall be adopted. If the parties fail to adopt a written form and the lease term cannot be determined, the lease shall be deemed to be one with an indefinite term.
Article 708 The lessor shall deliver the leased property to the lessee as agreed and shall, during the lease term, keep the leased property suitable for the agreed purpose.

Article 709 The lessee shall use the leased property in the agreed manner. Where the manner of use of the leased property is not agreed upon or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined pursuant to Article 510 of this Law, the lessee shall use the leased property in accordance with its nature.

Article 710 Where the lessee uses the leased property in the agreed manner or in accordance with its nature, causing wear and tear to the leased property, the lessee shall not bear compensation liability.

Article 711 Where the lessee fails to use the leased property in the agreed manner or in accordance with its nature, causing damage to the leased property, the lessor may dissolve the contract and claim compensation for losses.
Article 712 The lessor shall perform the obligation to maintain the leased property, unless the parties agree otherwise.

Article 713 Where the leased property requires maintenance, the lessee may request the lessor to carry out the maintenance within a reasonable period. If the lessor fails to perform the maintenance obligation, the lessee may carry out the maintenance themselves, and the maintenance expenses shall be borne by the lessor. Where the maintenance of the leased property affects the lessee's use, the rent shall be reduced accordingly or the lease term shall be extended. Where the leased property requires maintenance due to the lessee's fault, the lessor shall not bear the maintenance obligation as provided in the preceding paragraph.
Article 714 The lessee shall take good care of the leased property. Where the leased property is damaged or destroyed due to improper care, the lessee shall bear compensation liability.

Article 715 With the consent of the lessor, the lessee may make improvements to or add ancillary items to the leased property. Where the lessee makes improvements to or adds ancillary items to the leased property without the consent of the lessor, the lessor may request the lessee to restore the property to its original condition or compensate for the losses.

Article 716 With the consent of the lessor, the lessee may sublease the leased property to a third party. Where the lessee subleases the property, the lease contract between the lessee and the lessor shall remain valid; if the third party causes damage to the leased property, the lessee shall compensate for the losses. Where the lessee subleases the property without the consent of the lessor, the lessor may dissolve the contract.

Article 717 Where the lessee, with the consent of the lessor, subleases the leased property to a third party, and the sublease term exceeds the remaining lease term of the lessee, the agreement on the excess part shall not be legally binding on the lessor, unless the lessor and the lessee agree otherwise.

Article 718 If the lessor knows or should have known that the lessee has subleased the property but fails to raise an objection within six months, the lessor shall be deemed to have consented to the sublease.

Article 719 Where the lessee is in arrears with rent, the sub-lessee may pay the overdue rent and liquidated damages on behalf of the lessee, unless the sublease contract is not legally binding on the lessor. The rent and liquidated damages paid by the sub-lessee on behalf of the lessee may be set off against the rent payable by the sub-lessee to the lessee; any amount exceeding the rent payable by the sub-lessee may be recovered from the lessee.
Article 720 Income derived from the possession or use of the leased property during the lease term shall belong to the lessee, unless the parties agree otherwise.

Article 721 The lessee shall pay the rent within the agreed period. Where the period for payment of rent is not agreed or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, if the lease term is less than one year, the rent shall be paid at the expiration of the lease term; if the lease term is one year or more, the rent shall be paid at the expiration of each year, and if the remaining term is less than one year, the rent shall be paid at the expiration of the lease term.

Article 722 Where the lessee fails to pay or delays payment of the rent without a justifiable reason, the lessor may request the lessee to pay within a reasonable period; if the lessee still fails to pay beyond the specified period, the lessor may dissolve the contract.

Article 723 Where a third party claims a right, thereby preventing the lessee from using and deriving benefits from the leased property, the lessee may request a reduction of or exemption from the rent. Where a third party claims a right, the lessee shall promptly notify the lessor.

Article 724 Under any of the following circumstances, where the leased property cannot be used due to reasons not attributable to the lessee, the lessee may dissolve the contract: (1) the leased property is sealed up or seized by a judicial organ or an administrative organ according to law; (2) there is a dispute over the ownership of the leased property; or (3) the leased property violates the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations regarding conditions for use.

Article 725 Where the ownership of the leased property changes during the period in which the lessee possesses it in accordance with the lease contract, the validity of the lease contract shall not be affected.

Article 726 Where the lessor sells the leased house, it shall notify the lessee within a reasonable period prior to the sale, and the lessee shall have the preemptive right to purchase the house under the same conditions; except where a co-owner by shares of the house exercises the preemptive right or the lessor sells the house to a close relative. After the lessor fulfills the obligation of notification, if the lessee fails to expressly indicate its intention to purchase within fifteen days, the lessee shall be deemed to have waived the preemptive right.

Article 727 Where the lessor entrusts an auctioneer to auction the leased house, the lessor shall notify the lessee five days prior to the auction. If the lessee does not participate in the auction, the lessee shall be deemed to have waived the preemptive right.

Article 728 Where the lessor fails to notify the lessee or has other circumstances that hinder the lessee from exercising the preemptive right, the lessee may request the lessor to bear compensation liability. However, the validity of the house sale contract concluded between the lessor and a third party shall not be affected.

Article 729 Where the leased property is partially or totally damaged or lost due to a cause not attributable to the lessee, the lessee may request a reduction of or exemption from the rent; where the purpose of the contract cannot be achieved due to such partial or total damage or loss of the leased property, the lessee may dissolve the contract.

Article 730 Where the parties do not agree on the lease term or the agreement is unclear, and the term cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the lease shall be deemed to be for an indefinite term; either party may dissolve the contract at any time, provided that it shall notify the other party within a reasonable period in advance.

Article 731 Where the leased property endangers the safety or health of the lessee, the lessee may dissolve the contract at any time, even if the lessee knew at the time of concluding the contract that the leased property was of defective quality.
Article 732 Where the lessee dies during the lease term of the house, the persons who lived with the lessee or the co-operators may lease the house in accordance with the original lease contract.

Article 733 Upon expiration of the lease term, the lessee shall return the leased property. The returned leased property shall be in a condition consistent with its use in accordance with the agreement or the nature of the leased property.

Article 734 Upon expiration of the lease term, if the lessee continues to use the leased property and the lessor does not object, the original lease contract shall continue to be valid, but the lease term shall be for an indefinite period. Upon expiration of the lease term, the lessee of a house shall have a preemptive right to lease the house under the same conditions.

Article 735 A financial lease contract is a contract in which the lessor, based on the lessee's choice of the seller and the leased property, purchases the leased property from the seller and provides it to the lessee for use, and the lessee pays rent.

Article 736 The contents of a financial lease contract shall generally include clauses such as the name, quantity, specifications, technical performance, and inspection method of the leased property, the lease term, the composition of the rent and its payment period, method, and currency, and the ownership of the leased property upon expiration of the lease term. A financial lease contract shall be in written form.
Article 737 A financial lease contract concluded by the parties through fabricating the leased property shall be void.

Article 738 Where an administrative license shall be obtained for the operation and use of the leased property in accordance with the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, the lessor's failure to obtain such administrative license shall not affect the validity of the financial lease contract.

Article 739 Where the lessor concludes a sales contract based on the lessee's choice of the seller and the leased property, the seller shall deliver the subject matter to the lessee in accordance with the agreement, and the lessee shall enjoy the rights of a buyer relating to the acceptance of the subject matter.

Article 740 Where the seller breaches its obligation to deliver the subject matter to the lessee, and under any of the following circumstances, the lessee may refuse to accept the subject matter delivered by the seller: (1) the subject matter seriously fails to conform to the agreement; or (2) the subject matter is not delivered in accordance with the agreement, and is still not delivered within a reasonable period after the lessee or the lessor has given notice requesting delivery. Where the lessee refuses to accept the subject matter, the lessee shall promptly notify the lessor.

Article 741 The lessor, the seller and the lessee may agree that, if the seller fails to perform its obligations under the sales contract, the lessee shall have the right to claim. Where the lessee exercises its right to claim, the lessor shall assist.

Article 742 The lessee's exercise of the right to claim against the seller shall not affect its obligation to pay the rent. However, where the lessee has relied on the lessor's expertise in determining the leased object or the lessor has interfered in the selection of the leased object, the lessee may request a reduction or exemption of the corresponding rent.

Article 743 Where the lessor falls under any of the following circumstances, causing the lessee's failure to exercise the right to claim against the seller, the lessee shall have the right to request that the lessor bear the corresponding liability: (1) it knows of a quality defect in the leased object but fails to inform the lessee; (2) it fails to provide necessary assistance in a timely manner when the lessee exercises the right to claim. Where the lessor neglects to exercise the right to claim which may only be exercised by it against the seller, causing losses to the lessee, the lessee shall have the right to request that the lessor bear compensation liability.

Article 744 For a sales contract concluded by the lessor based on the lessee's selection of the seller and the leased object, the lessor may not modify the content of the contract related to the lessee without the lessee's consent.
Article 745 The lessor's ownership of the leased object shall not be set up against a bona fide third party if not registered.

Article 746 The rent under a financial leasing contract shall be determined based on most or all of the cost of purchasing the leased object and the lessor's reasonable profit, unless the parties agree otherwise.

Article 747 The lessor shall not be liable if the leased object does not conform to the agreement or is not fit for the purpose of use, unless the lessee has relied on the lessor's expertise in determining the leased object or the lessor has interfered in the selection of the leased object.

Article 748 The lessor shall ensure the lessee's possession and use of the leased object. Where the lessor falls under any of the following circumstances, the lessee shall have the right to request compensation for its losses: (1) it withdraws the leased object without justifiable grounds; (2) it obstructs or interferes with the lessee's possession and use of the leased object without justifiable grounds; (3) it causes a third party to assert a right over the leased object due to the lessor's reasons; (4) any other circumstance that improperly affects the lessee's possession and use of the leased object.

Article 749 Where, during the period of the lessee's possession of the leased object, the leased object causes personal injury or property damage to a third party, the lessor shall not bear liability.
Article 750 The lessee shall take good care of and use the leased object. The lessee shall perform the obligation of maintenance during the period of its possession of the leased object.

Article 751 Where the leased object is damaged or lost during the period of the lessee's possession, the lessor shall have the right to request the lessee to continue paying the rent, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties.

Article 752 The lessee shall pay the rent as agreed. Where the lessee still fails to pay the rent within a reasonable period after being demanded, the lessor may request payment of all the rent; or it may dissolve the contract and take back the leased object.

Article 753 Where the lessee transfers, mortgages, pledges, contributes as capital investment, or otherwise disposes of the leased object without the lessor's consent, the lessor may dissolve the financial leasing contract.

Article 754 Under any of the following circumstances, the lessor or the lessee may dissolve the financial leasing contract: (1) the sales contract concluded between the lessor and the seller is dissolved, confirmed as void, or revoked, and a new sales contract cannot be concluded; (2) the leased object is damaged or lost due to reasons not attributable to the parties, and it cannot be repaired or a substitute cannot be determined; (3) the purpose of the financial leasing contract cannot be achieved due to the seller's reasons.

Article 755 Where a financial leasing contract is dissolved due to the dissolution, confirmation as void, or revocation of the sales contract, and the seller and the leased object were selected by the lessee, the lessor shall have the right to request the lessee to compensate for corresponding losses; except where the dissolution, confirmation as void, or revocation of the sales contract is caused by the lessor's reasons. Where the lessor's losses have already been compensated upon the dissolution, confirmation as void, or revocation of the sales contract, the lessee shall no longer bear the corresponding compensation liability.

Article 756 Where a financial leasing contract is dissolved due to reasons not attributable to the parties, such as accidental damage or loss of the leased object after its delivery to the lessee, the lessor may request the lessee to provide compensation based on the depreciation of the leased object.

Article 757 The lessor and the lessee may agree on the ownership of the leased object upon the expiry of the lease term; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and under Article 510 of this Law it still cannot be determined, the ownership of the leased object shall vest in the lessor.

Article 758 Where the parties agree that the leased object shall belong to the lessee upon the expiry of the lease term, and the lessee has paid most of the rent but is unable to pay the remaining rent, and the lessor therefore dissolves the contract and takes back the leased object, if the value of the leased object taken back exceeds the rent and other expenses in arrears by the lessee, the lessee may request the corresponding return. Where the parties agree that the leased object shall belong to the lessor upon the expiry of the lease term, and the lessee is unable to return the leased object due to its damage, loss, or attachment to or mixture with another object, the lessor shall have the right to request the lessee to provide reasonable compensation.

Article 759 Where the parties agree that, upon the expiry of the lease term, the lessee only needs to pay a nominal price to the lessor, the ownership of the leased object shall be deemed to vest in the lessee after the agreed rent obligations are performed.

Article 760 Where a financial leasing contract is void, and the parties have agreed on the ownership of the leased object under such circumstance, such agreement shall prevail; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the leased object shall be returned to the lessor. However, if the contract is void due to the lessee's reasons, and the lessor does not request the return, or the return would significantly reduce the utility of the leased object, the ownership of the leased object shall vest in the lessee, and the lessee shall provide reasonable compensation to the lessor.

Article 761 A factoring contract is a contract under which an accounts receivable creditor assigns its existing or future accounts receivable to a factor, and the factor provides services such as financing, management or collection of accounts receivable, or guarantee of payment by the accounts receivable debtor.

Article 762 The contents of a factoring contract generally include clauses such as the business type, scope of services, term of services, underlying transaction contract information, accounts receivable information, factoring financing funds or service remuneration, and the payment method thereof. A factoring contract shall be in writing.

Article 763 Where the accounts receivable creditor and debtor fabricate accounts receivable as the subject of assignment and enter into a factoring contract with the factor, the accounts receivable debtor may not oppose the factor on the ground that the accounts receivable do not exist, unless the factor knew of the fabrication.

Article 764 Where the factor issues a notice of assignment of accounts receivable to the accounts receivable debtor, the factor shall indicate its status and attach the necessary supporting documents.

Article 765 After the accounts receivable debtor receives the notice of assignment of accounts receivable, if the accounts receivable creditor and debtor, without justifiable cause, negotiate to modify or terminate the underlying transaction contract to the detriment of the factor, such modification or termination shall not be effective against the factor.

Article 766 Where the parties agree on factoring with recourse, the factor may claim against the accounts receivable creditor for repayment of the principal and interest of the factoring financing funds or repurchase of the accounts receivable, or may claim against the accounts receivable debtor for the accounts receivable. If, after the factor claims against the accounts receivable debtor for the accounts receivable, a surplus remains after deducting the principal and interest of the factoring financing funds and relevant expenses, the surplus shall be returned to the accounts receivable creditor.

Article 767 Where the parties agree on factoring without recourse, the factor shall claim against the accounts receivable debtor for the accounts receivable, and the factor may retain any amount exceeding the principal and interest of the factoring financing funds and relevant expenses without the need to return it to the accounts receivable creditor.

Article 768 Where the accounts receivable creditor enters into multiple factoring contracts with respect to the same accounts receivable, causing multiple factors to claim rights, the factor that has registered shall obtain the accounts receivable before those that have not registered; if all have registered, the factors shall obtain the accounts receivable in the order of registration time; if none has registered, the factor named in the notice of assignment that first reaches the accounts receivable debtor shall obtain the accounts receivable; if there is neither registration nor notice, the factors shall obtain the accounts receivable in proportion to the factoring financing funds or service remuneration.
Article 769 Matters not provided for in this Chapter are governed by the relevant provisions on the assignment of claims in Chapter 6 of this Book.

Article 770 A work contract is a contract under which the contractor, in accordance with the requirements of the client, completes a task and delivers the results of the work, and the client pays remuneration. Work contracting includes processing, customizing, repairing, reproducing, testing, inspecting, and similar tasks.

Article 771 The contents of a work contract generally include clauses such as the subject matter, quantity, quality, and remuneration of the work; the method of work contracting; the provision of materials; the performance period; and the standards and methods for acceptance inspection.

Article 772 The contractor shall complete the principal work with its own equipment, technology, and labor, unless otherwise agreed by the parties. Where the contractor entrusts the principal work to a third party for completion, the contractor shall be liable to the client for the work results completed by that third party; if the client does not consent, the client may rescind the contract.

Article 773 The contractor may entrust auxiliary tasks of the contracted work to a third party for completion. Where the contractor entrusts auxiliary tasks to a third party for completion, the contractor shall be liable to the client for the work results completed by that third party.
Article 774 Where materials are provided by the contractor, the contractor shall select materials as agreed and shall submit them to the client for inspection.

Article 775 Where materials are provided by the client, the client shall provide the materials as agreed. The contractor shall promptly inspect the materials provided by the client; if they are found not to conform to the agreement, the contractor shall promptly notify the client to replace, supplement, or take other remedial measures. The contractor shall not, without authorization, replace the materials provided by the client, nor replace parts that do not require repair.

Article 776 Where the contractor discovers that the drawings or technical requirements provided by the client are unreasonable, it shall promptly notify the client. If the client causes losses to the contractor by failing to reply promptly or for other reasons, the client shall compensate for such losses.
Article 777 If the client changes the requirements of the work in progress, causing losses to the contractor, the client shall compensate for such losses.

Article 778 Where the work requires the assistance of the client, the client has the obligation to provide such assistance. If the client fails to perform its duty of assistance so that the work cannot be completed, the contractor may urge the client to perform its obligation within a reasonable period and may extend the performance period; if the client fails to perform within the extended period, the contractor may rescind the contract.

Article 779 During the period of work, the contractor shall submit to necessary supervision and inspection by the client. The client shall not, by exercising supervision and inspection, hinder the normal work of the contractor.

Article 780 Upon completion of the work, the contractor shall deliver the work results to the client and submit the necessary technical documents and relevant quality certifications. The client shall accept the work results.

Article 781 Where the work result delivered by the contractor fails to meet the quality requirements, the ordering party may, within a reasonable scope, choose to request the contractor to bear liability for breach of contract by means of repair, rework, reduction of remuneration, or compensation for losses.

Article 782 The ordering party shall pay the remuneration within the agreed time limit. Where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear on the time limit for payment of remuneration, and it still cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, the ordering party shall pay the remuneration when the contractor delivers the work result; where the work result is partially delivered, the ordering party shall make a corresponding payment.

Article 783 Where the ordering party fails to pay the contractor the remuneration or equivalent material costs, the contractor shall have a lien over the completed work result or the right to refuse delivery, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 784 The contractor shall properly keep the materials supplied by the ordering party and the completed work result. Where such materials or work result are damaged or lost due to improper storage, the contractor shall bear compensation liability.

Article 785 The contractor shall keep secrets in accordance with the requirements of the ordering party and shall not retain reproductions or technical materials without the permission of the ordering party.
Article 786 Co-contractors shall bear joint and several liability to the ordering party, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 787 The ordering party may dissolve the contract at any time before the contractor completes the work. Where losses are caused to the contractor, the ordering party shall compensate for such losses.

Article 788 A construction project contract is a contract under which the contractor carries out the construction of a project and the owner pays the price. Construction project contracts include contracts for geotechnical engineering, design, and construction.
Article 789 A construction project contract shall be concluded in writing.
Article 790 Bidding activities for construction projects shall be conducted openly, fairly, and impartially in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws.

Article 791 The owner may enter into a construction project contract with a general contractor, or may enter into separate contracts for geotechnical engineering, design, and construction with a geotechnical engineer, a designer, and a constructor respectively. The owner shall not split a construction project that shall be completed by one contractor into several parts and award them to several contractors. With the consent of the owner, a general contractor, or a geotechnical engineer, designer, or constructor may assign part of the contracted work to a third party. The third party shall bear joint and several liability to the owner together with the general contractor or the geotechnical engineer, designer, or constructor for the work result completed by it. A contractor shall not subcontract the entire contracted construction project to a third party, nor shall it split the entire contracted construction project and then subcontract it separately to third parties in the name of subcontracting. It is prohibited for a contractor to subcontract the project to a unit that does not possess the corresponding qualifications. It is prohibited for the subcontracting unit to further subcontract the project it has contracted. The construction of the main structure of a construction project must be completed by the contractor itself.

Article 792 A contract for a major national construction project shall be concluded in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the State and with documents such as the investment plan and feasibility study report approved by the State.

Article 793 Where a construction project construction contract is void, but the construction project is accepted as conforming to the standards, the contractor may be compensated by a discounted amount with reference to the agreement on the project price as stipulated in the contract. Where a construction project construction contract is void and the construction project is accepted as not conforming to the standards, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the following circumstances: (1) If the repaired construction project is accepted as conforming to the standards, the owner may request the contractor to bear the repair costs; (2) If the repaired construction project is accepted as not conforming to the standards, the contractor shall have no right to request compensation by a discounted amount with reference to the agreement on the project price as stipulated in the contract. If the owner is at fault for the losses caused by the non-conforming construction project, it shall bear corresponding liability.

Article 794 The content of geotechnical engineering and design contracts generally includes terms such as the time limit for submitting relevant basic data and documents including budgets and estimates, quality requirements, fees, and other collaboration conditions.

Article 795 The content of a construction contract generally includes terms such as the scope of the project, construction period, start and completion times for intermediate handover works, project quality, project cost, time for delivery of technical materials, responsibility for supply of materials and equipment, allocation and settlement, completion acceptance, scope of quality warranty and warranty period, and mutual collaboration.

Article 796 Where a project supervisor is engaged for a construction project, the owner shall conclude a commission contract for supervision with the supervisor in writing. The rights, obligations, and legal liabilities of the owner and the supervisor shall be governed by the provisions of this Book on commission contracts and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Article 797 The owner may at any time, without hindering the normal operation of the contractor, inspect the progress and quality of the work.

Article 798 Before a concealed work is covered, the contractor shall notify the owner for inspection. If the owner fails to conduct the inspection in a timely manner, the contractor may extend the project period and shall have the right to request compensation for losses such as from work stoppage or idle labor.

Article 799 After a construction project is completed, the owner shall timely carry out acceptance in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications, the construction acceptance norms and quality inspection standards issued by the State. If the acceptance is passed, the owner shall pay the price as agreed and take over the construction project. A construction project may be delivered for use only after it has been accepted as conforming to the standards upon completion; a project that has not been accepted or has been accepted as not conforming to the standards shall not be delivered for use.

Article 800 Where the quality of geotechnical engineering or design fails to meet the requirements, or the submission of geotechnical engineering or design documents is delayed beyond the time limit, thereby causing losses to the owner, the geotechnical engineer or designer shall continue to improve the geotechnical engineering or design, reduce or waive the geotechnical engineering or design fees, and compensate for the losses.

Article 801 Where the quality of a construction project fails to meet the agreement due to the cause of the builder, the employer shall have the right to request the builder to repair, rework, or reconstruct without charge within a reasonable period. Where delayed delivery results after repair, rework, or reconstruction, the builder shall bear liability for breach of contract.

Article 802 Where a construction project causes personal injury or property loss within its reasonable service life due to the cause of the contractor, the contractor shall bear compensation liability.

Article 803 Where the employer fails to provide raw materials, equipment, site, funds, or technical data at the time and in the manner agreed upon, the contractor may extend the project period and shall have the right to claim compensation for losses such as work stoppage and idling of workers.

Article 804 Where the construction of a project is suspended or postponed midway due to the cause of the employer, the employer shall take measures to compensate for or mitigate the losses, and compensate the contractor for losses and actual expenses incurred thereby, including work stoppage, idling of workers, relocation, removal and relocation of machinery and equipment, and overstock of materials and components.

Article 805 Where the employer changes the plan, provides inaccurate data, or fails to provide the necessary surveying and designing work conditions within the time limit, thereby causing rework, suspension, or modification of the surveying and design, the employer shall pay additional fees based on the actual workload consumed by the surveyor or designer.

Article 806 Where the contractor subcontracts or illegally subcontracts a construction project, the employer may dissolve the contract. Where the employer provides main construction materials, building components and fittings, or equipment that do not meet mandatory standards, or fails to perform the obligation of assistance, making it impossible for the contractor to carry out the construction, and fails to perform the corresponding obligations within a reasonable period after receiving a reminder, the contractor may dissolve the contract. After the contract is dissolved, if the quality of the completed construction project is up to standard, the employer shall pay the corresponding project price in accordance with the agreement; if the quality of the completed construction project is not up to standard, Article 793 of this Law shall apply.

Article 807 Where the employer fails to pay the price in accordance with the agreement, the contractor may remind the employer to pay the price within a reasonable period. If the employer fails to pay within the extended period, unless the nature of the construction project is unsuitable for price reduction or auction, the contractor may negotiate with the employer for a price reduction of the project, or may request the People's Court to auction the project according to law. The price paid for the construction project shall be satisfied on a priority basis from the proceeds of the price reduction or auction of the project.
Article 808 Matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be governed by the relevant provisions on work contracts.

Article 809 A transport contract is a contract under which the carrier transports passengers or cargo from the place of departure to the agreed place, and the passenger, shipper, or consignee pays the fare or shipping charges.
Article 810 A carrier engaged in public transport shall not refuse the usual and reasonable transport requests made by passengers or shippers.
Article 811 The carrier shall transport passengers or cargo safely to the agreed place within the agreed period or a reasonable period.
Article 812 The carrier shall transport passengers or cargo to the agreed place via the agreed or usual transport route.

Article 813 The passenger, shipper, or consignee shall pay the fare or shipping charges. Where the carrier increases the fare or shipping charges by failing to transport via the agreed or usual route, the passenger, shipper, or consignee may refuse to pay the increased portion of the fare or shipping charges.
Article 814 A passenger transport contract is formed when the carrier issues a ticket to the passenger, except where the parties have agreed otherwise or where there is a different trade practice.

Article 815 A passenger shall board the vehicle at the time, on the run, and by the seat number indicated on the valid ticket. If a passenger rides without a ticket, travels beyond the paid distance, upgrades their class, or holds a discounted ticket that does not meet the conditions for price reduction, the passenger shall make up the fare, and the carrier may charge an additional fare in accordance with the regulations; if the passenger fails to pay the fare, the carrier may refuse to transport them. If a passenger under a real-name passenger transport contract loses their ticket, they may request the carrier to report the loss and reissue the ticket, and the carrier shall not charge the fare again or impose any other unreasonable fees.

Article 816 If a passenger cannot board at the time indicated on the ticket due to their own reasons, they shall go through the procedures for refund or change within the agreed period; if they go through the procedures beyond the period, the carrier may refuse to refund the fare and shall no longer be obliged to provide transport.

Article 817 The hand luggage a passenger carries shall comply with the agreed limits on quantity and category; if the hand luggage exceeds the limits or violates the category requirements, the passenger shall go through the check-in procedures.

Article 818 A passenger shall not carry in person or smuggle in their baggage any dangerous or prohibited articles that are flammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, radioactive, or may endanger human life or property on the means of transport. If a passenger violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the carrier may unload, destroy, or deliver the dangerous or prohibited articles to the relevant authorities. If a passenger insists on carrying or smuggling dangerous or prohibited articles, the carrier shall refuse to transport them.

Article 819 The carrier shall strictly perform the obligation of safe transport and promptly inform passengers of matters to be noted for safe transport. Passengers shall actively assist and cooperate with the reasonable arrangements made by the carrier for safe transport.

Article 820 The carrier shall transport passengers at the time, by the run, and to the seat number indicated on the valid ticket. If the carrier delays transport or is otherwise unable to provide normal transport, it shall promptly inform and remind passengers, take necessary accommodation measures, and arrange transfer to another run or a refund in accordance with the passenger's request; if passengers suffer losses as a result, the carrier shall bear compensation liability, unless the cause is not attributable to the carrier.

Article 821 Where a carrier lowers its service standard without authorization, it shall, upon the request of a passenger, refund the fare or reduce the fare; where it raises its service standard, it shall not increase the fare.
Article 822 During the carriage, the carrier shall use its best efforts to assist passengers who suffer from acute diseases, are giving birth, or are in danger.

Article 823 The carrier shall bear compensation liability for the death of or injury to any passenger occurring in the course of carriage, unless the death or injury is caused by the passenger’s own health condition, or the carrier proves that the death or injury is caused by the passenger’s intentional act or gross negligence. The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply to passengers who, under relevant regulations, are exempt from tickets, hold concession tickets, or travel without a ticket with the carrier’s permission.

Article 824 Where any article carried by a passenger is damaged or lost during the carriage, the carrier shall bear compensation liability if the carrier is at fault. Where any checked luggage of a passenger is damaged or lost, the relevant provisions on the carriage of goods shall apply.

Article 825 When handling the carriage of goods, the consignor shall accurately inform the carrier of the name or title of the consignee, or the consignee upon instructions, as well as the name, nature, weight, quantity, place of receipt, and other necessary information concerning the carriage of goods. Where the carrier suffers any loss due to the consignor’s false declaration or omission of material information, the consignor shall bear compensation liability.
Article 826 Where the carriage of goods requires formalities such as approval or inspection, the consignor shall submit the documents evidencing completion of such formalities to the carrier.

Article 827 The consignor shall package the goods in the agreed manner. Where there is no agreement on the packaging manner or the agreement is unclear, the provisions of Article 619 of this Law shall apply. If the consignor violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the carrier may refuse to carry the goods.

Article 828 Where a consignor consigns dangerous goods such as flammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, or radioactive articles, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State on the carriage of dangerous goods, properly package the dangerous goods, affix warning signs and labels, and submit to the carrier written materials regarding the name, nature, and preventive measures of the dangerous goods. If the consignor violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the carrier may refuse to carry the goods, or may take corresponding measures to avoid the occurrence of loss, and any expenses incurred thereby shall be borne by the consignor.

Article 829 Before the carrier delivers the goods to the consignee, the consignor may request the carrier to suspend the carriage, return the goods, change the place of destination, or deliver the goods to another consignee, provided that the consignor shall compensate the carrier for any loss suffered thereby.

Article 830 After the arrival of the goods at the place of destination, if the carrier knows the consignee, it shall promptly notify the consignee, and the consignee shall promptly take delivery of the goods. If the consignee delays in taking delivery, it shall pay the carrier such expenses as storage fees.

Article 831 When taking delivery, the consignee shall inspect the goods within the agreed time limit. If no time limit for inspection is agreed upon or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the inspection shall be conducted within a reasonable time limit. If the consignee raises no objection to the quantity or damage of the goods within the agreed time limit or a reasonable time limit, it shall be deemed as prima facie evidence that the carrier has delivered the goods as recorded in the transport documents.

Article 832 The carrier shall bear compensation liability for the damage to or loss of goods occurring during the carriage. However, the carrier shall not bear compensation liability if it proves that the damage to or loss of the goods is caused by force majeure, the inherent nature of the goods, reasonable depletion, or the fault of the consignor or the consignee.

Article 833 The amount of compensation for the damage to or loss of goods shall be calculated in accordance with the agreement of the parties; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, it shall be calculated based on the market price at the place of destination at the time of delivery or when delivery should have been made. If laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise for the calculation method of the compensation amount or the limit of compensation, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 834 Where two or more carriers engage in successive carriage using the same mode of transport, the carrier that has entered into the contract with the consignor shall be liable for the entire carriage; if the loss occurs in a particular section of the transport, the carrier that has entered into the contract with the consignor and the carrier in that section shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 835 If the goods are lost due to force majeure during carriage and the freight has not been collected, the carrier shall not claim payment of the freight; if the freight has already been collected, the consignor may request its return. If the law provides otherwise, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 836 If the consignor or the consignee fails to pay freight, storage fees, or other expenses, the carrier shall have a lien over the relevant goods in transport, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.
Article 837 If the consignee is unknown or if the consignee refuses to take delivery of the goods without just cause, the carrier may deposit the goods in accordance with law.

Article 838 The multimodal transport operator shall be responsible for performing or arranging the performance of the multimodal transport contract, and shall enjoy the rights and bear the obligations of a carrier with respect to the entire transport.

Article 839 The multimodal transport operator may agree with the carriers of the various sections participating in the multimodal transport on their respective responsibilities regarding the transport of each section under the multimodal transport contract; however, such agreement shall not affect the obligations of the multimodal transport operator in respect of the entire transport.

Article 840 When the multimodal transport operator receives the goods delivered by the consignor, it shall issue a multimodal transport document. At the request of the consignor, the multimodal transport document may be a negotiable document or a non-negotiable document.

Article 841 Where the consignor causes losses to the multi-modal transport operator due to its fault in consigning the goods, the consignor shall still be liable for compensation even if the consignor has already transferred the multi-modal transport document.

Article 842 Where the damage to or loss of the goods occurs during a particular stage of the multi-modal transport, the liability for compensation and the limitation of liability of the multi-modal transport operator shall be governed by the relevant laws regulating the mode of transport for that stage. Where the stage of transport during which the damage to or loss of the goods occurs cannot be determined, the liability for compensation shall be borne in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.
Article 843 A technology contract is a contract concluded by parties to establish their mutual rights and obligations regarding technology development, transfer, licensing, consultation or services.

Article 844 The conclusion of a technology contract shall be conducive to the protection of intellectual property and the advancement of science and technology, and shall promote the research and development, transformation, application and dissemination of scientific and technological achievements.

Article 845 The contents of a technology contract generally include clauses such as the project name, the subject matter's content, scope and requirements, the plan, place and method of performance, the confidentiality of technical information and materials, the attribution of technical achievements and the method of distributing proceeds, the acceptance criteria and methods, and the interpretation of terms and expressions. Technical background materials, feasibility studies and technical evaluation reports, project task statements and plans, technical standards, technical specifications, original designs and process documents, as well as other technical documentation related to the performance of the contract, may be made part of the contract according to the agreement of the parties. Where a technology contract involves a patent, the name of the invention or creation, the patent applicant and patentee, the application date, the application number, the patent number, and the term of validity of the patent right shall be indicated.

Article 846 The method of payment for the price, remuneration or royalty under a technology contract shall be agreed upon by the parties; it may be in the form of a lump sum payment in full, a lump sum payment in installments, or a royalty payment or a royalty payment with an upfront fee. Where royalty payment is agreed upon, the calculation may be based on a certain percentage of the product price, or the newly increased output value, profit or product sales revenue resulting from the implementation of the patent or use of the technical know-how, or may be calculated according to other methods agreed upon. The percentage for royalty payment may be fixed, or increase or decrease on a yearly basis. Where royalty payment is agreed upon, the parties may agree on a method for inspecting the relevant accounting books.

Article 847 Where the right to use and the right to transfer a service-related technological achievement belong to a legal person or unincorporated organization, such legal person or unincorporated organization may conclude a technology contract regarding such service-related technological achievement. Where a legal person or unincorporated organization concludes a technology contract to transfer a service-related technological achievement, the individual who has accomplished the service-related technological achievement shall have the right of first refusal to acquire it under the same conditions. A service-related technological achievement is a technological achievement accomplished in the course of performing the tasks of a legal person or unincorporated organization, or predominantly by utilizing the material and technical conditions of a legal person or unincorporated organization.

Article 848 The right to use and the right to transfer a non-service-related technological achievement belong to the individual who has accomplished the technological achievement, and such individual may conclude a technology contract regarding such non-service-related technological achievement.

Article 849 The individual who has accomplished a technological achievement shall have the right to be identified as the acclaimer of the technological achievement in the relevant documents on the technological achievement and the right to obtain a certificate of honor and a reward.
Article 850 A technology contract that illegally monopolizes technology or infringes upon the technological achievements of others is void.

Article 851 A technology development contract is a contract concluded between parties for the research and development of new technologies, new products, new processes, new varieties or new materials and their systems. Technology development contracts include commissioned development contracts and cooperative development contracts. A technology development contract shall be in writing. A contract concluded between parties for the transformation and implementation of scientific and technological achievements with practical value shall be governed by reference to the relevant provisions on technology development contracts.

Article 852 The commissioning party under a commissioned development contract shall pay the research and development expenses and remuneration, provide technical information, put forward the research and development requirements, complete the matters of collaboration, and accept the research and development results in accordance with the agreement.

Article 853 The research and developer under a commissioned development contract shall formulate and implement the research and development plan, rationally use the research and development funds, complete the research and development work on schedule, deliver the research and development results, provide relevant technical information and necessary technical guidance, and assist the commissioning party in mastering the research and development results in accordance with the agreement.

Article 854 Where a party to a commissioned development contract violates the agreement, causing the research and development work to be stalled, delayed or fail, such party shall bear the liability for breach of contract.

Article 855 The parties to a cooperative development contract shall make investments, including investment in the form of technology, participate in the research and development work with a division of labor, and collaborate and cooperate in the research and development work in accordance with the agreement.

Article 856 Where a party to a cooperative development contract violates the agreement, causing the research and development work to be stalled, delayed or fail, such party shall bear the liability for breach of contract.

Article 857 Where the technology that is the subject matter of a technology development contract has already been made public by another person, rendering the performance of the technology development contract meaningless, any party may rescind the contract.

Article 858 During the performance of a technology development contract, where the research and development fails or partially fails due to insurmountable technical difficulties, the risk shall be borne as agreed by the parties; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, andcannot be determined pursuant to the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, the risk shall be reasonably shared by the parties. Where one party discovers the circumstances specified in the preceding paragraph that may lead to the failure or partial failure of the research and development, it shall promptly notify the other party and take appropriate measures to mitigate the losses; where it fails to promptly notify or take appropriate measures, causing the losses to be aggravated, it shall bear liability for the aggravated losses.

Article 859 For an invention or creation accomplished under a commissioned development contract, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties, the right to apply for a patent belongs to the research and developer. Where the research and developer obtains the patent right, the commissioning party may exploit the patent according to law. Where the research and developer transfers the right to apply for a patent, the commissioning party shall have the right of first refusal to acquire it under the same conditions.

Article 860 For an invention or creation accomplished under a cooperative development contract, the right to apply for a patent belongs to the parties to the cooperative development jointly. Where one party transfers its joint right to apply for a patent, the other parties shall have the right of first refusal to acquire it under the same conditions, unless otherwise agreed by the parties. Where one party to a cooperative development declares its waiver of its joint right to apply for a patent, the other party may apply alone or the other parties may jointly apply, unless otherwise agreed by the parties. Where the applicant obtains the patent right, the party that has waived its right to apply for a patent may exploit the patent free of charge. Where one party to a cooperative development does not agree to apply for a patent, the other party or parties may not apply for a patent.

Article 861 The parties shall agree on the right to use, the right to assign, and the method of distribution of proceeds from the results of technical secrets achieved through commissioned development or cooperative development. Where there is no such agreement or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, before a patent right is granted for the same technical solution, each party shall have the right to use and assign such results. However, the developer in a commissioned development may not assign the research and development results to a third party before delivering the research and development results to the commissioning party.

Article 862 A technology transfer contract is a contract whereby a right holder who lawfully owns technology assigns to another party the relevant rights to an existing specific patent, patent application, or technical secret. A technology license contract is a contract whereby a right holder who lawfully owns technology licenses another party to exploit or use the relevant rights to an existing specific patent or technical secret. The stipulations in a technology transfer contract or a technology license contract regarding the provision of special-purpose equipment or raw materials for exploiting the technology, or the provision of related technical consultation or technical services, shall constitute an integral part of the contract.

Article 863 Technology transfer contracts include contracts for the assignment of patent rights, the assignment of patent application rights, and the assignment of technical secrets. Technology license contracts include contracts for the license to exploit a patent, the license to use a technical secret, and the like. A technology transfer contract or a technology license contract shall be in writing.

Article 864 A technology transfer contract or a technology license contract may stipulate the scope within which the patent is exploited or the technical secret is used, but shall not restrict technological competition or technological development.

Article 865 A patent exploitation license contract shall only be valid during the term of the patent right. After the term of validity of the patent right expires or the patent right is declared invalid, the patentee may not enter into a patent exploitation license contract with any other person in respect of that patent.

Article 866 The licensor under a patent exploitation license contract shall, in accordance with the agreement, license the licensee to exploit the patent, deliver the technical materials related to the exploitation of the patent, and provide necessary technical guidance.

Article 867 The licensee under a patent exploitation license contract shall exploit the patent in accordance with the agreement, may not license any third party other than those agreed upon to exploit the patent, and shall pay the royalty in accordance with the agreement.

Article 868 The assignor under a technical secret assignment contract and the licensor under a technical secret use license contract shall, in accordance with the agreement, provide technical materials, provide technical guidance, guarantee the practicality and reliability of the technology, and bear the obligation of confidentiality. The obligation of confidentiality stipulated in the preceding paragraph shall not restrict the licensor from applying for a patent, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Article 869 The transferee under a technical secret assignment contract and the licensee under a technical secret use license contract shall, in accordance with the agreement, use the technology, pay the assignment fee or royalty, and bear the obligation of confidentiality.

Article 870 The assignor under a technology transfer contract and the licensor under a technology license contract shall guarantee that they are the lawful owner of the technology provided, and shall guarantee that the technology provided is complete, free from error, effective, and capable of achieving the agreed-upon objective.

Article 871 The transferee under a technology transfer contract and the licensee under a technology license contract shall, within the agreed scope and period, bear the obligation of confidentiality with respect to the secret parts of the technology provided by the assignor or licensor that have not been disclosed.

Article 872 Where the licensor fails to license the technology in accordance with the agreement, it shall refund part or all of the royalty and shall bear liability for breach of contract; where the licensor exploits the patent or uses the technical secret beyond the agreed scope, or in violation of the agreement, licenses a third party to exploit the patent or use the technical secret without authorization, it shall cease the breaching act and bear liability for breach of contract; where the licensor violates the agreed obligation of confidentiality, it shall bear liability for breach of contract. The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis to the assignor's liability for breach of contract.

Article 873 Where the licensee fails to pay the royalty in accordance with the agreement, it shall make up the royalty and pay liquidated damages in accordance with the agreement; where it fails to make up the royalty or pay the liquidated damages, it shall cease exploiting the patent or using the technical secret, return the technical materials, and bear liability for breach of contract; where the licensee exploits the patent or uses the technical secret beyond the agreed scope, or, without the consent of the licensor, licenses a third party to exploit the patent or use the technical secret without authorization, it shall cease the breaching act and bear liability for breach of contract; where the licensee violates the agreed obligation of confidentiality, it shall bear liability for breach of contract. The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis to the transferee's liability for breach of contract.

Article 874 Where the transferee or licensee, in exploiting the patent or using the technical secret in accordance with the agreement, infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of another person, the assignor or licensor shall bear liability, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Article 875 The parties may stipulate in the contract the method of sharing the technical results subsequently improved upon the exploitation of the patent or the use of the technical secret in accordance with the principle of mutual benefit. Where there is no such agreement or the agreement is unclear, and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the other parties shall have no right to share the technical results subsequently improved upon by one party.

Article 876 The assignment and licensing of other intellectual property rights, such as the exclusive right to layout designs of integrated circuits, the right to new plant varieties, and the copyright in computer software, shall be governed by the relevant provisions of this Section by reference.
Article 877 Where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise for technology import and export contracts or contracts for patents or patent applications, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 878 A technical consultation contract is a contract whereby one party uses its technical knowledge to provide the other party with reports on feasibility studies, technical forecasts, special technical investigations, analysis and evaluation, etc., in respect of a specific technical project. A technical service contract is a contract whereby one party uses its technical knowledge to solve a specific technical problem for the other party, but does not include a work contract or a construction project contract.
