Article 879 The commissioning party under a technical consultation contract shall, in accordance with the agreement, clarify the subject matter of the consultation, provide technical background materials and related technical data, accept the work product of the commissioned party, and pay the remuneration.

Article 880 The commissioned party under a technical consultation contract shall complete the consultation report or answer the questions within the agreed time period, and the consultation report submitted shall meet the agreed requirements.

Article 881 If the client of a technology consulting contract fails to provide necessary materials as agreed, which affects the work progress and quality, or fails to accept or accept the work results beyond the agreed time limit, the remuneration paid shall not be recovered, and the unpaid remuneration shall be paid. If the受托人 of a technology consulting contract fails to submit a consulting report on time or submits a consulting report that does not conform to the agreement, it shall bear liability for breach of contract, such as reduction or exemption of remuneration. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the losses caused by the client's decision made in accordance with the consulting report and opinions of the受托人 that comply with the agreed requirements shall be borne by the client.
Article 882 The client of a technical service contract shall provide working conditions as agreed, complete the matters of cooperation, accept the work results, and pay remuneration.
Article 883 The受托人 of a technical service contract shall complete the service items as agreed, solve technical problems, ensure work quality, and impart the knowledge for solving technical problems.

Article 884 If the client of a technical service contract fails to perform the contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, which affects the work progress and quality, or fails to accept or accept the work results beyond the agreed time limit, the remuneration paid shall not be recovered, and the unpaid remuneration shall be paid. If the受托人 of a technical service contract fails to complete the service work as agreed, it shall bear liability for breach of contract, such as exemption from remuneration.

Article 885 During the performance of a technology consulting contract or technical service contract, any new technological achievement completed by the受托人 using the technical materials and working conditions provided by the client shall belong to the受托人. Any new technological achievement completed by the client using the work results of the受托人 shall belong to the client. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 886 If a technology consulting contract or technical service contract has no agreement or the agreement is unclear on the bearing of the expenses necessary for the受托人 to carry out its normal work, such expenses shall be borne by the受托人.
Article 887 If laws or administrative regulations have other provisions on technology intermediary contracts or technology training contracts, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 888 A deposit contract is a contract where the depositary keeps the deposited item delivered by the depositor and returns such item. If a depositor, while engaging in activities such as shopping, dining, or accommodation at the depositary's premises, places items in a designated area, it shall be deemed as a deposit, unless the parties have otherwise agreed or there is a different trade practice.

Article 889 The depositor shall pay the deposit fee to the depositary as agreed. If the parties have no agreement or the agreement on the deposit fee is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, the deposit shall be deemed as gratuitous.
Article 890 A deposit contract shall be formed upon the delivery of the deposited item, unless the parties have otherwise agreed.
Article 891 Where the depositor delivers the deposited item to the depositary, the depositary shall issue a deposit receipt, unless there is a different trade practice.

Article 892 The depositary shall properly keep the deposited item. The parties may agree on the place or method of deposit. Unless in an emergency or for the purpose of protecting the interests of the depositor, the depositary shall not change the place or method of deposit without authorization.

Article 893 If the deposited item delivered by the depositor has defects or requires special deposit measures due to its nature, the depositor shall inform the depositary of the relevant circumstances. If the depositor fails to inform, causing damage to the deposited item, the depositary shall not bear compensation liability. If the depositary suffers losses as a result, the depositor shall bear compensation liability unless the depositary knew or should have known of the situation and failed to take remedial measures.

Article 894 The depositary shall not transfer the deposited item to a third party for deposit, unless the parties have otherwise agreed. If the depositary, in violation of the provisions of the preceding paragraph, transfers the deposited item to a third party for deposit, causing damage to the deposited item, it shall bear compensation liability.
Article 895 The depositary shall not use or permit a third party to use the deposited item, unless the parties have otherwise agreed.

Article 896 If a third party claims a right over the deposited item, the depositary shall perform the obligation to return the deposited item to the depositor, except where property preservation or enforcement measures are taken against the deposited item in accordance with law. If a third party initiates a lawsuit against the depositary or applies for seizure of the deposited item, the depositary shall promptly notify the depositor.

Article 897 Within the deposit period, if the deposited item is damaged or lost due to the depositary's failure to keep it properly, the depositary shall bear compensation liability. However, if a gratuitous depositary proves that it has no intention or gross negligence, it shall not bear compensation liability.

Article 898 If a depositor deposits currency, negotiable securities, or other valuable items, it shall declare this to the depositary, and the depositary shall inspect or seal them. If the depositor fails to make such declaration, the depositary may compensate for the damage or loss of such items as ordinary items.

Article 899 The depositor may retrieve the deposited item at any time. If the parties have no agreement or the agreement on the deposit period is unclear, the depositary may request the depositor to retrieve the deposited item at any time. If a deposit period is agreed, the depositary shall not request the depositor to retrieve the deposited item early unless there are special reasons.
Article 900 When the deposit period expires or the depositor retrieves the deposited item early, the depositary shall return the original item and its fruits to the depositor.

Article 901 Where a depositary keeps currency, it may return the currency of the same type and quantity; where it keeps other fungible items, it may return items of the same type, quality, and quantity in accordance with the agreement.

Article 902 Under a contract of deposit for value, the depositor shall pay the storage fee to the depositary within the agreed time limit. If the time limit for payment is not agreed or the agreement is unclear and cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, the payment shall be made at the same time as the deposited item is collected.

Article 903 If the depositor fails to pay the storage fee or other expenses in accordance with the agreement, the depositary shall have a lien over the deposited item, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
Article 904 A warehousing contract is a contract whereby the depositary stores the goods delivered by the depositor and the depositor pays the warehousing fee.
Article 905 A warehousing contract shall be formed when the depositary and the depositor reach a consensus through their mutual expressions of intent.

Article 906 Where dangerous goods such as inflammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, or radioactive items or perishable goods are stored, the depositor shall state the nature of such goods and provide relevant information. Where the depositor violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the depositary may reject the goods or take corresponding measures to avoid the occurrence of loss, and the expenses incurred as a result thereof shall be borne by the depositor. Where a depositary stores dangerous goods such as inflammable, explosive, toxic, corrosive, or radioactive items, it shall have the corresponding storage conditions.

Article 907 The depositary shall inspect the goods delivered into storage in accordance with the agreement. If the depositary, during inspection, discovers that the goods delivered into storage do not conform to the agreement, it shall promptly notify the depositor. If, after inspection by the depositary, the type, quantity, or quality of the goods fails to conform to the agreement, the depositary shall bear compensation liability.
Article 908 Upon delivery of the goods by the depositor, the depositary shall issue documents such as a warehouse receipt or a storage receipt.

Article 909 The depositary shall sign or affix its seal on the warehouse receipt. The warehouse receipt shall include the following items: (1) the name or title and domicile of the depositor; (2) the type, quantity, quality, packaging, number of packages, and marks of the goods; (3) the standard for loss and damage of the goods; (4) the storage premises; (5) the term of storage; (6) the warehousing fee; (7) where the goods have been insured, the sum insured, the insurance period, and the name of the insurer; and (8) the issuer, place of issue, and date of issue.

Article 910 The warehouse receipt is a document for taking delivery of the goods. The depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt may transfer the right to take delivery of the goods by endorsing the warehouse receipt and obtaining the signature or seal of the depositary.
Article 911 The depositary shall, at the request of the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt, agree to allow such person to inspect the goods or take samples.

Article 912 If the depositary discovers that the goods delivered into storage have deteriorated or suffered other damage, it shall promptly notify the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt.

Article 913 If the depositary discovers that the goods delivered into storage have deteriorated or suffered other damage, thereby endangering the safety and proper storage of other goods, it shall urge the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt to make necessary dispositions. In an emergency, the depositary may make necessary dispositions; provided, however, that it shall promptly notify the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt of such situation thereafter.

Article 914 Where the parties have not agreed on the term of storage or the agreement is unclear, the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt may take delivery of the goods at any time, and the depositary may also demand at any time that the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt take delivery of the goods, provided that a necessary period of preparation shall be given.

Article 915 Upon expiry of the term of storage, the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt shall take delivery of the goods by presenting the warehouse receipt, storage receipt, or such other documents. If the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt takes delivery after the expiry of the term, an additional warehousing fee shall be charged; if delivery is taken before the expiry of the term, the warehousing fee shall not be reduced.

Article 916 Upon expiry of the term of storage, if the depositor or the holder of the warehouse receipt fails to take delivery of the goods, the depositary may urge such person to take delivery within a reasonable period; if delivery is not taken after the expiry of such period, the depositary may deposit the goods with a competent authority.

Article 917 If, during the term of storage, the goods are damaged or lost due to improper storage, the depositary shall bear compensation liability. If the goods deteriorate or are damaged due to the natural nature of the goods themselves, defective packaging not conforming to the agreement, or exceeding the effective storage period, the depositary shall not bear compensation liability.
Article 918 Matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be governed by the relevant provisions on contracts of deposit.
Article 919 A contract of mandate is a contract whereby the principal and the agent agree that the agent shall handle the affairs of the principal.
Article 920 The principal may specifically mandate the agent to handle one or several affairs, or may generally mandate the agent to handle all affairs.

Article 921 The principal shall advance the expenses for handling the entrusted affairs. For necessary expenses advanced by the agent in handling the entrusted affairs, the principal shall reimburse such expenses and pay interest thereon.

Article 922 The agent shall handle the entrusted affairs in accordance with the instructions of the principal. Where any modification of the principal's instructions is necessary, the consent of the principal must be obtained; if under urgent circumstances it is difficult to contact the principal, the agent shall properly handle the entrusted affairs, but shall promptly report such circumstances to the principal afterwards.

Article 923 The agent shall handle the entrusted affairs in person. With the consent of the principal, the agent may sub-entrust the affairs. Where the sub-entrustment is consented to or ratified, the principal may give direct instructions to the third party on the entrusted affairs, and the agent shall only be liable for the selection of the third party and for the instructions given to the third party. Where the sub-entrustment is not consented to or ratified, the agent shall be liable for the acts of the third party to whom the affairs are sub-entrusted; except that under urgent circumstances, the agent needs to sub-entrust the affairs to a third party in order to safeguard the interests of the principal.

Article 924 The agent shall, as requested by the principal, report on the handling of the entrusted affairs. Upon termination of the agency contract, the agent shall report the results of the entrusted affairs.

Article 925 Where an agent enters into a contract with a third party in its own name and within the scope of authority granted by the principal, and the third party knows at the time of entering into the contract of the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, such contract shall directly bind the principal and the third party; except where there is conclusive evidence to prove that the contract only binds the agent and the third party.

Article 926 Where an agent enters into a contract with a third party in its own name, and the third party is unaware of the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, if the agent fails to perform its obligations to the principal due to the fault of the third party, the agent shall disclose the third party to the principal, and the principal may then exercise the rights of the agent against the third party. However, this shall not apply if the third party would not have entered into the contract had it known of the identity of the principal at the time of entering into the contract. If the agent fails to perform its obligations to the third party due to the fault of the principal, the agent shall disclose the principal to the third party. The third party may then choose either the agent or the principal as the counterparty to assert its rights, but the third party may not change the chosen counterparty. Where the principal exercises the rights of the agent against the third party, the third party may raise against the principal the defenses it has against the agent. Where the third party chooses the principal as its counterparty, the principal may raise against the third party the defenses it has against the agent, as well as the defenses the agent has against the third party.
Article 927 Any property acquired by the agent in handling the entrusted affairs shall be transferred to the principal.

Article 928 Where the agent completes the entrusted affairs, the principal shall pay the remuneration to the agent as agreed. If the agency contract is dissolved or the entrusted affairs cannot be completed due to reasons not attributable to the agent, the principal shall pay the agent corresponding remuneration. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 929 For a remunerated agency contract, the principal may claim compensation for losses caused to the principal by the agent's fault. For a gratuitous agency contract, the principal may claim compensation for losses caused to the principal by the agent's intentional act or gross negligence. Where the agent causes losses to the principal by acting beyond its authority, the agent shall compensate for such losses.
Article 930 Where the agent, when handling the entrusted affairs, suffers losses due to reasons not attributable to itself, it may claim compensation for such losses from the principal.

Article 931 With the consent of the agent, the principal may entrust a third party other than the agent to handle the entrusted affairs. Where losses are thereby caused to the agent, the agent may claim compensation for such losses from the principal.
Article 932 Where two or more agents jointly handle the entrusted affairs, they shall bear joint and several liability to the principal.

Article 933 Either the principal or the agent may dissolve the agency contract at any time. Where losses are caused to the other party due to the dissolution, unless due to reasons not attributable to the dissolving party, the dissolving party of a gratuitous agency contract shall compensate for the direct losses caused by the improper timing of the dissolution, and the dissolving party of a remunerated agency contract shall compensate for the other party's direct losses and the benefits that could have been obtained after the performance of the contract.

Article 934 The agency contract shall terminate upon the death or termination of the principal, or upon the death, loss of civil capacity, or termination of the agent; except where the parties have otherwise agreed, or it is inappropriate to terminate based on the nature of the entrusted affairs.

Article 935 Where the termination of the agency contract due to the death of the principal or its being declared bankrupt or dissolved would harm the interests of the principal, the agent shall continue to handle the entrusted affairs until the heir, estate administrator or liquidator of the principal takes over the entrusted affairs.

Article 936 Where the agency contract terminates due to the death, loss of civil capacity, or being declared bankrupt or dissolved of the agent, the heir, estate administrator, legal representative or liquidator of the agent shall promptly notify the principal. Where the termination of the agency contract would harm the interests of the principal, the heir, estate administrator, legal representative or liquidator of the agent shall take necessary measures before the principal makes proper arrangements.

Article 937 A property service contract is a contract under which a property service provider provides property services, including the repair and maintenance of buildings and their ancillary facilities, environmental sanitation, and management and maintenance of relevant order, within the property service area to the owners, and the owners pay property fees. Property service providers include property service enterprises and other managers.

Article 938 The contents of a property service contract generally include clauses on service items, service quality, the standards and methods for collecting service fees, the use of maintenance funds, the management and use of service premises, the service term, and the handover of services. A service commitment publicly made by the property service provider that is beneficial to the owners shall be an integral part of the property service contract. A property service contract shall be in writing.

Article 939 The preliminary property service contract entered into by the construction entity and the property service provider in accordance with the law, and the property service contract entered into by the owners' committee and the property service provider legally selected and appointed by the owners' assembly, shall have legal binding force on the owners.

Article 940 Where, prior to the expiration of the service term agreed in the preliminary property service contract entered into by the construction entity and the property service provider in accordance with the law, the property service contract entered into by the owners' committee or the owners with a new property service provider becomes effective, the preliminary property service contract shall terminate.

Article 941 Where a property service provider delegates certain specialized service matters within the property service area to a professional service organization or another third party, it shall be liable to the owners for such specialized service matters. A property service provider shall not subcontract the entire property services it shall provide to a third party, nor shall it split the entire property services into parts and subcontract them separately to third parties.

Article 942 A property service provider shall, in accordance with the agreement and the nature of the property's use, properly repair, maintain, clean, landscape, and manage the common areas of the owners within the property service area, maintain basic order within the property service area, and take reasonable measures to protect the personal and property safety of the owners. Where any act violating laws and regulations on public security, environmental protection, fire control, or the like occurs within the property service area, the property service provider shall promptly take reasonable measures to stop such act, report it to the relevant administrative department, and assist in handling it.

Article 943 A property service provider shall periodically disclose to the owners, and report to the owners' assembly and the owners' committee, in a reasonable manner, the matters of service, responsible personnel, quality requirements, fee items, fee rates, performance status, as well as the use of maintenance funds and the operation and income of the common areas of the owners.

Article 944 An owner shall pay the property service fee to the property service provider in accordance with the agreement. Where the property service provider has provided services in accordance with the agreement and relevant provisions, the owner shall not refuse to pay the property service fee on the grounds of not receiving or not needing the relevant property services. Where an owner fails to pay the property service fee within the agreed time limit in violation of the agreement, the property service provider may demand payment within a reasonable period; if the owner still fails to pay after the reasonable period expires, the property service provider may initiate a lawsuit or apply for arbitration. A property service provider shall not resort to measures such as cutting off power, water, heat, or gas supply to coerce payment of the property service fee.

Article 945 Where an owner decorates or renovates the premises, he shall inform the property service provider in advance, comply with the reasonable precautions advised by the property service provider, and cooperate in any necessary on-site inspection. Where an owner transfers or leases the exclusive part of the property, establishes a right of habitation, or changes the use of the common area according to law, he shall promptly inform the property service provider of the relevant situation.

Article 946 Where the owners jointly decide to dismiss the property service provider in accordance with the statutory procedures, they may dissolve the property service contract. If they decide to dismiss, they shall notify the property service provider in writing sixty days in advance, unless the contract stipulates otherwise regarding the notice period. If the dissolution of the contract pursuant to the preceding paragraph causes losses to the property service provider, the owners shall compensate for the losses, unless the cause is not attributable to the owners.

Article 947 Before the expiration of the property service term, if the owners jointly decide to renew the engagement in accordance with the law, they shall renew the property service contract with the original property service provider before the expiration of the contract term. Before the expiration of the property service term, if the property service provider does not agree to renew the engagement, it shall notify the owners or the owners' committee in writing ninety days before the expiration of the contract term, unless the contract stipulates otherwise regarding the notice period.

Article 948 After the expiration of the property service term, if the owners have not made a decision according to law to renew the engagement or engage another property service provider, and the property service provider continues to provide property services, the original property service contract shall remain effective, but the service term shall be indefinite. A party may dissolve an indefinite property service contract at any time, but shall notify the other party in writing sixty days in advance.

Article 949 Upon termination of the property service contract, the original property service provider shall withdraw from the property service area within the agreed period or a reasonable period, return the property service premises, relevant facilities, and the relevant materials necessary for property services to the owners' committee, the owners who decide to self-manage, or the persons designated by them, cooperate with the new property service provider in the handover, and truthfully inform the status of the property's use and management. Where the original property service provider violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, it shall not request the owners to pay the property service fee after the termination of the property service contract; if it causes losses to the owners, it shall compensate for the losses.

Article 950 After the termination of the property service contract, before the new property service provider selected by the owners or the owners' assembly, or the owners who decide to self-manage, takes over, the original property service provider shall continue to handle property service matters and may request the owners to pay the property service fee for such period.
Article 951 A commission contract is a contract under which a commission agent engages in trading activities in its own name for a principal, and the principal pays remuneration.
Article 952 The expenses incurred by a commission agent in handling the entrusted affairs shall be borne by the commission agent, unless the parties agree otherwise.
Article 953 Where a commission agent is in possession of the entrusted property, it shall keep it in safe custody.

Article 954 If the entrusted property, when delivered to the commission agent, is defective or is perishable or subject to deterioration, the commission agent may dispose of it with the consent of the principal; if the commission agent cannot contact the principal in a timely manner, it may dispose of it in a reasonable manner.

Article 955 If a commission agent sells at a price lower than the price designated by the principal or buys at a price higher than the price designated by the principal, it shall obtain the consent of the principal; if, without the consent of the principal, the commission agent compensates for the difference, the transaction shall be binding on the principal. If a commission agent sells at a price higher than the price designated by the principal or buys at a price lower than the price designated by the principal, it may claim additional remuneration in accordance with the agreement; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and it cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of this Law, such benefit shall belong to the principal. If the principal gives specific instructions regarding the price, the commission agent shall not sell or buy in violation of such instructions.

Article 956 When a commission agent sells or buys commodities with a market price, unless the principal indicates a contrary intention, the commission agent may itself act as the buyer or seller. Where the commission agent falls under the circumstances specified in the preceding paragraph, it may still request the principal to pay remuneration.

Article 957 Where a commission agent purchases the entrusted property in accordance with the agreement, the principal shall accept it in a timely manner. If, after the commission agent demands acceptance, the principal refuses to accept it without just cause, the commission agent may, according to law, deposit the entrusted property. If the entrusted property cannot be sold or the principal withdraws the sale, and after the commission agent demands action, the principal fails to recover or dispose of the property, the commission agent may, according to law, deposit the entrusted property.

Article 958 Where a commission agent enters into a contract with a third party, the commission agent directly enjoys rights and assumes obligations under such contract. If the third party fails to perform its obligations, thereby causing damage to the principal, the commission agent shall bear compensation liability, unless the commission agent and the principal agree otherwise.

Article 959 Where a commission agent completes or partially completes the entrusted affairs, the principal shall pay corresponding remuneration to it. If the principal fails to pay the remuneration within the time limit, the commission agent has a lien over the entrusted property, unless the parties agree otherwise.
Article 960 Matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be governed by the relevant provisions on commission contracts, mutatis mutandis.

Article 961 A intermediary contract is a contract under which the intermediary reports to the client on opportunities for concluding a contract or provides intermediary services for the conclusion of a contract, and the client pays remuneration therefor.

Article 962 The intermediary shall report truthfully to the client on matters pertaining to the conclusion of the contract. Where the intermediary intentionally conceals material facts relating to the conclusion of the contract or provides false information, thereby harming the interests of the client, it may not claim remuneration and shall bear compensation liability.

Article 963 Where the intermediary facilitates the formation of the contract, the client shall pay remuneration as agreed. If the remuneration of the intermediary is not agreed upon or the agreement is unclear and cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, it shall be reasonably determined based on the services provided by the intermediary. Where the formation of the contract is facilitated by the intermediary providing intermediary services for the conclusion of the contract, the parties to that contract shall equally bear the intermediary's remuneration. Where the intermediary facilitates the formation of the contract, the expenses of the intermediary activities shall be borne by the intermediary.

Article 964 Where the intermediary does not facilitate the formation of the contract, it may not claim payment of remuneration; however, it may claim payment by the client of the necessary expenses incurred in carrying out the intermediary activities as agreed.

Article 965 Where, after accepting the services of the intermediary, the client uses the transaction opportunities or intermediary services provided by the intermediary to bypass the intermediary and directly conclude a contract, it shall pay remuneration to the intermediary.
Article 966 Matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be governed by applying mutatis mutandis the relevant provisions on the contract of mandate.
Article 967 A partnership contract is an agreement concluded by two or more partners for a common business purpose to share interests and bear risks.
Article 968 The partners shall perform their capital contribution obligations in accordance with the agreed method, amount, and time of payment.

Article 969 The partners' capital contributions, returns obtained lawfully from partnership affairs, and other property shall constitute partnership property. Before the termination of the partnership contract, no partner may claim a division of the partnership property.

Article 970 Decisions made by the partners on partnership affairs shall be subject to the unanimous consent of all partners, unless otherwise agreed in the partnership contract. Partnership affairs shall be jointly executed by all partners. In accordance with the provisions of the partnership contract or the decision of all partners, one or several partners may be appointed to execute the partnership affairs; the other partners shall no longer execute the partnership affairs, but shall have the right to supervise the execution thereof. Where partners execute the partnership affairs separately, the executing partner may raise objections to the affairs executed by other partners; after such objections are raised, the other partners shall suspend the execution of such affairs.
Article 971 No partner may claim remuneration for the execution of partnership affairs, unless otherwise agreed in the partnership contract.

Article 972 The distribution of profits and the sharing of losses of the partnership shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the partnership contract; if the partnership contract contains no such provisions or the provisions are unclear, the partners shall decide by consultation; if consultation fails, the partners shall distribute profits and share losses in proportion to their actually paid capital contributions; if the proportion of capital contributions cannot be determined, the partners shall distribute profits and share losses equally.

Article 973 The partners shall bear joint and several liability for partnership debts. A partner who has discharged partnership debts in excess of its own share shall have the right to recover from the other partners.

Article 974 Unless otherwise agreed in the partnership contract, a partner transferring all or part of its property share to a person other than the partners shall require the unanimous consent of the other partners.

Article 975 A creditor of a partner may not exercise by subrogation the rights enjoyed by the partner under this Chapter and the partnership contract, except for the partner's right to claim distribution of interests.

Article 976 Where the partners have not agreed on the term of the partnership or the agreement is unclear and cannot be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 510 of this Law, the partnership shall be deemed to be a partnership for an indefinite term. Upon expiry of the partnership term, if the partners continue to execute partnership affairs and the other partners raise no objection, the original partnership contract shall continue to be valid, but the partnership term shall be indefinite. A partner may terminate the partnership contract for an indefinite term at any time, provided that it gives notice to the other partners within a reasonable period in advance.

Article 977 Upon the death, loss of civil capacity, or termination of a partner, the partnership contract shall terminate; except where otherwise agreed in the partnership contract or where termination is not appropriate based on the nature of the partnership affairs.

Article 978 After the termination of the partnership contract, any partnership property remaining after payment of the expenses incurred as a result of the termination and satisfaction of the partnership debts shall be distributed in accordance with the provisions of Article 972 of this Law. Subdivision III Quasi-Contracts

Article 979 A manager who, without a legal or contractual obligation, manages the affairs of another person with the intention of preventing losses to the interests of that person may request the beneficiary to reimburse the necessary expenses incurred in managing the affairs; if the manager suffers losses as a result of managing the affairs, it may request the beneficiary to provide appropriate compensation. If the management of affairs is not in conformity with the true intention of the beneficiary, the manager shall not enjoy the rights provided for in the preceding paragraph; except where the true intention of the beneficiary violates the law or public order and good customs.

Article 980 Where the management of affairs by the manager does not fall within the circumstances specified in the preceding article, but the beneficiary enjoys the benefits of the management, the beneficiary shall assume the obligations provided for in paragraph 1 of the preceding article to the manager to the extent of the benefits it obtains.

Article 981 A manager who manages the affairs of another person shall adopt methods beneficial to the principal. If interrupting the management is detrimental to the principal, the manager shall not interrupt it without justifiable reasons.

Article 982 If a manager who manages the affairs of another person may notify the principal, he shall promptly notify the principal. If the matter managed does not require urgent handling, he shall await the principal's instructions.

Article 983 After the management concludes, the manager shall report to the principal on the situation of the managed affairs. Any property obtained by the manager from managing the affairs shall be promptly transferred to the principal.

Article 984 If the principal subsequently ratifies the management of affairs by the manager, the relevant provisions on the entrustment contract shall apply from the commencement of the management, unless the manager expresses a contrary intention.

Article 985 Where a benefit recipient obtains unjust benefits without legal basis, the person who suffers loss may request the benefit recipient to return the benefits obtained, except under any of the following circumstances: (1) Performance made to fulfill a moral obligation; (2) Satisfaction of a debt before it becomes due; (3) Satisfaction of a debt while knowing that there is no obligation to perform.

Article 986 Where a benefit recipient neither knows nor ought to have known that the benefits obtained have no legal basis, and the benefits obtained no longer exist, he shall not bear the obligation to return such benefits.

Article 987 Where a benefit recipient knows or ought to have known that the benefits obtained have no legal basis, the person who suffers loss may request the benefit recipient to return the benefits obtained and to compensate for the losses according to law.

Article 988 Where a benefit recipient has transferred the benefits obtained to a third party without consideration, the person who suffers loss may request the third party to bear the obligation of return to the corresponding extent.
Article 989 This Book regulates the civil relations arising from the enjoyment and protection of personality rights.

Article 990 Personality rights are the rights enjoyed by civil subjects, including the rights to life, body, health, name, entity name, likeness, reputation, honor, privacy, and other rights. In addition to the personality rights provided for in the preceding paragraph, natural persons enjoy other personality interests arising from personal freedom and human dignity.
Article 991 The personality rights of civil subjects shall be protected by law, and no organization or individual may infringe upon them.
Article 992 Personality rights may not be waived, transferred, or inherited.
Article 993 A civil subject may license others to use his name, entity name, likeness, or the like, except where such licensing is prohibited by law or by the nature of the right.

Article 994 Where the name, likeness, reputation, honor, privacy, or remains of a deceased person are infringed upon, his spouse, children, and parents shall have the right to request, according to law, that the infringer bear civil liability. If the deceased person has no spouse or children, and his parents are deceased, his other close relatives shall have the right to request, according to law, that the infringer bear civil liability.

Article 995 Where a personality right is infringed upon, the victim shall have the right to request, in accordance with this Law and other laws, that the infringer bear civil liability. The victim's right to request cessation of the infringement, removal of the obstruction, elimination of the danger, elimination of adverse effects, restoration of reputation, or making an apology shall not be subject to the statute of limitations.

Article 996 Where a party's breach of contract infringes upon the other party's personality right and causes serious mental distress, and the injured party elects to request the breaching party to bear liability for breach of contract, such election shall not preclude the injured party from claiming compensation for moral damages.

Article 997 Where a civil subject has evidence proving that an infringer is committing or about to commit an unlawful act that infringes upon his personality right, and failure to promptly stop it shall cause irreparable damage to his lawful rights and interests, he shall have the right to apply to the People's Court according to law for measures ordering the infringer to cease the relevant acts.

Article 998 In determining the civil liability of an infringer for infringement upon personality rights other than the rights to life, body, and health, factors such as the occupations of the infringer and the victim, the scope of impact, the degree of fault, and the purpose, method, and consequences of the act shall be considered.

Article 999 Where acts such as news reporting or supervision by public opinion are carried out for the public interest, the name, entity name, likeness, personal information, etc. of a civil subject may be used reasonably. If the use is unreasonable and infringes upon the personality rights of the civil subject, civil liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 1000 Where an infringer bears civil liability such as eliminating adverse effects, restoring reputation, or making an apology for infringing upon personality rights, such liability shall be commensurate with the specific manner of the act and the scope of the adverse impact caused. If the infringer refuses to bear the civil liability provided for in the preceding paragraph, the People's Court may enforce it by means such as publishing an announcement on media like newspapers or the internet, or publishing the effective judgment document, and the costs incurred shall be borne by the infringer.

Article 1001 The protection of the right to status of a natural person arising from marital and family relations and the like shall be governed by the relevant provisions of Book One, Book Five and other laws of this Code; in the absence of such provisions, the relevant provisions on the protection of personality rights in this Book may be applied mutatis mutandis based on its nature.

Article 1002 A natural person shall enjoy the right to life. The life safety and dignity of a natural person shall be protected by law. No organization or individual shall infringe upon the right to life of another person.

Article 1003 A natural person shall enjoy the right to physical integrity. The physical integrity and freedom of movement of a natural person shall be protected by law. No organization or individual shall infringe upon the right to physical integrity of another person.

Article 1004 A natural person shall enjoy the right to health. The physical and mental health of a natural person shall be protected by law. No organization or individual shall infringe upon the right to health of another person.

Article 1005 Where a natural person's right to life, right to physical integrity or right to health is infringed upon, or such person is in other perilous circumstances, an organization or individual that has a legal obligation to provide rescue shall promptly render such rescue.

Article 1006 A person with full capacity for civil conduct shall have the right to independently decide to donate his or her human cells, human tissues, human organs, or remains free of charge according to law. No organization or individual may coerce, deceive, or induce such person into making such donation. Where a person with full capacity for civil conduct consents to donation in accordance with the preceding paragraph, such consent shall be made in writing, or a will may be made. Where a natural person did not express disagreement with donation during his or her lifetime, after the death of such natural person, his or her spouse, adult children, and parents may jointly decide on the donation, and the decision to donate shall be made in writing.
Article 1007 The sale of human cells, human tissues, human organs, or remains in any form shall be prohibited. Any act of sale in violation of the preceding paragraph shall be void.

Article 1008 Where a clinical trial is required for the development of new drugs, medical devices, or new methods for prevention and treatment, it shall be approved by the relevant competent authority and reviewed and approved by an ethics committee according to law. The subject or the subject's guardian shall be informed of detailed information such as the purpose, use, and potential risks of the trial, and their written consent shall be obtained. No fees shall be charged to the subject for conducting a clinical trial.

Article 1009 Medical and scientific research activities involving human genes, human embryos, and the like shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions, and shall not harm human health, violate ethical morality, or damage the public interest.

Article 1010 Where a person commits sexual harassment against another person by means of words, text, images, physical acts, or the like against such other person's will, the victim shall have the right to request the actor to bear civil liability according to law. State organs, enterprises, schools, and other entities shall take reasonable measures such as prevention, acceptance of complaints, investigation, and handling to prevent and stop sexual harassment committed through the abuse of authority, subordinate relationships, or the like.

Article 1011 Where a person deprives or restricts another person's freedom of action by means of unlawful detention or the like, or unlawfully searches another person's body, the victim shall have the right to request the actor to bear civil liability according to law.

Article 1012 A natural person shall enjoy the right to name, and shall have the right to decide, use, change, or permit another person to use his or her name according to law, provided that such acts shall not contravene public order and good customs.

Article 1013 A legal person or an unincorporated organization shall enjoy the right to name, and shall have the right to decide, use, change, transfer, or permit another person to use its name according to law.
Article 1014 No organization or individual may infringe upon another person's right to name by means of interference, misappropriation, impersonation, or the like.

Article 1015 A natural person shall bear the surname of his or her father or mother, but may, under any of the following circumstances, choose a surname other than the father's or mother's surname: (1) choosing the surname of another direct lineal elder relative by blood; (2) choosing the surname of the person who has raised the natural person due to being raised by a person other than a legally designated supporter; or (3) having other justifiable reasons that do not contravene public order and good customs. The surname of a natural person of an ethnic minority may follow the cultural traditions and customs of that ethnic group.

Article 1016 Where a natural person decides on or changes his or her name, or a legal person or an unincorporated organization decides on, changes, or transfers its name, it shall go through the registration formalities with the relevant authority according to law, except as otherwise provided by law. Where a civil subject changes his, her, or its name, the juridical acts performed before such change shall be legally binding on such subject.

Article 1017 Where a pen name, stage name, online pseudonym, translated name, business name, abbreviation of a name or designation, or the like has a certain degree of social recognition and its use by another person is sufficient to cause public confusion, the relevant provisions on the protection of the right to name shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 1018 A natural person shall enjoy the right to portrait, and shall have the right to make, use, disclose, or permit another person to use his or her portrait according to law. A portrait refers to the recognizable external image of a specific natural person reflected on a certain medium through images, sculptures, paintings, or other means.

Article 1019 No organization or individual may infringe upon another person's right to portrait by means of defacing, tarnishing, or forging by using information technology, or the like. Without the consent of the right holder of the portrait, the portrait of the right holder shall not be made, used, or disclosed, except as otherwise provided by law. Without the consent of the right holder of the portrait, the right holder of a portrait work shall not use or disclose the portrait of the right holder of the portrait by means of publication, reproduction, distribution, rental, exhibition, or the like.

Article 1020 The following acts may be reasonably performed without the consent of the right holder of the portrait: (1) using the portrait of the right holder that has already been disclosed within the necessary scope for personal study, artistic appreciation, classroom teaching, or scientific research; (2) inevitably making, using, or disclosing the portrait of the right holder for the purpose of carrying out news reporting; (3) making, using, or disclosing the portrait of the right holder within the necessary scope by a state organ for the purpose of performing its duties according to law; (4) inevitably making, using, or disclosing the portrait of the right holder for the purpose of displaying a specific public environment; or (5) other acts of making, using, or disclosing the portrait of the right holder for the purpose of maintaining the public interest or the lawful rights and interests of the right holder of the portrait.

Article 1021 Where a dispute arises between the parties regarding the understanding of the terms concerning the use of a portrait in a portrait licensing contract, an interpretation favorable to the right holder of the portrait shall be adopted.

Article 1022 Where the parties have not agreed on or have not clearly agreed on the term of portrait licensing, any party may dissolve the portrait licensing contract at any time, provided that the other party shall be notified within a reasonable period in advance. Where the parties have clearly agreed on the term of portrait licensing, the right holder of the portrait may, for justified reasons, dissolve the portrait licensing contract, provided that the other party shall be notified within a reasonable period in advance. If the dissolution of the contract causes losses to the other party, compensation shall be made, unless the cause is not attributable to the right holder of the portrait.

Article 1023 The licensing of the use of names and other such matters shall be governed by mutatis mutandis the relevant provisions on the licensing of the use of portraits. The protection of a natural person's voice shall be governed by mutatis mutandis the relevant provisions on the protection of the right to a portrait.

Article 1024 Civil subjects shall enjoy the right to reputation. No organization or individual may infringe upon the right to reputation of others by means of insult, defamation, or the like. Reputation refers to the social evaluation of a civil subject's moral character, prestige, talent, credit, and the like.

Article 1025 Where a person engages in news reporting, supervision by public opinion, or similar acts for the public interest, which adversely affects another person's reputation, the person shall not bear civil liability unless any of the following circumstances exists: (1) the fabrication or distortion of facts; (2) failure to fulfill the reasonable duty of verification regarding seriously inaccurate content provided by others; or (3) the use of insulting language or other means to disparage another person's reputation.

Article 1026 When determining whether a person has fulfilled the reasonable duty of verification as provided in subparagraph (2) of the preceding article, the following factors shall be taken into consideration: (1) the credibility of the source of the content; (2) whether necessary investigation has been conducted into content that is manifestly likely to give rise to controversy; (3) the timeliness of the content; (4) the relevance of the content to public order and good customs; (5) the likelihood of damage to the victim's reputation; and (6) the capability and cost of verification.

Article 1027 Where a literary or artistic work published by a person describes a real person, real event, or a specific person, contains insulting or defamatory content, and infringes upon another person's right to reputation, the victim shall have the right to request the person to bear civil liability in accordance with law. Where a literary or artistic work published by a person does not describe a specific person, and only the plot therein is similar to the circumstances of that specific person, the person shall not bear civil liability.

Article 1028 Where a civil subject has evidence proving that content reported by media such as newspapers or the internet is inaccurate and infringes upon his or her right to reputation, the civil subject shall have the right to request such media to promptly take necessary measures, such as correction or deletion.

Article 1029 A civil subject may, in accordance with law, inquire about his or her credit evaluation; if the civil subject finds that the credit evaluation is improper, the civil subject shall have the right to raise an objection and request the adoption of necessary measures such as correction or deletion. The credit evaluator shall promptly verify such matters; if the verification confirms the issue, the credit evaluator shall promptly adopt necessary measures.

Article 1030 The relationship between a civil subject and a credit information processor such as a credit investigation agency shall be governed by the provisions of this Part on the protection of personal information and the relevant provisions of other laws and administrative regulations.

Article 1031 Civil subjects shall enjoy the right to honor. No organization or individual may unlawfully deprive another person of his or her honorary title, or slander or disparage another person's honor. Where an honorary title obtained by a civil subject should have been recorded but has not been recorded, the civil subject may request its recording; where the honorary title obtained by a civil subject is recorded incorrectly, the civil subject may request its correction.

Article 1032 Natural persons shall enjoy the right to privacy. No organization or individual may infringe upon another person's right to privacy by means of prying, intrusion, disclosure, publication, or the like. Privacy refers to a natural person's peace of private life and the private space, private activities, and private information that the natural person does not wish to be known by others.

Article 1033 Unless otherwise provided by law or expressly consented to by the right holder, no organization or individual may commit any of the following acts: (1) intruding upon another person's peace of private life by means of telephone, text messages, instant messaging tools, emails, leaflets, or the like; (2) entering, photographing, or peeping into another person's private spaces such as a residence or hotel room; (3) photographing, peeping at, eavesdropping on, or publishing another person's private activities; (4) photographing or peeping at the intimate body parts of another person; (5) processing another person's private information; or (6) infringing upon another person's right to privacy by other means.

Article 1034 A natural person's personal information shall be protected by law. Personal information refers to all kinds of information recorded electronically or by other means that can identify a specific natural person either alone or in combination with other information, including a natural person's name, date of birth, identity document number, biometric information, address, telephone number, email address, health information, whereabouts information, and the like. For private information among personal information, the provisions on the right to privacy shall apply; where there are no such provisions, the provisions on the protection of personal information shall apply.

Article 1035 When processing personal information, the principles of legality, legitimacy, and necessity shall be followed, and excessive processing shall not be allowed, and the following conditions shall be met: (1) obtaining the consent of the natural person or his or her guardian, unless otherwise provided by law or administrative regulations; (2) disclosing the rules for processing the information; (3) expressly stating the purpose, method, and scope of processing the information; and (4) not violating the provisions of laws or administrative regulations or the agreement of the parties. Processing of personal information includes the collection, storage, use, processing, transmission, provision, publication, and the like of personal information.

Article 1036 Where personal information is processed under any of the following circumstances, the person shall not bear civil liability: (1) the act is reasonably carried out within the scope of consent of the natural person or his or her guardian; (2) the act reasonably processes information that has been voluntarily made public by the natural person or has otherwise been lawfully made public, unless the natural person expressly refuses or the processing of such information infringes upon his or her material interests; or (3) the act is reasonably carried out to safeguard the public interest or the lawful rights and interests of the natural person.

Article 1037 A natural person may, in accordance with law, access or copy his or her personal information from an information processor; if the natural person finds errors in the information, the natural person shall have the right to raise an objection and request the timely adoption of necessary measures such as correction. If a natural person finds that an information processor processes his or her personal information in violation of the provisions of laws or administrative regulations or the agreement of the parties, the natural person shall have the right to request the information processor to promptly delete it.

Article 1038 An information processor shall not disclose or tamper with the personal information it collects or stores; without the consent of the natural person, it shall not illegally provide the natural person's personal information to others, unless the information, after processing, cannot identify a specific individual and cannot be restored. An information processor shall adopt technical measures and other necessary measures to ensure the security of the personal information it collects and stores, and prevent such information from being disclosed, tampered with, or lost; where a disclosure, tampering, or loss of personal information has occurred or is likely to occur, the information processor shall promptly adopt remedial measures, inform the natural person in accordance with the provisions, and report to the relevant competent authority.

Article 1039 State organs, statutory institutions with administrative functions, and their staff shall keep confidential the privacy and personal information of natural persons that they become aware of in the course of performing their duties, and shall not disclose or illegally provide such information to others.
Article 1040 This Part regulates civil relations arising from marriage and family.

Article 1041 Marriage and family shall be protected by the State. A marriage system based on freedom of marriage, monogamy, and equality between men and women shall be implemented. The legitimate rights and interests of women, minors, the elderly, and persons with disabilities shall be protected.

Article 1042 Arranged marriage, mercenary marriage, and any other acts interfering with the freedom of marriage shall be prohibited. The exaction of money or gifts in connection with marriage shall be prohibited. Bigamy shall be prohibited. No person who has a spouse may cohabit with another person. Domestic violence shall be prohibited. Abuse of or desertion of family members shall be prohibited.

Article 1043 Families shall establish good family traditions, promote family virtues, and attach importance to the building of a civilized family. Spouses shall be faithful to, respect, and care for each other. Family members shall respect the aged and love the young, help each other, and maintain marriage and family relations that are equal, harmonious, and civilized.

Article 1044 Adoption shall follow the principle most beneficial to the adopted person, and the legitimate rights and interests of the adopted person and the adopter shall be guaranteed. The sale of minors under the guise of adoption shall be prohibited.

Article 1045 Relatives include spouses, blood relatives, and relatives by marriage. Spouses, parents, children, siblings, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren are close relatives. Spouses, parents, children, and other close relatives living together are family members.
Article 1046 Marriage shall be based on the complete willingness of both a man and a woman. No party may compel the other party, and no organization or individual may interfere.
Article 1047 For marriage, the man shall reach the age of twenty-two, and the woman shall reach the age of twenty.
Article 1048 No marriage may be contracted between lineal blood relatives or collateral blood relatives within three generations.

Article 1049 Both a man and a woman requesting marriage shall appear in person before a marriage registration authority to apply for marriage registration. If the requirements set out in this Law are met, the marriage shall be registered and a marriage certificate shall be issued. Once the marriage is registered, the marital relationship is established. Where the marriage has not been registered, the parties shall go through the registration procedures subsequently.

Article 1050 After marriage registration, in accordance with the agreement between both a man and a woman, the woman may become a member of the man's family, and the man may become a member of the woman's family.

Article 1051 A marriage shall be void under any of the following circumstances: (1) bigamy; (2) having a prohibited family relationship between the parties; (3) failing to meet the legal age for marriage.

Article 1052 Where a marriage is concluded by coercion, the coerced party may petition the People's Court for revocation of the marriage. A petition for revocation of marriage shall be filed within one year from the date on which the coercive act ceases. Where a party whose personal freedom is illegally restricted petitions for revocation of marriage, the petition shall be filed within one year from the date on which the party's personal freedom is restored.

Article 1053 Where one party suffers from a serious disease, it shall truthfully inform the other party before marriage registration. If it fails to truthfully inform, the other party may petition the People's Court for revocation of the marriage. A petition for revocation of marriage shall be filed within one year from the date on which the party knows or should have known the cause for revocation.

Article 1054 A void or revoked marriage has no legal effect from its inception, and the parties shall not have the rights or obligations of husband and wife. Property acquired during cohabitation shall be disposed of by agreement between the parties. If no agreement is reached, the People's Court shall render a judgment based on the principle of protecting the innocent party. In the case of a void marriage due to bigamy, the disposal of property shall not infringe upon the property rights and interests of the party to the lawful marriage. The provisions of this Law on the relationship between parents and children shall apply to any children born of the parties. Where a marriage is void or revoked, the innocent party has the right to claim damages.
Article 1055 The status of husband and wife shall be equal in marriage and family.
Article 1056 Both the husband and the wife have the right to use their own respective surnames.
Article 1057 Both the husband and the wife have the freedom to participate in production, work, study, and social activities. Neither party may restrict or interfere with the other.
Article 1058 Both the husband and the wife enjoy equal rights to raise, educate, and protect minor children, and shall jointly bear the obligations to raise, educate, and protect minor children.

Article 1059 The husband and wife have the duty to support each other. Where one party in need of support fails to receive support from the other party, it has the right to demand the other party to pay support.

Article 1060 A civil juristic act carried out by one spouse for the needs of daily family life shall have effect on both spouses, except where the spouse and the counterparty have otherwise agreed. Any restriction agreed between the spouses on the scope of civil juristic acts that one spouse may carry out shall not be set up against a bona fide counterparty.
Article 1061 Spouses shall have the right to inherit each other's estate.

Article 1062 The following property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship shall be the common property of the spouses and shall be jointly owned by them: (1) wages, bonuses, and labor remuneration; (2) proceeds from production, business operations, and investments; (3) proceeds from intellectual property rights; (4) property inherited or donated, except as provided in Item 3 of Article 1063 of this Code; and (5) other property that shall be jointly owned. Spouses shall have equal rights to manage the common property.

Article 1063 The following property shall be the separate property of one spouse: (1) pre-marital property of one spouse; (2) compensation or damages received by one spouse for personal injury; (3) property designated in a will or gift contract to be owned solely by one spouse; (4) articles for daily use exclusively for one spouse; and (5) other property that shall belong to one spouse.

Article 1064 Debts incurred through a joint expression of intent, such as joint signature by both spouses or subsequent ratification by one spouse, and debts incurred by one spouse in his or her own name during the existence of the marital relationship for the needs of daily family life, shall be community debts of the spouses. Debts incurred by one spouse in his or her own name during the existence of the marital relationship beyond the needs of daily family life shall not be community debts of the spouses; unless the creditor can prove that such debts were used for the spouses' community life, community production or business operations, or were based on the joint expression of intent of both spouses.

Article 1065 A man and a woman may agree that the property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship and pre-marital property shall be owned separately, jointly, or partially separately and partially jointly. Such an agreement shall be in writing. Where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the provisions of Articles 1062 and 1063 of this Code shall apply. An agreement between the spouses concerning property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship and pre-marital property shall be legally binding on both parties. Where the spouses agree that property acquired during the existence of the marital relationship shall be owned separately, and one spouse incurs a debt to a third party, if the third party is aware of such agreement, the debt shall be satisfied from the separate property of that spouse.

Article 1066 During the existence of the marital relationship, under any of the following circumstances, one spouse may petition the People's Court for the partition of the common property: (1) One spouse commits acts that seriously impair the interests of the common property, such as concealing, transferring, selling, damaging, wasting the common property, or fabricating community debts; or (2) A person to whom one spouse has a statutory duty of support suffers from a serious illness and requires medical treatment, and the other spouse refuses to pay the relevant medical expenses.

Article 1067 Where parents fail to perform their duty of support, minor children or adult children who are unable to live independently shall have the right to claim child support from their parents. Where adult children fail to perform their duty of maintenance, parents who lack the capacity to work or are experiencing financial hardship shall have the right to claim maintenance from their adult children.
Article 1068 Parents shall have the right and duty to educate and protect their minor children. Where minor children cause damage to others, the parents shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 1069 Children shall respect their parents' marital rights and shall not interfere with their parents' divorce, remarriage, or post-marital life. The duty of children to maintain their parents shall not terminate due to any change in the parents' marital relationship.
Article 1070 Parents and children shall have the right to inherit each other's estate.

Article 1071 Children born out of wedlock shall enjoy the same rights as children born in wedlock, and no organization or individual may harm or discriminate against them. The biological father or mother who does not directly raise a child born out of wedlock shall bear the child support for the minor child or the adult child who is unable to live independently.

Article 1072 Stepparents and stepchildren shall not abuse or discriminate against each other. The rights and obligations between a stepfather or stepmother and stepchildren raised and educated by him or her shall be governed by the provisions of this Code concerning the relationship between parents and children.

Article 1073 Where there is a dispute over a parent-child relationship and there is a legitimate reason, the father or mother may institute an action in the People's Court to confirm or deny the parent-child relationship. Where there is a dispute over a parent-child relationship and there is a legitimate reason, an adult child may institute an action in the People's Court to confirm the parent-child relationship.

Article 1074 Grandparents and maternal grandparents who have the ability to bear the burden shall have the duty to support their minor grandchildren or maternal grandchildren whose parents have died or are unable to support them. Grandchildren and maternal grandchildren who have the ability to bear the burden shall have the duty to maintain their grandparents or maternal grandparents whose children have died or are unable to maintain them.

Article 1075 Elder brothers and sisters who have the ability to bear the burden shall have the duty to support their minor younger brothers and sisters whose parents have died or are unable to support them. Younger brothers and sisters who have been raised by their elder brothers or sisters and have the ability to bear the burden shall have the duty to support their elder brothers or sisters who lack the capacity to work and have no source of livelihood.

Article 1076 Where both spouses voluntarily divorce, they shall conclude a written divorce agreement and personally apply to the marriage registration authority for divorce registration. The divorce agreement shall state the expression of intent of both parties to voluntarily divorce and the mutually agreed opinions on matters such as the custody of children, property, and debt settlement.

Article 1077 Within 30 days from the date on which the marriage registration authority receives the application for divorce registration, if either party is unwilling to divorce, that party may withdraw the application for divorce registration with the marriage registration authority. Within 30 days after the expiration of the period specified in the preceding paragraph, both parties shall personally appear before the marriage registration authority to apply for the issuance of a divorce certificate; if no application is made, the application for divorce registration shall be deemed to have been withdrawn.

Article 1078 Where the marriage registration authority ascertains that both parties are indeed voluntarily divorcing and have reached a consensus on matters such as the custody of children, property, and debt settlement, it shall register the divorce and issue a divorce certificate.

Article 1079 Where one spouse demands a divorce, the relevant organization may conduct mediation, or the spouse may directly file a divorce action in the People's Court. When adjudicating a divorce case, the People's Court shall conduct mediation; if the mutual affection is indeed broken and mediation fails, the divorce shall be granted. A divorce shall be granted if mediation fails under any of the following circumstances: (1) bigamy or cohabitation with another person; (2) domestic violence or maltreatment, abandonment of family members; (3) repeated engagement in vices such as gambling or drug addiction despite repeated admonitions; (4) separation for at least two years due to incompatibility in affection; (5) other circumstances leading to the breakdown of mutual affection. Where one spouse has been declared missing, and the other spouse files a divorce action, the divorce shall be granted. After a judgment by the People's Court refusing a divorce, if the parties have been separated for another full year, and one party again files a divorce action, the divorce shall be granted.
Article 1080 The marital relationship shall be dissolved upon the completion of divorce registration or upon the effectiveness of a divorce judgment or mediation statement.
Article 1081 Where the spouse of a serviceperson on active duty requests a divorce, the consent of the serviceperson shall be obtained, except where the serviceperson has committed a major fault.

Article 1082 The husband may not initiate divorce proceedings while his wife is pregnant, within one year after childbirth, or within six months after the termination of pregnancy; however, this restriction does not apply where the wife initiates the divorce proceedings or where the People's Court deems it necessary to accept the husband's divorce request.
Article 1083 After divorce, if both the man and the woman voluntarily wish to restore the marital relationship, they shall undergo anew marriage registration at the marriage registration authority.

Article 1084 The relationship between parents and children shall not be terminated by the divorce of the parents. After divorce, regardless of whether the child is directly raised by the father or the mother, the child remains the child of both parents. After divorce, parents shall still have the rights and obligations to raise, educate, and protect their children. After divorce, a child under the age of two shall be raised directly by the mother as a principle. For a child who has reached the age of two, if the parents fail to reach an agreement on custody, the People's Court shall render a judgment in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the minor child based on the specific circumstances of both parties. If the child has reached the age of eight, the child's true wishes shall be respected.

Article 1085 After divorce, where a child is directly raised by one party, the other party shall bear part or all of the child support. The amount and duration of such child support shall be agreed upon by both parties; where an agreement cannot be reached, the People's Court shall render a judgment. The agreement or judgment as provided in the preceding paragraph shall not preclude the child from making reasonable requests to either parent for an amount exceeding the originally agreed or adjudicated sum when necessary.

Article 1086 After divorce, the parent who does not directly raise the child shall have the right to visit the child, and the other party shall have the obligation to provide assistance. The manner and time for exercising the visitation right shall be agreed upon by the parties; where an agreement cannot be reached, the People's Court shall render a judgment. If the visitation by the father or mother is detrimental to the physical or mental health of the child, the People's Court shall suspend the visitation in accordance with law; after the grounds for suspension cease to exist, visitation shall be resumed.

Article 1087 Upon divorce, the common property of the husband and wife shall be disposed by agreement between the parties; where an agreement cannot be reached, the People's Court shall render a judgment based on the specific circumstances of the property and in accordance with the principle of protecting the interests of the child, wife, and the non-fault party. The rights and interests enjoyed by the husband or wife in the operation of household land contracts, among others, shall be protected in accordance with law.

Article 1088 Where one spouse has undertaken more obligations, such as raising children, caring for the elderly, or assisting the other spouse in work, that spouse shall have the right to request compensation from the other spouse upon divorce, and the other spouse shall make such compensation. The specific method shall be agreed upon by both parties; where an agreement cannot be reached, the People's Court shall render a judgment.

Article 1089 Upon divorce, the joint debts of the husband and wife shall be repaid jointly.
